title: ser vs estar

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to do or be something is a wish, and when the wanting is in the past, the verb after que goes in the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que fueras feliz.
examples.en: I wanted you to be happy.
examples.note: Past wish + different subjects (yo / tú) means que + imperfect subjunctive. Never 'quería que eres' or 'quería que seas'.

examples.es: Quería que estuvieras tranquila durante la boda.
examples.en: I wanted you to be calm during the wedding.
examples.note: Estar is irregular here: estuvieras comes from estuvieron, never 'estaras'. Unlike the present estés, it has no written accent.

examples.es: Mi madre quería que yo estuviera listo a las ocho.
examples.en: My mother wanted me to be ready at eight.
examples.note: Listo with estar means ready. 'Fuera listo' would mean she wanted me to be clever.

contrast.es: Yo quería estar listo a las ocho.
contrast.en: I wanted to be ready at eight.
contrast.note: Same subject means infinitive. A different subject means que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting or denying something in the past takes away the claim of fact, so the verb after que goes in the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que fuera caro.
examples.en: I didn't think it was expensive.
examples.note: No creía que = past doubt, so fuera, not era.

examples.es: No creía que Marta estuviera en casa ese día.
examples.en: I didn't think Marta was at home that day.
examples.note: Location uses estar, and the past doubt pushes it into estuviera.

examples.es: No creía que el profesor fuera aburrido.
examples.en: I didn't think the teacher was boring.
examples.note: With ser, aburrido describes personality. With estar it would mean bored at that moment.

contrast.es: Creía que el profesor era aburrido.
contrast.en: I thought the teacher was boring.
contrast.note: Affirmative creía que takes the indicative (era). No creía que takes the imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive describes a hypothetical or unlikely situation, and the result is usually in the conditional.

examples.es: Si estuvieras aquí, sería más fácil.
examples.en: If you were here, it would be easier.
examples.note: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional (sería). Never 'si estarías'.

examples.es: Si fuese mayor, querría ser piloto.
examples.en: If I were older, I'd want to be a pilot.
examples.note: Fuese is the -se form of fuera. Both are correct, and both come from fueron.

examples.es: Si estuviéramos en Madrid, te enseñaría el barrio.
examples.en: If we were in Madrid, I'd show you the neighbourhood.
examples.note: Nosotros forms take an accent before -ramos: estuviéramos.

contrast.es: Cuando estamos en Madrid, te enseño el barrio.
contrast.en: Whenever we're in Madrid, I show you the neighbourhood.
contrast.note: A real habit uses the indicative. An unreal situation uses si + imperfect subjunctive.

tricky: Fuera is the imperfect subjunctive of both ser and ir, and estuviera is estar, so 'quería que fueras feliz' (be a happy person, happy in life) and 'quería que estuvieras feliz' (be happy right now, in a particular state) are both correct but mean different things. The accent only appears in nosotros (fuéramos, estuviéramos). The -se forms (fuese, estuviese) are equally correct.

title: fue vs era

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive is a wish about the present that is unlikely or contrary to fact: 'I wish it were'.

examples.es: Ojalá fuera una noche tranquila.
examples.en: I wish it were a quiet night.
examples.note: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive suggests it probably isn't. Ojalá sea would be an open hope.

examples.es: Ojalá el concierto fuese tan bueno como dicen.
examples.en: I wish the concert were as good as they say.
examples.note: The -se form fuese is just as correct as fuera. You doubt it will be that good.

examples.es: Ojalá la entrevista fuera corta, pero dudo que lo sea.
examples.en: I wish the interview were short, but I doubt it will be.
examples.note: You are wishing for something you think is unlikely.

contrast.es: La entrevista fue corta.
contrast.en: The interview was short.
contrast.note: Fue states a completed fact. After ojalá, fuera expresses a wish that probably isn't real.

triggers.explanation: Denying that something was true means you aren't asserting it as fact, so the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No era cierto que fuera caro.
examples.en: It wasn't true that it was expensive.
examples.note: Denial = subjunctive. Era appears in the main clause, fuera in the subordinate one.

examples.es: No era cierto que la fiesta fuera el sábado.
examples.en: It wasn't true that the party was on Saturday.
examples.note: Events use ser, and the denial pushes it into the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era cierto que él fuera mi mejor amigo.
examples.en: It wasn't true that he was my best friend.
examples.note: You deny a past state. Era or fue after que would assert it.

contrast.es: Era cierto que fue mi mejor amigo.
contrast.en: It was true that he was my best friend.
contrast.note: Era cierto states a fact (indicative, and fue = the friendship is over). No era cierto denies it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical rather than a known fact.

examples.es: Aunque fuera tarde, iría.
examples.en: Even if it were late, I'd go.
examples.note: Fuera is hypothetical. The result is in the conditional (iría).

examples.es: Aunque la entrevista fuera larga, no me preocuparía.
examples.en: Even if the interview were long, I wouldn't worry.
examples.note: You don't know how long it will be, so aunque + subjunctive.

examples.es: Aunque fuera difícil, lo haría.
examples.en: Even if it were hard, I'd do it.
examples.note: You are allowing for a hypothetical difficulty.

contrast.es: Aunque fue difícil, lo hice.
contrast.en: Although it was hard, I did it.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a known fact (fue = completed past). Aunque + imperfect subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Fuera and fuese are not the same as fue or era: 'ojalá fuera' is a wish, 'fue' is a completed fact and 'era' is background. Nosotros takes an accent (fuéramos). 'Como si fuera' (as if it were) always takes the imperfect subjunctive.

title: por vs para

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose involving a different subject, and after a past main verb the verb goes in the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Trabajaba para que mi familia viviera bien.
examples.en: I worked so my family could live well.
examples.note: Past main verb + para que = imperfect subjunctive. Not 'vive' or 'viva'.

examples.es: Te llamé para que me dijeras la verdad.
examples.en: I called you so that you'd tell me the truth.
examples.note: Decir's preterite is dijeron, so the subjunctive is dijeras. No i before -eras: never 'dijieras'.

examples.es: Te escribí para que supieras que pensaba en ti.
examples.en: I wrote to you so that you'd know I was thinking of you.
examples.note: Saber's preterite stem is sup-. Different subjects (yo / tú) = para que + subjunctive. Pensaba stays indicative.

contrast.es: Te escribí para saber cómo estabas.
contrast.en: I wrote to find out how you were.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. Different subject = para que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Necessity is a judgement about what should happen, not a fact, so it takes the subjunctive. Past tense gives the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era necesario que habláramos por teléfono.
examples.en: We needed to talk by phone.
examples.note: Por teléfono = by means of the phone. Nosotros takes an accent: habláramos.

examples.es: Era necesario que pagaras por adelantado.
examples.en: You needed to pay in advance.
examples.note: No spelling change before -ra: pagaras. The gu only appears before e (pagues).

examples.es: Era necesario que lo hicieras por convicción, no por obligación.
examples.en: You had to do it out of conviction, not out of obligation.
examples.note: Por = motive or cause. Hacer's preterite stem is hic-: hicieras.

contrast.es: Era necesario hacerlo por convicción.
contrast.en: It was necessary to do it out of conviction.
contrast.note: No specific person = infinitive. Naming who must act = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubt in the past means you didn't take the statement as fact, so the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que Ana trabajara por la noche.
examples.en: I doubted Ana worked at night.
examples.note: Por la noche = during the night (por for time periods).

examples.es: Dudaba que llegaran para las ocho.
examples.en: I doubted they'd arrive by eight.
examples.note: Llegar has no spelling change here: llegaran. Para = a deadline.

examples.es: Dudaba que ese regalo fuera para mí.
examples.en: I doubted that gift was for me.
examples.note: Para marks the recipient. Fuera is the imperfect subjunctive of ser.

contrast.es: No dudaba que ese regalo era para mí.
contrast.en: I didn't doubt that gift was for me.
contrast.note: Dudar takes the subjunctive. No dudar expresses certainty, so the indicative (era).

tricky: Por and para never change, but para que after a past verb needs the imperfect subjunctive: 'trabajaba para que viviera', not 'para que vive'. It is not 'porque' (because), which takes the indicative. With the same subject use para + infinitive: 'Estudiaba para aprobar'.

title: saber vs conocer

triggers.explanation: When you describe someone who may not exist or isn't identified, the relative clause takes the subjunctive. A past search gives the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Buscaba a alguien que supiera cocinar.
examples.en: I was looking for someone who knew how to cook.
examples.note: Saber = skill. Supiera is irregular (sup-), not 'sabiera'.

examples.es: Buscaba a alguien que conociera la ciudad.
examples.en: I was looking for someone who knew the city.
examples.note: Conocer is regular here: conociera. The present -zc- (conozca) does not carry over.

examples.es: Buscaba a alguien que conociera a mi hermano.
examples.en: I was looking for someone who knew my brother.
examples.note: Any person who fits, existence not guaranteed, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Buscaba a la chica que conocía a mi hermano.
contrast.en: I was looking for the girl who knew my brother.
contrast.note: A specific, known person takes the indicative (conocía).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive. After a past main verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me lo dijo antes de que lo supieran todos.
examples.en: She told me before everyone knew.
examples.note: Antes de que always triggers the subjunctive. Supieran is the ellos form.

examples.es: Te lo expliqué antes de que conocieras a mi familia.
examples.en: I explained it to you before you met my family.
examples.note: Conocer = to meet someone for the first time.

examples.es: Se lo conté antes de que lo supiera por otra persona.
examples.en: I told her before she found out from someone else.
examples.note: Antes de que + subjunctive: the knowing hadn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Se lo conté después de que lo supo por otra persona.
contrast.en: I told her after she found out from someone else.
contrast.note: Después de que with a completed event takes the indicative, while antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Reacting emotionally to something takes the subjunctive, even when the fact is true.

examples.es: Me alegré de que conocieras a Sofía.
examples.en: I was glad you met Sofía.
examples.note: Emotion + different subject = que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Me alegraba de que supieras tanto de música.
examples.en: I was glad you knew so much about music.
examples.note: Saber de = to know about a subject. Supieras is irregular.

examples.es: Me alegré de que ya conocieras a mi jefe.
examples.en: I was glad you already knew my boss.
examples.note: Conocer is personal acquaintance.

contrast.es: Sabía que ya conocías a mi jefe.
contrast.en: I knew you already knew my boss.
contrast.note: Simply knowing a fact takes the indicative. Reacting to it takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Supiera (saber) is irregular, but conociera (conocer) is regular here, so the present-tense -zc- does not carry over: 'conociera', never 'conozciera'. With 'buscaba a alguien que...', 'que supiera' means anyone who qualifies, while 'que sabía' points to a particular person.

title: salir vs quedar

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something, even in the past, involves a wish rather than a fact, so the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que quedáramos el sábado.
examples.en: I hoped we'd get together on Saturday.
examples.note: Quedar = to arrange to meet. Quedáramos carries an accent.

examples.es: Esperaba que salieras con nosotros esa noche.
examples.en: I hoped you'd go out with us that night.
examples.note: Salir is regular here: salieras. Unlike the present salgas, there is no -g-.

examples.es: Esperaba que la cena de la noche siguiente saliera bien.
examples.en: I hoped the next night's dinner would go well.
examples.note: Salir bien = to turn out well. Hope = subjunctive.

contrast.es: Sabía que la cena saldría bien.
contrast.en: I knew the dinner would go well.
contrast.note: Saber = certainty, so indicative or conditional. Esperar = hope, so subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Saying what would be better is a judgement, so it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era mejor que quedáramos en el centro.
examples.en: It was better if we met downtown.
examples.note: Quedar en = to arrange to meet at a place. In Spain, el centro (the city centre).

examples.es: Era mejor que salieras temprano del trabajo.
examples.en: It was better if you left work early.
examples.note: Salir de = to leave a place.

examples.es: Era mejor que no salieras esa noche.
examples.en: It was better that you didn't go out that night.
examples.note: Advice, not fact, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Era obvio que no salías esa noche.
contrast.en: It was obvious you weren't going out that night.
contrast.note: Era obvio states a fact (indicative). Era mejor gives advice (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something still unfinished from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que trabajaría hasta que saliera el último cliente.
examples.en: He said he would work until the last customer left.
examples.note: From his viewpoint, the leaving hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Me pidió que no me fuera hasta que quedara todo limpio.
examples.en: He asked me not to leave until everything was clean.
examples.note: Quedar + adjective = to end up in a state.

examples.es: Prometió esperar hasta que salieras del hospital.
examples.en: He promised to wait until you left the hospital.
examples.note: A promised, still-unfinished event = subjunctive.

contrast.es: Esperó hasta que saliste del hospital.
contrast.en: He waited until you left the hospital.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Quedar is regular (quedara, quedáramos). Salir is also regular in the imperfect subjunctive (saliera, salieras), so the -g- of salga does not appear. Quedar con alguien (to arrange to meet), quedar (to be left) and quedarse (to stay) are different verbs in practice.

title: llevar vs hacer (time)

triggers.explanation: Reacting with surprise to a fact calls for the subjunctive, even though the fact is true.

examples.es: Me sorprendió que llevaras tanto tiempo esperando.
examples.en: I was surprised you had been waiting for so long.
examples.note: Llevar + gerund = how long you've been doing something. Llevaras is the tú form.

examples.es: Me sorprendía que hiciera tantos años que no nos veíamos.
examples.en: I was surprised it had been so many years since we last saw each other.
examples.note: Hace + time becomes hiciera. The clause after que stays indicative: no nos veíamos.

examples.es: Me sorprendió que Ana llevara diez años sin vacaciones.
examples.en: I was surprised Ana had gone ten years without a holiday.
examples.note: Llevar + time + sin + noun = how long you've gone without something.

contrast.es: Sabía que Ana llevaba diez años sin vacaciones.
contrast.en: I knew Ana had gone ten years without a holiday.
contrast.note: Simply knowing a fact takes the indicative. Reacting to it takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubting a statement takes it out of the realm of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que llevara mucho tiempo.
examples.en: I didn't think it took long.
examples.note: Llevar can also mean to take (time).

examples.es: No creía que hiciera ya un año que se había marchado.
examples.en: I didn't think it had been a year already since he'd left.
examples.note: Only the hace verb changes: hiciera, never 'hacera'. Hiciera is irregular.

examples.es: No creía que llevaran allí más de una semana.
examples.en: I didn't think they'd been there more than a week.
examples.note: Llevar allí + time = how long they'd been there.

contrast.es: Creía que llevaban allí más de una semana.
contrast.en: I thought they'd been there more than a week.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Si + imperfect subjunctive describes a hypothetical situation, with the conditional in the result.

examples.es: Si llevaras el coche al taller, te lo arreglarían hoy.
examples.en: If you took the car to the garage, they'd fix it today.
examples.note: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional (arreglarían).

examples.es: Si hiciera calor, iríamos a la playa.
examples.en: If it were warm, we'd go to the beach.
examples.note: Weather uses hacer: hace calor becomes hiciera calor.

examples.es: Si llevaras un año aquí, podrías pedir el permiso.
examples.en: If you had been here a year, you could apply for the permit.
examples.note: A hypothetical time threshold, so the imperfect subjunctive.

contrast.es: Si llevas un año aquí, puedes pedir el permiso.
contrast.en: If you've been here a year, you can apply for the permit.
contrast.note: Si + present indicative = a real, open possibility. Si + imperfect subjunctive = hypothetical or unlikely.

tricky: Llevar is regular (llevara, llevaras) and hacer is irregular (hiciera, hicieras), so never 'hacera'. In hace-clauses only the hace verb changes: 'Era increíble que hiciera diez años que vivía allí', with the second clause staying indicative.

title: pedir vs preguntar

triggers.explanation: An instruction passed on through que is a wish for someone to act, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Le dije que preguntara por el horario.
examples.en: I told him to ask about the schedule.
examples.note: Preguntar por = to ask about. Regular: preguntara.

examples.es: Le dije que pidiera un café con leche.
examples.en: I told him to order a coffee with milk.
examples.note: Pedir changes e→i in pidieron, so pidiera, never 'pediera'. Pedir = to ask for / order.

examples.es: Le dije que pidiera perdón a su madre.
examples.en: I told him to apologise to his mother.
examples.note: Pedir perdón = to apologise. Le dije que = an instruction.

contrast.es: Dijo que pedía perdón a su madre.
contrast.en: He said he apologised to his mother.
contrast.note: Le dije que to give an order takes the subjunctive. Dijo que to report a fact takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Annoyance is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive follows.

examples.es: Me molestaba que preguntaras tantas cosas.
examples.en: It annoyed me that you asked so many questions.
examples.note: Regular verb, regular -aras ending.

examples.es: Me molestaba que siempre pidieras lo más caro.
examples.en: It bothered me that you always ordered the most expensive thing.
examples.note: Stem change e→i: pidieras.

examples.es: Me molestaba que nunca me preguntaras cómo estaba.
examples.en: It bothered me that you never asked me how I was.
examples.note: Preguntar = ask a question. 'Me pidieras cómo estaba' would be wrong.

contrast.es: Nunca me preguntabas cómo estaba.
contrast.en: You never asked me how I was.
contrast.note: A plain statement uses the indicative. The emotional reaction uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Sin que always takes the subjunctive when a different subject is involved.

examples.es: Entró sin que nadie preguntara nada.
examples.en: He went in without anyone asking anything.
examples.note: Sin que = without + a different subject.

examples.es: Lo hacía todo sin que se lo pidieran.
examples.en: She did everything without being asked.
examples.note: Stem change in the ellos form: pidieran.

examples.es: Entré sin que me pidieran el carné.
examples.en: I got in without them asking for my ID.
examples.note: They ask, I get in, so a different subject.

contrast.es: Entré sin pedir el carné.
contrast.en: I went in without asking for the ID.
contrast.note: Same subject = sin + infinitive. Different subject = sin que + imperfect subjunctive.

tricky: Pedir changes e→i in every imperfect subjunctive form, nosotros included: pidiera, pidieras, pidiera, pidiéramos, pidieran, never 'pediera'. Preguntar is regular: preguntara. Keep the meanings apart: 'que preguntara por ti' asks about you, while 'que pidiera por ti' would mean ask (or order) for you, and 'que pidiera en tu nombre' would mean ask on your behalf.

title: poder vs saber (can)

triggers.explanation: A mere possibility isn't a fact, so the subjunctive is used.

examples.es: Era posible que Luis pudiera venir al día siguiente.
examples.en: It was possible that Luis could come the next day.
examples.note: Poder's preterite stem is pud-: pudiera. The o→ue change of the present (pueda) is gone.

examples.es: Era posible que no pudiéramos salir.
examples.en: It was possible we wouldn't be able to go out.
examples.note: Nosotros: pudiéramos, with an accent.

examples.es: Era posible que él no supiera nadar.
examples.en: It was possible he couldn't swim.
examples.note: Saber + infinitive = can, as a learned skill. Supiera is irregular.

contrast.es: Era evidente que él no sabía nadar.
contrast.en: It was obvious he couldn't swim.
contrast.note: Era posible expresses uncertainty (subjunctive). Era evidente states a fact (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Strong liking or delight is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive follows.

examples.es: Me encantó que supieras cantar.
examples.en: I loved that you could sing.
examples.note: Saber cantar = can sing as a skill. Supieras is irregular.

examples.es: Me encantó que pudieran venir todos.
examples.en: I loved that everyone could come.
examples.note: Poder = be free / able to. Stem pud-: pudieran.

examples.es: Me encantaba que supieras tocar el piano.
examples.en: I loved that you could play the piano.
examples.note: A skill you learned uses saber, not poder.

contrast.es: Vi que sabías tocar el piano.
contrast.en: I saw you could play the piano.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting emotionally uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: A menos que always takes the subjunctive because it introduces a condition that may not happen. After a past or conditional main verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que iría a la fiesta a menos que no pudiera.
examples.en: She said she'd go to the party unless she couldn't.
examples.note: A menos que = unless. Always followed by the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prometió ayudarte a menos que no supiera cómo hacerlo.
examples.en: He promised to help you unless he didn't know how to do it.
examples.note: Saber cómo = to know how to.

examples.es: Dijo que no iría a menos que pudiera llevar a su hijo.
examples.en: She said she wouldn't go unless she could take her son.
examples.note: Poder = to be allowed / able.

contrast.es: Dijo que no iría si no podía llevar a su hijo.
contrast.en: She said she wouldn't go if she couldn't take her son.
contrast.note: Si + imperfect indicative reports a similar condition. A menos que always needs the subjunctive.

tricky: Poder uses pud- in the imperfect subjunctive: pudiera, pudieras, pudiéramos, never 'pueda' or 'podiera'. Saber uses sup-: supiera. For 'can', poder is ability or permission, saber is a learned skill: 'que supieras nadar' (you knew how) vs 'que pudieras nadar' (you were able to).

title: deber vs tener que

triggers.explanation: Judging what is normal is an evaluation, not a statement of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era normal que tuvieras miedo.
examples.en: It was normal that you were scared.
examples.note: Tener miedo = to be afraid. Tener's preterite stem is tuv-: tuvieras.

examples.es: Era normal que tuviéramos que repetir los ejercicios.
examples.en: It was normal that we had to repeat the exercises.
examples.note: Tener que + infinitive = have to. Tener changes (tuviéramos), but tener que keeps the infinitive.

examples.es: Era normal que debiéramos pedir permiso antes.
examples.en: It was normal that we should ask permission first.
examples.note: Deber + infinitive = obligation. Deber is regular: debiéramos, with an accent.

contrast.es: Debíamos pedir permiso antes.
contrast.en: We had to ask permission first.
contrast.note: Deber states the obligation as a fact (indicative). After era normal que it goes in the imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotion, and the thing feared hasn't happened, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Temía que tuvieras razón.
examples.en: I was afraid you were right.
examples.note: Tener razón = to be right. Temía que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Temía que debieras pagar una multa.
examples.en: I was afraid you had to pay a fine.
examples.note: Deber + infinitive = must / have to. It's regular: debieras.

examples.es: Temía que tuvieran que cancelar el viaje.
examples.en: I feared they'd have to cancel the trip.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ellos) = que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Sabía que tenían que cancelar el viaje.
contrast.en: I knew they had to cancel the trip.
contrast.note: Sabía que states a fact (indicative). Temía que expresses fear (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Por mucho que means 'however much', and it takes the subjunctive when the amount is hypothetical or conceded.

examples.es: Por mucho que tuvieras, nunca era suficiente.
examples.en: However much you had, it was never enough.
examples.note: Por mucho que + subjunctive = however much.

examples.es: Por mucho que debiera estudiar, siempre sacaba tiempo para jugar.
examples.en: However much he had to study, he always found time to play.
examples.note: Deber + infinitive = obligation. Debiera is regular.

examples.es: Por mucho que tuvieras que esforzarte, valía la pena.
examples.en: However hard you had to try, it was worth it.
examples.note: Concession with a hypothetical amount of effort.

contrast.es: Tenías que esforzarte mucho, pero valía la pena.
contrast.en: You had to try very hard, but it was worth it.
contrast.note: A flat statement of fact uses the indicative. Por mucho que + subjunctive concedes a point.

tricky: Tener is irregular (tuviera, tuvieras, tuviéramos), but deber is regular (debiera, debiéramos). In 'era normal que tuviéramos que repetirlo' only tener changes, and tener que is still followed by an infinitive. Deber de + infinitive means probability, not obligation.

title: ir vs venir

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to do something is a request, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is imperfect.

examples.es: Te pedí que vinieras temprano.
examples.en: I asked you to come early.
examples.note: Venir's preterite is vinieron, so vinieras, never 'venieras'.

examples.es: Te pedí que fueras a la farmacia.
examples.en: I asked you to go to the pharmacy.
examples.note: Ir shares fueras with ser. Context tells you which verb it is.

examples.es: Te pedí que vinieras conmigo al médico.
examples.en: I asked you to come with me to the doctor.
examples.note: Venir = movement toward the speaker or a shared destination.

contrast.es: Me dijiste que venías conmigo al médico.
contrast.en: You told me you were coming with me to the doctor.
contrast.note: Pedir que = a request (subjunctive). Decir que = reporting (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Después de que about an event that was still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que saldría después de que viniera su madre.
examples.en: She said she'd go out after her mother came.
examples.note: From her viewpoint, the coming hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Dijimos que comeríamos después de que fuéramos al banco.
examples.en: We said we'd eat after we went to the bank.
examples.note: Fuéramos is the nosotros subjunctive, with an accent.

examples.es: Quedamos en que hablaríamos después de que vinieras a casa.
examples.en: We agreed we'd talk after you came home.
examples.note: Future from a past viewpoint, so the imperfect subjunctive.

contrast.es: Hablamos después de que viniste a casa.
contrast.en: We talked after you came home.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Judging something as strange is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era raro que Luis no viniera.
examples.en: It was odd that Luis didn't come.
examples.note: Era raro que + subjunctive, even though the fact is real.

examples.es: Era raro que fueran solos.
examples.en: It was odd that they went on their own.
examples.note: Fueran is the ellos form of ir.

examples.es: Era raro que no vinieras a las reuniones.
examples.en: It was odd that you didn't come to the meetings.
examples.note: The speaker is evaluating a fact, not stating one.

contrast.es: Era cierto que no venías a las reuniones.
contrast.en: It was true that you didn't come to the meetings.
contrast.note: Era cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Era raro judges it (subjunctive).

tricky: Venir's imperfect subjunctive is viniera, vinieras, viniéramos, vinieran. Ir shares fuera with ser, so 'fueras' can mean 'you were' or 'you went', and context decides. The speaker's anchor point still decides ir vs venir.

title: traer vs llevar

triggers.explanation: Needing someone else to act is a request, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesitaba que llevaras esta carta al correo.
examples.en: I needed you to take this letter to the post office.
examples.note: Llevar = to take away from where we are. Regular: llevaras.

examples.es: Necesitaba que me trajeras los documentos.
examples.en: I needed you to bring me the documents.
examples.note: Traer is irregular in the preterite (trajeron), so trajeras. No i before -eras: never 'trajieras'.

examples.es: Necesitaba que trajeras los papeles a la oficina.
examples.en: I needed you to bring the papers to the office.
examples.note: Traer = toward the speaker's location. The office is where I was.

contrast.es: Necesitaba traer los papeles a la oficina.
contrast.en: I needed to bring the papers to the office.
contrast.note: Same person = infinitive. A different person = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something important is a judgement about what should happen, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era importante que llevaras agua.
examples.en: It was important that you took water.
examples.note: Regular: llevaras.

examples.es: Era importante que todos trajeran el pasaporte.
examples.en: It was important that everyone brought their passport.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so trajeran.

examples.es: Era importante que llevaras el paraguas ese día.
examples.en: It was important that you took the umbrella that day.
examples.note: Llevar here means carry with you.

contrast.es: Era evidente que llevabas el paraguas ese día.
contrast.en: It was obvious you were carrying the umbrella that day.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era importante expresses what should happen (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Con tal de que introduces a condition that may or may not be met, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que iría a la fiesta con tal de que lo llevaras.
examples.en: He said he'd go to the party as long as you took him.
examples.note: Con tal de que always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me prestó el coche con tal de que lo trajera con el depósito lleno.
examples.en: He lent me the car as long as I brought it back with a full tank.
examples.note: Traer = bring back to where he is.

examples.es: Hacía lo que fuera con tal de que le trajeran buenas noticias.
examples.en: He'd do anything as long as they brought him good news.
examples.note: A different subject, so con tal de que + subjunctive.

contrast.es: Hacía lo que fuera con tal de traer buenas noticias.
contrast.en: He'd do anything to bring good news.
contrast.note: Same subject = con tal de + infinitive. Different subject = con tal de que + imperfect subjunctive.

tricky: Traer is irregular: trajera, trajeras, trajéramos, trajeran (from trajeron), with no i. Llevar is regular: llevara. Direction decides the verb: 'que me trajeras' (bring it to me) vs 'que me llevaras' (take me away).

title: querer vs amar

triggers.explanation: Preferring that someone else act in a certain way is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prefería que amaras tu trabajo.
examples.en: I preferred that you loved your job.
examples.note: Amar is regular: amaras.

examples.es: Prefería que me quisieras tal como era.
examples.en: I preferred that you loved me as I was.
examples.note: Querer's preterite stem is quis-: quisieras. No e→ie change here.

examples.es: Prefería que quisieran a mis hijos como a los suyos.
examples.en: I preferred that they loved my children like their own.
examples.note: Querer a = to love someone (family, friends). The personal a is needed.

contrast.es: Sabía que querían a mis hijos como a los suyos.
contrast.en: I knew they loved my children like their own.
contrast.note: Saber states a fact (indicative). Preferir expresses a wish (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Tal vez expresses real uncertainty and usually takes the subjunctive (the indicative is also possible). With a past or unlikely situation, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Tal vez amara la música clásica de joven.
examples.en: Maybe he loved classical music when he was young.
examples.note: Tal vez + imperfect subjunctive = doubt about the past.

examples.es: Tal vez quisiera quedarse en casa aquel día.
examples.en: Maybe she wanted to stay at home that day.
examples.note: Querer = to want. Quisiera is also the polite 'I would like' form.

examples.es: Tal vez quisiera todavía a su ex entonces.
examples.en: Maybe she still loved her ex back then.
examples.note: You aren't sure, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Tal vez quería todavía a su ex entonces.
contrast.en: Maybe she still loved her ex back then (I lean toward yes).
contrast.note: Tal vez + indicative is also possible and leans toward belief. The subjunctive signals stronger doubt.

triggers.explanation: Por más que means 'no matter how much', and it takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Por más que quisiera, no podía ir.
examples.en: No matter how much I wanted to, I couldn't go.
examples.note: Por más que + subjunctive = however much.

examples.es: Por más que amaras tu trabajo, necesitabas vacaciones.
examples.en: No matter how much you loved your job, you needed a holiday.
examples.note: Concession with a hypothetical degree.

examples.es: Por más que lo quisieras, no iba a cambiar.
examples.en: No matter how much you loved him, he wasn't going to change.
examples.note: Lo quisieras = you loved him. Concession.

contrast.es: Lo querías mucho, pero no iba a cambiar.
contrast.en: You loved him a lot, but he wasn't going to change.
contrast.note: A direct statement of fact uses the indicative. Por más que + subjunctive concedes a point.

tricky: Querer uses quis- in the imperfect subjunctive: quisiera, quisieras, quisiéramos, never 'quiriera' or 'queriera'. Amar is regular (amara). Quisiera is also the polite 'I would like', which is a different use from the past-time meaning in these examples.

title: mirar vs ver

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que miraras esta foto.
examples.en: I wanted you to look at this photo.
examples.note: Mirar is regular: miraras.

examples.es: Quería que vieras esta película conmigo.
examples.en: I wanted you to see this film with me.
examples.note: Ver is regular in this tense: vieras, built on vieron.

examples.es: Quería que me miraras a los ojos.
examples.en: I wanted you to look me in the eye.
examples.note: Mirar = point your eyes deliberately.

contrast.es: Quería mirarte a los ojos.
contrast.en: I wanted to look you in the eye.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era probable que mirara la tele esa noche.
examples.en: He would probably watch TV that night.
examples.note: Mirar la tele = to watch TV (deliberately looking).

examples.es: Era probable que viéramos a tus primos al día siguiente.
examples.en: We would probably see your cousins the next day.
examples.note: Viéramos takes an accent. It's the nosotros form.

examples.es: Era probable que viera a Marta en la fiesta.
examples.en: I would probably see Marta at the party.
examples.note: Ver = to see or run into, without effort.

contrast.es: Estaba seguro de que vería a Marta en la fiesta.
contrast.en: I was sure I'd see Marta at the party.
contrast.note: Estar seguro de que = certainty (indicative/conditional). Era probable que = likelihood (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: When the person you describe doesn't exist, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No había nadie que mirara esa serie.
examples.en: There was nobody who watched that series.
examples.note: Nadie = no such person, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No había nadie que viera bien sin gafas.
examples.en: There was nobody who saw well without glasses.
examples.note: Viera = ver.

examples.es: No había nadie que viera el error.
examples.en: There was nobody who saw the error.
examples.note: A non-existent person calls for the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Había alguien que veía el error.
contrast.en: There was someone who saw the error.
contrast.note: Había alguien que + indicative: such a person existed.

tricky: Ver's imperfect subjunctive is viera, vieras, viéramos, vieran, regular from vieron. Mirar is regular (mirara). Viéramos has a written accent, as every nosotros form does, unlike the present veamos. Mirar is the deliberate act, ver is what reaches your eyes.

title: escuchar vs oír

triggers.explanation: Giving advice expresses what you want someone to do, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te aconsejé que escucharas a tu madre.
examples.en: I advised you to listen to your mother.
examples.note: Escuchar is regular: escucharas.

examples.es: Te aconsejé que oyeras ambas versiones.
examples.en: I advised you to hear both versions.
examples.note: Oír has a y in the preterite (oyeron), so oyeras, never 'oyieras'.

examples.es: Te aconsejé que escucharas lo que decía el médico.
examples.en: I advised you to listen to what the doctor said.
examples.note: Escuchar = listen with attention.

contrast.es: Te dije que escuchabas lo que decía el médico.
contrast.en: I told you that you listened to what the doctor said.
contrast.note: Aconsejar expresses a wish (subjunctive). Decir que reports a fact (indicative).

triggers.explanation: Expressing regret is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era una lástima que no escucharas música.
examples.en: It was a shame you didn't listen to music.
examples.note: Era una lástima que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Era una lástima que no oyeran bien.
examples.en: It was a shame they couldn't hear well.
examples.note: Oír is the ability to hear. Oyeran has a y.

examples.es: Era una lástima que no oyeras bien con ese ruido.
examples.en: It was a shame you couldn't hear well with that noise.
examples.note: Oír = physically hear, not choose to.

contrast.es: Era cierto que no oías bien con ese ruido.
contrast.en: It was true that you couldn't hear well with that noise.
contrast.note: Era cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Era una lástima reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablaba alto para que todos escucharan.
examples.en: I spoke loudly so that everyone listened.
examples.note: Para que = so that. Different subjects.

examples.es: Te lo repetí para que lo oyeras bien.
examples.en: I repeated it so that you'd hear it properly.
examples.note: Oír = to catch what is said.

examples.es: Puse la radio para que escucháramos las noticias.
examples.en: I put the radio on so that we could listen to the news.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / nosotros).

contrast.es: Puse la radio para escuchar las noticias.
contrast.en: I put the radio on to listen to the news.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. Different subject = para que + imperfect subjunctive.

tricky: Oír has a y in the imperfect subjunctive: oyera, oyeras, oyéramos, oyeran, never 'oigiera' (the present oiga does not carry over). Escuchar is regular: escuchara. Don't mix them: 'que oyeras' is the sound reaching you, 'que escucharas' is you paying attention.

title: acordarse vs recordar

triggers.explanation: Expressing amazement is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era increíble que te acordaras de todo.
examples.en: It was incredible that you remembered everything.
examples.note: Acordarse de = to remember. The o→ue change is gone: te acordaras.

examples.es: Era increíble que recordaran aquel día.
examples.en: It was incredible that they remembered that day.
examples.note: Recordar takes no de. Regular: recordaran.

examples.es: Era increíble que no te acordaras de mi cumpleaños.
examples.en: It was incredible that you didn't remember my birthday.
examples.note: Acordarse is reflexive and takes de.

contrast.es: Era cierto que no te acordabas de mi cumpleaños.
contrast.en: It was true that you didn't remember my birthday.
contrast.note: Era cierto asserts a fact (indicative). Era increíble reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: No era que denies a reason someone might assume, and takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era que me acordara de todo.
examples.en: It wasn't that I remembered everything.
examples.note: Reflexive: me acordara.

examples.es: No era que recordara mucho de aquella época.
examples.en: It wasn't that I remembered much from that time.
examples.note: Recordar + direct object, no de.

examples.es: No era que me acordara mal; era que nadie me lo había dicho.
examples.en: It wasn't that I remembered badly; it was that nobody had told me.
examples.note: You are denying a reason.

contrast.es: Era que me acordaba mal.
contrast.en: The thing was, I remembered it wrong.
contrast.note: Era que + indicative gives a real reason. No era que + subjunctive denies one.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me dijo que me avisaría en cuanto se acordara.
examples.en: He told me he'd let me know as soon as he remembered.
examples.note: The remembering hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Prometió decírmelo en cuanto recordara su nombre.
examples.en: He promised to tell me as soon as he remembered his name.
examples.note: Promise about the future, from a past viewpoint, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que llamaría en cuanto se acordara.
examples.en: She said she'd call as soon as she remembered.
examples.note: A future moment that hadn't come yet.

contrast.es: Llamó en cuanto se acordó.
contrast.en: She called as soon as she remembered.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: The o→ue stem change of the present disappears: me acordara, recordara, never 'me acuerdara'. Acordarse takes de ('me acordaba de eso') while recordar takes the object directly ('recordaba eso'). Only recordar can mean 'to remind'.

title: sentir vs sentirse

triggers.explanation: Hoping something for someone else is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que te sintieras mejor.
examples.en: I hoped you felt better.
examples.note: Sentirse + adjective = to feel (a state). The preterite sintieron gives sintieras.

examples.es: Esperaba que nos sintiéramos cómodos allí.
examples.en: I hoped we'd feel comfortable there.
examples.note: Every form uses sint-: sintiéramos, with an accent, never 'sentiéramos'.

examples.es: Esperaba que no te sintieras obligado.
examples.en: I hoped you didn't feel obliged.
examples.note: Sentirse obligado = to feel obliged. The reflexive describes your own state.

contrast.es: Sabía que no te sentías obligado.
contrast.en: I knew you didn't feel obliged.
contrast.note: Sabía que states a fact (indicative). Esperaba que expresses a hope (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Regret is an emotional reaction to something, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Lamentaba que te sintieras solo.
examples.en: I was sorry you felt lonely.
examples.note: Sentirse solo = to feel lonely.

examples.es: Lamentaba que sintieras tanto dolor.
examples.en: I was sorry you felt so much pain.
examples.note: Sentir + noun = to feel something. No reflexive pronoun.

examples.es: Lamentaba que se sintiera culpable.
examples.en: I was sorry he felt guilty.
examples.note: Sentirse culpable = to feel guilty. Reflexive.

contrast.es: Veía que se sentía culpable.
contrast.en: I saw he felt guilty.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical or not established.

examples.es: Aunque me sintiera mal, iría.
examples.en: Even if I felt bad, I'd go.
examples.note: Hypothetical feeling, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque sintiera miedo, seguiría adelante.
examples.en: Even if I felt fear, I'd carry on.
examples.note: Sentir miedo = to feel fear. No reflexive pronoun.

examples.es: Aunque te sintieras cansado, tendrías que ir.
examples.en: Even if you felt tired, you'd have to go.
examples.note: You aren't sure you'd feel tired, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Aunque te sentías cansado, tenías que ir.
contrast.en: Although you did feel tired, you had to go.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = the tiredness was real. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Sentir changes e→i in every imperfect subjunctive form: sintiera, sintieras, sintiéramos, sintieran, never 'sentiera'. Without the reflexive it means something different: 'que sintieras pena' (feel sorrow) vs 'que te sintieras triste' (feel sad).

title: pensar vs creer

triggers.explanation: Denying that something was true removes it from fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era verdad que pensara en otra persona.
examples.en: It wasn't true that I was thinking of someone else.
examples.note: Pensar en = to think about. Regular here: pensara.

examples.es: No era verdad que ella creyera en fantasmas.
examples.en: It wasn't true that she believed in ghosts.
examples.note: Creer en = to believe in. Creyera has a y, as in creyeron.

examples.es: No era verdad que él creyera todo lo que decían.
examples.en: It wasn't true that he believed everything they said.
examples.note: Creer = to believe something is true.

contrast.es: Era verdad que él creía todo lo que decían.
contrast.en: It was true that he believed everything they said.
contrast.note: Era verdad asserts a fact (indicative). No era verdad denies it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me daba miedo que pensaras mal de mí.
examples.en: I was afraid you'd think badly of me.
examples.note: Pensar mal de = to think badly of.

examples.es: Me daba miedo que no creyeran mi historia.
examples.en: I was afraid they wouldn't believe my story.
examples.note: Creer + direct object = to believe.

examples.es: Me daba miedo que pensaran que mentía.
examples.en: I was afraid they'd think I was lying.
examples.note: Pensar que + indicative: 'mentía' stays indicative.

contrast.es: Sabía que pensaban que mentía.
contrast.en: I knew they thought I was lying.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Me daba miedo que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que me avisaría en cuanto pensara en algo.
examples.en: He said he'd let me know as soon as he thought of something.
examples.note: Future event from a past viewpoint, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me prometió decírmelo en cuanto creyera que estaba listo.
examples.en: He promised to tell me as soon as he thought it was ready.
examples.note: Creer que + indicative: 'estaba listo' is indicative.

examples.es: Dijo que decidiría en cuanto lo pensara bien.
examples.en: He said he'd decide as soon as he'd thought it through.
examples.note: Pensar bien = to think carefully.

contrast.es: Decidió en cuanto lo pensó bien.
contrast.en: He decided as soon as he thought it through.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Creía que and pensaba que take the indicative, but no creía que and no pensaba que take the imperfect subjunctive. Pensar loses its e→ie change here (pensara). Creer becomes creyera, with a y, not 'creiera'.

title: gastar vs pasar (spend)

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quería que gastaras tanto dinero.
examples.en: I didn't want you to spend so much money.
examples.note: Gastar = spend money or use up. Regular.

examples.es: No quería que pasaras la noche solo.
examples.en: I didn't want you to spend the night alone.
examples.note: Pasar = spend time, never gastar.

examples.es: No quería que se gastara la vida trabajando.
examples.en: I didn't want him to wear his life away working.
examples.note: Gastarse la vida = to wear your life away. Gastarse is reflexive here.

contrast.es: No quería gastarme la vida trabajando.
contrast.en: I didn't want to spend my whole life working.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Pleasure at something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me alegraba que pasaras el verano allí.
examples.en: I was glad you were spending the summer there.
examples.note: Pasar el verano = spend the summer.

examples.es: Me alegraba que gastaran menos energía.
examples.en: I was glad they used less energy.
examples.note: Gastar energía = to use up energy.

examples.es: Me alegraba que ya no gastaras tanto en ropa.
examples.en: I was glad you didn't spend so much on clothes any more.
examples.note: Gastar en = to spend on.

contrast.es: Veía que ya no gastabas tanto en ropa.
contrast.en: I saw you didn't spend so much on clothes any more.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Mientras + subjunctive means 'as long as', for a condition that was ongoing or still to be met.

examples.es: Dijo que mientras gastaras con cuidado, no había problema.
examples.en: He said that as long as you spent carefully, there was no problem.
examples.note: Mientras + subjunctive = as long as.

examples.es: Decía que mientras pasáramos tiempo juntos, era feliz.
examples.en: She said that as long as we spent time together, she was happy.
examples.note: Pasar tiempo = to spend time.

examples.es: Me prometió que mientras pasaras tiempo con ellos, serías feliz.
examples.en: He promised me that as long as you spent time with them, you'd be happy.
examples.note: A condition about the future from a past viewpoint, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Mientras pasabas tiempo con ellos, eras feliz.
contrast.en: While you spent time with them, you were happy.
contrast.note: Mientras + indicative = an actual, simultaneous situation. Mientras + subjunctive = as long as.

tricky: Gastar and pasar are both regular (gastara, pasara), and neither has a stem change. The catch is which one you use: money is gastar, time spent is pasar ('que pasaras el verano'), and time wasted is perder. Nosotros takes an accent: pasáramos.

title: hablar vs decir

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que hablaras con él.
examples.en: I wanted you to talk to him.
examples.note: Hablar con = to talk with. Regular.

examples.es: Quería que me dijeras la verdad.
examples.en: I wanted you to tell me the truth.
examples.note: Decir's preterite is dijeron, so dijeras. No i: never 'dijieras'.

examples.es: Quería que me dijeras que me querías.
examples.en: I wanted you to tell me that you loved me.
examples.note: Decir que = to say that. The first que triggers the subjunctive. Querías stays indicative.

contrast.es: Me decías que me querías.
contrast.en: You used to tell me you loved me.
contrast.note: Reporting what's said uses the indicative. Wanting someone to say it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Liking something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me gustaba que hablaras despacio.
examples.en: I liked it that you spoke slowly.
examples.note: Me gustaba que + subjunctive when someone else is the subject.

examples.es: Me gustaba que me dijeras lo que pensabas.
examples.en: I liked that you told me what you thought.
examples.note: Decir lo que = to say what. Dijeras is irregular.

examples.es: Me gustaba que ella hablara tantos idiomas.
examples.en: I liked that she spoke so many languages.
examples.note: Hablar + language = to speak a language.

contrast.es: Sabía que ella hablaba tantos idiomas.
contrast.en: I knew she spoke so many languages.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Me gustaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Me lo contó antes de que hablara con ella.
examples.en: He told me before I talked to her.
examples.note: Antes de que + different subjects always means subjunctive.

examples.es: Se lo dije antes de que lo dijera otra persona.
examples.en: I told her before someone else did.
examples.note: Decir: dijera, irregular.

examples.es: Hablé con ella antes de que hablara con tu jefe.
examples.en: I talked to her before she talked to your boss.
examples.note: The talking hadn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Hablé con ella después de que habló con tu jefe.
contrast.en: I talked to her after she talked to your boss.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative.

tricky: Decir is irregular: dijera, dijeras, dijéramos, dijeran, never 'dijiera'. Hablar is regular: hablara. The mood changes the meaning: 'te dije que vinieras' is an order (subjunctive) but 'te dije que venías' reports a fact (indicative).

title: encontrar vs buscar

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá encontraras lo que buscas.
examples.en: I wish you could find what you're looking for.
examples.note: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive suggests it seems unlikely. 'Buscas' stays indicative because it's a fact.

examples.es: Ojalá encontráramos un hotel barato.
examples.en: I wish we could find a cheap hotel.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: encontráramos.

examples.es: Ojalá encontraran a mi perro.
examples.en: I wish they would find my dog.
examples.note: A wish for something not yet achieved and uncertain.

contrast.es: Encontraron a mi perro.
contrast.en: They found my dog.
contrast.note: Ojalá + subjunctive = a wish. Indicative = a fact.

triggers.explanation: Judging how hard something is, is an evaluation, not a statement of fact.

examples.es: Era difícil que encontraras un buen taxi allí.
examples.en: It was hard for you to find a good taxi there.
examples.note: Era difícil que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Era difícil que buscaran otra solución.
examples.en: It was unlikely they'd look for another solution.
examples.note: Buscar has no spelling change before -ran: buscaran.

examples.es: Era difícil que encontrara trabajo sin experiencia.
examples.en: It was hard for him to find a job without experience.
examples.note: Evaluating how difficult something is, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Era verdad que encontraba trabajo sin experiencia.
contrast.en: It was true that he found jobs without experience.
contrast.note: Era verdad states a fact (indicative). Era difícil que gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Tan pronto como about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que saldríamos tan pronto como encontrara las llaves.
examples.en: He said we'd leave as soon as he found the keys.
examples.note: Future event from a past viewpoint, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me avisaría tan pronto como buscara en el sótano.
examples.en: He said he'd let me know as soon as he looked in the basement.
examples.note: Buscar en = to look in.

examples.es: Planeabas mudarte tan pronto como encontraras trabajo.
examples.en: You planned to move as soon as you found a job.
examples.note: A plan about the future, from a past viewpoint, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Te mudaste tan pronto como encontraste trabajo.
contrast.en: You moved as soon as you found a job.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Encontrar loses its o→ue change here: encontrara, encontraras, encontráramos, never 'encuentrara'. Buscar has no spelling change before -ra: buscara. 'Que buscaras' is the effort, and 'que encontraras' is the result.

title: perder vs faltar

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No quería que perdieras el tren.
examples.en: I didn't want you to miss the train.
examples.note: Perder el tren = to miss the train. The e→ie stem change of the present is gone: perdieras, never 'pierdieras'.

examples.es: No quería que faltara nada en la fiesta.
examples.en: I didn't want anything to be missing at the party.
examples.note: Faltar = to be missing / lacking. The subject is the thing that's missing: nada.

examples.es: No quería que perdieras la esperanza.
examples.en: I didn't want you to lose hope.
examples.note: Perder la esperanza = to lose hope.

contrast.es: Veía que perdías la esperanza.
contrast.en: I could see you were losing hope.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative (perdías). A wish uses the imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Regret is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era una pena que perdieras tanto tiempo.
examples.en: It was a shame you wasted so much time.
examples.note: Perder tiempo = to waste time.

examples.es: Era una pena que faltaran tantos jugadores.
examples.en: It was a shame so many players were missing.
examples.note: Plural subject (tantos jugadores), so faltaran.

examples.es: Era una pena que Luis faltara a la boda.
examples.en: It was a shame Luis missed the wedding.
examples.note: Faltar a = to miss (an event you should attend).

contrast.es: Era evidente que Luis faltaba a la boda.
contrast.en: It was obvious Luis was missing the wedding.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era una pena reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: A no ser que means 'unless' and always takes the subjunctive. With a conditional main verb, the clause is in the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Llegaríamos a tiempo, a no ser que perdiéramos el tren.
examples.en: We'd arrive on time, unless we missed the train.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: perdiéramos. Unlike the present, there is no stem change.

examples.es: Dijo que empezaríamos ya, a no ser que faltara algo.
examples.en: He said we'd start now, unless something was missing.
examples.note: Reporting a plan from a past viewpoint, so the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijeron que llegaría mañana, a no ser que se perdiera el paquete.
examples.en: They said it would arrive tomorrow, unless the parcel got lost.
examples.note: Perderse = to get lost. The main clause is conditional because it looks forward from the past.

contrast.es: Se perdió el paquete, así que no llegó.
contrast.en: The parcel got lost, so it didn't arrive.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite). Only the hypothetical exception takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Perder loses its e→ie stem change in the imperfect subjunctive: perdiera, perdieras, perdiéramos, perdieran, never 'pierdiera'. Faltar is regular (faltara) and has two uses. Faltar a + event or class = to be absent from it ('faltaba a clase'). The gustar-like use means to be lacking, and the missing thing is the subject ('me faltaba tiempo'). Perder is for missing a bus or train.

title: tocar vs jugar

triggers.explanation: Suggesting what someone else should do is a wish, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Proponía que jugáramos a las cartas.
examples.en: I suggested that we play cards.
examples.note: Jugar a = to play a game. Nosotros takes an accent: jugáramos.

examples.es: Proponía que Pablo jugara de portero.
examples.en: I suggested that Pablo play in goal.
examples.note: The u→ue stem change of the present is gone: jugara, never 'juegara'.

examples.es: Proponía que tocáramos esta canción en la fiesta.
examples.en: I suggested that we play this song at the party.
examples.note: Tocar = to play an instrument or piece of music. The c→qu change does not apply before -ára.

contrast.es: Proponía tocar esta canción en la fiesta.
contrast.en: I suggested playing this song at the party.
contrast.note: Same people involved = infinitive. A different subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que jugara hoy.
examples.en: I didn't think he'd play today.
examples.note: No creía que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que tocara bien la guitarra.
examples.en: I didn't think she played the guitar well.
examples.note: Tocar la guitarra = to play the guitar.

examples.es: No creía que Pablo jugara al tenis.
examples.en: I didn't think Pablo played tennis.
examples.note: Jugar al tenis = to play tennis.

contrast.es: Creía que Pablo jugaba al tenis.
contrast.en: I thought Pablo played tennis.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A habitual or completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Mi madre me decía que cuando jugara con mi hermano, tuviera cuidado.
examples.en: My mother used to tell me to be careful when I played with my brother.
examples.note: The playing hadn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me prometió que cuando tocara en el concierto, estaríamos en primera fila.
examples.en: He promised me that when he played at the concert, we'd be in the front row.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Me prometieron que cuando jugáramos la final, estarías aquí.
examples.en: They promised me that when we played the final, you'd be here.
examples.note: Jugar una final = to play a final. The event is still ahead of the promise.

contrast.es: Cuando jugamos la final, estabas allí.
contrast.en: When we played the final, you were there.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Jugar loses its u→ue change in the imperfect subjunctive: jugara, jugaras, jugáramos, jugaran, never 'juegara'. Tocar has no c→qu change either (tocara). Jugar is for games and sports (jugar a), tocar is for instruments and music (tocar la guitarra).

title: volver vs regresar

triggers.explanation: Worry is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me preocupaba que no regresara a tiempo.
examples.en: I was worried he wouldn't come back on time.
examples.note: Regresar is regular: regresara.

examples.es: Me preocupaba que no volvieras pronto.
examples.en: I was worried you wouldn't come back soon.
examples.note: The o→ue stem change of the present is gone: volvieras, never 'vuelvieras'.

examples.es: Me preocupaba que nunca volviera a casa.
examples.en: I was worried he would never come home again.
examples.note: Volver a casa = to come back home.

contrast.es: Veía que nunca volvía a casa.
contrast.en: I could see he never came home.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses uncertainty. In a past context, the imperfect subjunctive marks stronger doubt than the indicative.

examples.es: Quizás regresara aquella misma noche.
examples.en: Maybe he came back that same night.
examples.note: Quizás + imperfect subjunctive = doubt about something in the past.

examples.es: Quizás volvieran en verano, pero nadie lo sabía.
examples.en: Maybe they came back in the summer, but nobody knew.
examples.note: Volvieran has no stem change.

examples.es: Quizás no volviera a llamar nunca más; yo ya no esperaba nada.
examples.en: Maybe he never called again; I wasn't expecting anything any more.
examples.note: Volver a + infinitive = to do something again.

contrast.es: Quizás no volvió a llamar nunca más.
contrast.en: Maybe he never called again.
contrast.note: Quizás + indicative is also possible and sounds more confident. The subjunctive signals more doubt.

triggers.explanation: Siempre que + subjunctive means 'as long as' (a condition). With a habitual past meaning ('whenever'), it takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me dijo que siempre que regresaras, tendrías casa allí.
examples.en: He told me that as long as you came back, you'd have a home there.
examples.note: Siempre que = provided that, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Decíamos que siempre que regresáramos a tiempo, iríamos al cine.
examples.en: We said that as long as we got back in time, we'd go to the cinema.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: regresáramos.

examples.es: Te advirtió que siempre que volvieras tarde, le avisaras.
examples.en: He warned you that whenever you came home late, you should let him know.
examples.note: A rule about future situations, set in the past.

contrast.es: Siempre que volvías tarde, me avisabas.
contrast.en: Whenever you came home late, you let me know.
contrast.note: Siempre que + a habitual past fact takes the indicative.

tricky: Volver loses its o→ue change in the imperfect subjunctive: volviera, volvieras, volviéramos, volvieran, never 'vuelviera'. Its past participle is irregular (vuelto) but that doesn't affect these forms. Regresar is regular (regresara). In Spain regresar can sound more formal than volver.

title: dejar vs salir (leave)

triggers.explanation: Not allowing something is a wish about someone else's behaviour, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No permitía que dejaras la puerta abierta.
examples.en: I didn't allow you to leave the door open.
examples.note: Dejar = to leave something behind or in a state. Regular: dejaras.

examples.es: No permitía que salieras sin abrigo.
examples.en: I didn't allow you to go out without a coat.
examples.note: The -g- of the present (salgas) does not carry over: salieras, never 'salgieras'.

examples.es: No permitía que lo dejaras todo por un capricho.
examples.en: I didn't allow you to give up everything on a whim.
examples.note: Dejarlo todo = to give up everything.

contrast.es: Veía que lo dejabas todo por un capricho.
contrast.en: I could see you were giving up everything on a whim.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Not allowing something uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Judging something as logical is an evaluation, not a statement of fact, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era lógico que salieras temprano.
examples.en: It made sense that you left early.
examples.note: Regular in this tense: salieras.

examples.es: Era lógico que dejara el trabajo si no le pagaban.
examples.en: It made sense that he quit his job if they weren't paying him.
examples.note: Dejar el trabajo = to quit a job. The si clause stays indicative because it's a real fact.

examples.es: Era lógico que saliera de casa a los treinta.
examples.en: It made sense that she moved out at thirty.
examples.note: Salir de casa = to leave home, to move out.

contrast.es: Era evidente que salía de casa a los treinta.
contrast.en: It was clear she was moving out at thirty.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era lógico gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Salvo que means 'unless' and takes the subjunctive. With a conditional main verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me quedaría en casa, salvo que saliera el sol.
examples.en: I'd stay at home, unless the sun came out.
examples.note: Salir = to come out (of the sun). Salvo que + imperfect subjunctive after a conditional.

examples.es: Salvo que dejara de llover, nos quedaríamos en casa.
examples.en: Unless it stopped raining, we'd stay at home.
examples.note: Dejar de + infinitive = to stop doing something.

examples.es: Salvo que salieras antes, llegarías tarde.
examples.en: Unless you left earlier, you'd arrive late.
examples.note: A hypothetical exception, so the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Saliste antes, así que llegaste a tiempo.
contrast.en: You left earlier, so you arrived on time.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative.

tricky: Salir has no -g- in the imperfect subjunctive: saliera, salieras, saliéramos, salieran (from salieron), never 'salgiera'. Dejar is regular (dejara). Dejar is to leave something behind, salir is to go out of a place.

title: ser vs parecer

triggers.explanation: Not thinking something is true is a doubt, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No me parecía que fuera buena idea.
examples.en: I didn't think it was a good idea.
examples.note: Ser's imperfect subjunctive comes from fueron: fuera. It is the same as ir.

examples.es: No me parecía que fuera tan caro como decías.
examples.en: It didn't seem to me that it was as expensive as you said.
examples.note: Decías stays indicative because it is a fact about what was said.

examples.es: No me parecía que fuera de fiar.
examples.en: He didn't seem trustworthy to me.
examples.note: Ser de fiar = to be trustworthy.

contrast.es: Me parecía que era de fiar.
contrast.en: He seemed trustworthy to me.
contrast.note: Me parecía que takes the indicative. No me parecía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque pareciera fácil, no lo era.
examples.en: Even if it seemed easy, it wasn't.
examples.note: The -zc- of the present (parezca) does not carry over: pareciera, never 'parezciera'.

examples.es: Aunque pareciera mentira, era verdad.
examples.en: Even if it seemed unbelievable, it was true.
examples.note: Parecer mentira = to seem unbelievable.

examples.es: Aunque pareciera cansado, seguiría trabajando.
examples.en: Even if he seemed tired, he'd keep working.
examples.note: A hypothetical situation, with a conditional result.

contrast.es: Aunque parecía cansado, seguía trabajando.
contrast.en: Although he seemed tired, he kept working.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = he really did seem tired. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Por muy + adjective + que expresses 'however ... it may be' and takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Por muy simple que pareciera, funcionaba.
examples.en: However simple it seemed, it worked.
examples.note: Por muy + adjective + que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Por muy caro que fuera, lo compraría.
examples.en: However expensive it was, I'd buy it.
examples.note: A hypothetical concession, with a conditional result.

examples.es: Por muy tranquilo que pareciera, estaba nervioso.
examples.en: However calm he seemed, he was nervous.
examples.note: Por muy ... que keeps the subjunctive even when the speaker knows the facts.

contrast.es: Parecía muy tranquilo, pero estaba nervioso.
contrast.en: He seemed very calm, but he was nervous.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative. Por muy ... que concedes the point (subjunctive).

tricky: Parecer has no -zc- in the imperfect subjunctive: pareciera, parecieras, pareciéramos, parecieran, never 'parezciera'. Ser gives fuera / fuese, the same as ir. 'Me parecía que' takes the indicative but 'no me parecía que' takes the subjunctive.

title: haber

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que hubiera clase al día siguiente.
examples.en: It was possible there would be class the next day.
examples.note: Hay becomes hubiera in the imperfect subjunctive. It comes from hubieron, an irregular preterite stem.

examples.es: Era posible que ya hubieran llegado.
examples.en: It was possible that they had already arrived.
examples.note: Hubieran + participle = they had arrived. This is a compound form, so it is the earlier past.

examples.es: Era posible que hubiera veinte libros en la caja.
examples.en: It was possible there were twenty books in the box.
examples.note: Existential haber stays singular, even with plural nouns: hubiera, never 'hubieran'.

contrast.es: Sabía que había veinte libros en la caja.
contrast.en: I knew there were twenty books in the box.
contrast.note: Sabía que states a fact (indicative: había). Era posible que is a possibility (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely. Ojalá + hubiera + participle wishes the past had been different.

examples.es: Ojalá hubiera sol mañana.
examples.en: I wish there were sun tomorrow.
examples.note: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive suggests it seems unlikely.

examples.es: Ojalá hubieras dormido bien.
examples.en: I wish you had slept well.
examples.note: Hubieras + participle = a wish about the past that cannot be changed.

examples.es: Ojalá hubieran llegado ya a casa.
examples.en: I wish they had already got home.
examples.note: The speaker implies they haven't.

contrast.es: Ojalá hayan llegado ya a casa.
contrast.en: I hope they have already got home.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present perfect subjunctive = a real hope, still possible. Ojalá + hubieran = unlikely or contrary to fact.

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que en cuanto hubiera noticias, me avisaría.
examples.en: He said that as soon as there was news, he'd let me know.
examples.note: Future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Dijo que saldríamos en cuanto hubieras comido.
examples.en: He said we'd leave as soon as you had eaten.
examples.note: Hubieras + participle = completed before the main action.

examples.es: Prometió que en cuanto hubiera sitio, nos sentaríamos.
examples.en: He promised that as soon as there was room, we'd sit down.
examples.note: Sitio = room / a free place.

contrast.es: En cuanto hubo sitio, nos sentamos.
contrast.en: As soon as there was room, we sat down.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite hubo).

tricky: Haber is irregular: hubiera, hubieras, hubiéramos, hubieran (from hubieron), never 'haiga' or 'habiera'. The existential form stays singular: 'hubiera veinte libros'. Hubiera + participle is the pluperfect subjunctive, a compound tense, so those forms (hubieran llegado) are flagged separately from the simple imperfect.

title: tener

triggers.explanation: A reaction to something is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era una suerte que tuvieras tiempo.
examples.en: It was lucky that you had time.
examples.note: Tener's preterite is tuvieron, so tuvieras. The -g- of the present (tengas) is gone.

examples.es: Era una suerte que tuviéramos tan buenos vecinos.
examples.en: It was lucky that we had such good neighbours.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: tuviéramos.

examples.es: Era una suerte que no tuvieran hambre.
examples.en: It was lucky that they weren't hungry.
examples.note: Tener hambre = to be hungry.

contrast.es: Era cierto que no tenían hambre.
contrast.en: It was true that they weren't hungry.
contrast.note: Era cierto states a fact (indicative). Era una suerte reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A habitual or completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando tuviera hambre, comiera algo.
examples.en: He told me to eat something when I got hungry.
examples.note: The hunger hadn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Decidimos que cuando tuviéramos prisa, tomaríamos un taxi.
examples.en: We decided that when we were in a hurry, we'd take a taxi.
examples.note: Tener prisa = to be in a hurry.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando tuviera frío, le avisara.
examples.en: He told me to let him know when I felt cold.
examples.note: Tener frío = to feel cold.

contrast.es: Cuando tenías frío, me avisabas.
contrast.en: When you were cold, you told me.
contrast.note: A habitual past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: When the person you describe is unknown or not yet identified, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesitaba a alguien que tuviera paciencia.
examples.en: I needed someone who had patience.
examples.note: Alguien = unidentified, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesitaba a alguien que tuviera ganas de trabajar.
examples.en: I needed someone who felt like working.
examples.note: Tener ganas de = to feel like doing something.

examples.es: Necesitaba a alguien que tuviera coche.
examples.en: I needed someone who had a car.
examples.note: I didn't know whether such a person existed.

contrast.es: Conocía a alguien que tenía coche.
contrast.en: I knew someone who had a car.
contrast.note: A specific known person takes the indicative.

tricky: Tener keeps its irregular preterite stem, tuv-: tuviera, tuvieras, tuviéramos, tuvieran. The present -g- (tenga) does not carry over: never 'tengiera' or 'teniera'. The fixed tener expressions (tener hambre, frío, prisa, ganas) stay with tener.

title: hacer

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que hiciera calor al día siguiente.
examples.en: It was possible that it would be hot the next day.
examples.note: Hacer calor = to be hot (weather). The preterite stem is hic-, so hiciera.

examples.es: Era posible que no hiciéramos nada ese fin de semana.
examples.en: It was possible that we wouldn't do anything that weekend.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: hiciéramos.

examples.es: Era posible que hiciera frío esa noche.
examples.en: It was possible that it would be cold that night.
examples.note: Weather hacer stays singular.

contrast.es: Hacía frío esa noche.
contrast.en: It was cold that night.
