contrast.note: A plain fact takes the indicative. A possibility takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Insisting that someone else do something is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Insistía en que hicieras la tarea.
examples.en: I insisted that you do your homework.
examples.note: Hacer la tarea = to do homework.

examples.es: Insistía en que me hicieras caso.
examples.en: I insisted that you listen to me.
examples.note: Hacer caso = to pay attention to, to heed.

examples.es: Insistía en que lo hicieras tú mismo.
examples.en: I insisted that you do it yourself.
examples.note: Tú mismo adds emphasis.

contrast.es: Insistía en hacerlo yo mismo.
contrast.en: I insisted on doing it myself.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: En caso de que introduces a precaution against something that may happen, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llevé abrigo en caso de que hiciera frío.
examples.en: I took a coat in case it was cold.
examples.note: A precaution, so the imperfect subjunctive after a past main verb.

examples.es: Compré más en caso de que hiciéramos una fiesta.
examples.en: I bought more in case we had a party.
examples.note: Hacer una fiesta = to have a party.

examples.es: En caso de que hiciera mal tiempo, cancelaríamos.
examples.en: In case the weather was bad, we would cancel.
examples.note: Hacer mal tiempo = for the weather to be bad.

contrast.es: Como hacía mal tiempo, cancelamos.
contrast.en: Since the weather was bad, we cancelled.
contrast.note: A real, known fact takes the indicative.

tricky: Hacer's imperfect subjunctive is hiciera, hicieras, hiciéramos, hicieran (from hicieron), never 'hagiera' or 'haciera'. Don't confuse it with the preterite hizo (z), which only appears in the 3rd person singular. Weather hacer stays singular.

title: dar

triggers.explanation: Saying something was advisable is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Convenía que dieras las gracias.
examples.en: It was a good idea for you to say thank you.
examples.note: Dar's preterite is dieron, so dieras. Dar las gracias = to thank.

examples.es: Convenía que me dieras tu número.
examples.en: It was a good idea for you to give me your number.
examples.note: Dar is regular-looking here but takes -ier- endings (like a -er verb).

examples.es: Convenía que le diera tiempo a decidir.
examples.en: It was advisable to give him time to decide.
examples.note: Dar tiempo a = to give time to. There is no accent on diera, unlike the present dé.

contrast.es: Le di tiempo a decidir.
contrast.en: I gave him time to decide.
contrast.note: A real, completed action takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Indifference toward someone else's action is an emotional stance, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me daba igual que me dieran el puesto.
examples.en: I didn't care whether they gave me the job.
examples.note: Me daba igual que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me daba igual que te diera la razón.
examples.en: I didn't care if he agreed with you.
examples.note: Dar la razón = to agree that someone is right.

examples.es: Me daba igual que nos dieran una respuesta al día siguiente.
examples.en: I didn't mind if they gave us an answer the next day.
examples.note: The answer is something that may or may not happen.

contrast.es: Nos dieron una respuesta al día siguiente.
contrast.en: They gave us an answer the next day.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando me dieras tu número, te llamaría.
examples.en: I promised that when you gave me your number, I'd call you.
examples.note: The giving hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Pensaba que cuando le diera el regalo, se pondría contento.
examples.en: I thought that when I gave him the present, he'd be happy.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Sabía que cuando se diera cuenta, sería tarde.
examples.en: I knew that by the time he realised, it would be too late.
examples.note: Darse cuenta = to realise. Reflexive.

contrast.es: Cuando se dio cuenta, era tarde.
contrast.en: When he realised, it was too late.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Dar takes -er/-ir style endings in the preterite, so the imperfect subjunctive is diera, dieras, diéramos, dieran, never 'dara' or 'dé'. Unlike the present dé, diera has no accent, and only diéramos does (as every nosotros form). Don't mix up the forms: 'quiero que me dé' (present) vs 'quería que me diera' (imperfect).

title: poner

triggers.explanation: Saying something wasn't necessary is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era necesario que pusieras la mesa.
examples.en: It wasn't necessary for you to set the table.
examples.note: Poner's preterite is pusieron, so pusieras. The present -g- (pongas) is gone.

examples.es: No era necesario que te pusieras el abrigo.
examples.en: It wasn't necessary for you to put your coat on.
examples.note: Ponerse = to put on (clothing). Reflexive: te pusieras.

examples.es: No era necesario que se pusiera nervioso.
examples.en: It wasn't necessary for him to get nervous.
examples.note: Ponerse + adjective = to become. Keep the se.

contrast.es: Se puso nervioso sin motivo.
contrast.en: He got nervous for no reason.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite puso).

triggers.explanation: Annoyance at someone else's behaviour is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me daba rabia que pusieran la música tan alta.
examples.en: It annoyed me that they played the music so loud.
examples.note: Poner la música = to put the music on.

examples.es: Me daba rabia que me pusieran tantas pegas.
examples.en: It annoyed me that they raised so many objections.
examples.note: Poner pegas = to raise objections, to make difficulties.

examples.es: Me daba rabia que se pusiera a gritar por todo.
examples.en: It annoyed me that he started shouting about everything.
examples.note: Ponerse a + infinitive = to start doing something.

contrast.es: Veía que se ponía a gritar por todo.
contrast.en: I could see he started shouting about everything.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A habitual or completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te pidió que cuando pusieras la mesa, le avisaras.
examples.en: He asked you to let him know when you set the table.
examples.note: The table hadn't been set yet.

examples.es: Dijimos que cuando se pusiera el sol, volveríamos.
examples.en: We said that when the sun set, we'd go back.
examples.note: Ponerse = to set (of the sun).

examples.es: Me decía que cuando me pusiera nervioso, respirara hondo.
examples.en: He used to tell me to breathe deeply when I got nervous.
examples.note: Ponerse nervioso = to get nervous.

contrast.es: Cuando me ponía nervioso, respiraba hondo.
contrast.en: When I got nervous, I'd breathe deeply.
contrast.note: A habitual past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Poner's imperfect subjunctive is pusiera, pusieras, pusiéramos, pusieran (from pusieron), never 'pongiera' or 'poniera'. Don't drop the se for 'become': 'que se pusiera nervioso', not 'que pusiera nervioso'.

title: gustar

triggers.explanation: When the thing you are looking for is not yet identified, the relative clause takes the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Buscaba algo que le gustara a mi madre.
examples.en: I was looking for something my mother would like.
examples.note: Algo = not identified, so the subjunctive. Gustar agrees with the thing liked, and the person is the indirect object (le).

examples.es: Buscaba algo que les gustara a mis hijos.
examples.en: I was looking for something my children would like.
examples.note: Les refers to the children. The verb agrees with algo (singular): gustara, not 'gustaran'.

examples.es: Buscaba algo que gustara a todos.
examples.en: I was looking for something everyone would like.
examples.note: Without a pronoun, gustar a todos works the same way. The wanted item does not exist yet in the speaker's mind.

contrast.es: Encontré algo que les gustaba a todos.
contrast.en: I found something that everyone liked.
contrast.note: A thing that is known and real takes the indicative (gustaba). A thing still being sought takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Hoping something about someone else's reaction is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que te gustara la sorpresa.
examples.en: I hoped you would like the surprise.
examples.note: Esperaba que + imperfect subjunctive. La sorpresa is the subject, so gustara is singular.

examples.es: Esperaba que les gustasen las flores.
examples.en: I hoped they would like the flowers.
examples.note: This is the -se form, which is equivalent to gustaran. Las flores is plural, so the verb is plural.

examples.es: Esperaba que te gustara mi nuevo corte de pelo.
examples.en: I hoped you would like my new haircut.
examples.note: Corte de pelo is the singular subject.

contrast.es: Me dijiste que te gustaba mi nuevo corte de pelo.
contrast.en: You told me you liked my new haircut.
contrast.note: Reporting what someone said uses the indicative. Hoping uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque no me gustara, lo comería.
examples.en: Even if I didn't like it, I'd eat it.
examples.note: Hypothetical dislike, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Dijo que aunque no le gustaran los deportes, vendría con nosotros.
examples.en: He said that even if he didn't like sports, he'd come with us.
examples.note: Los deportes is plural, so gustaran.

examples.es: Te dije que aunque no te gustara el café, lo probaras.
examples.en: I told you that even if you didn't like coffee, you should try it.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: aunque (concession) and the reported request (probaras).

contrast.es: Aunque no te gustaba el café, lo probaste.
contrast.en: Although you didn't like coffee, you tried it.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = you really didn't like it. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Gustar agrees with the thing liked, not the person: 'que te gustara el libro' but 'que te gustaran los libros'. The imperfect subjunctive is gustara / gustase, regular. The -se form is equivalent, so gustaran = gustasen. Never use 'gustaba' after a trigger of wish or hope.

title: tomar

triggers.explanation: Recommending something is a wish about what someone else does, so the subjunctive. In the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Te recomendaba que tomaras un taxi.
examples.en: I recommended that you take a taxi.
examples.note: Tomar un taxi = to take a taxi. Regular: tomaras.

examples.es: Te recomendaba que tomaras una decisión pronto.
examples.en: I recommended that you make a decision soon.
examples.note: Tomar una decisión = to make a decision, never 'hacer una decisión'.

examples.es: Te recomendaba que tomaras esta medicina antes de comer.
examples.en: I recommended that you take this medicine before eating.
examples.note: Tomar a medicine = to take it. Comer is an infinitive because antes de has the same subject.

contrast.es: Sabía que tomabas esta medicina antes de comer.
contrast.en: I knew you took this medicine before eating.
contrast.note: Knowing a fact takes the indicative. Recommending takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te di dinero para que tomaras un taxi.
examples.en: I gave you money so you could take a taxi.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú), so para que.

examples.es: Te llamé para que tomáramos un café.
examples.en: I called you so that we could have a coffee.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: tomáramos. Tomar un café = to have a coffee.

examples.es: Les di una semana para que tomaran una decisión.
examples.en: I gave them a week so that they could make a decision.
examples.note: A different subject (ellos) makes the decision.

contrast.es: Tomaron una decisión en una semana.
contrast.en: They made a decision within a week.
contrast.note: A plain completed fact uses the indicative (preterite). Para que gives the purpose (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que tomara café.
examples.en: I didn't think he drank coffee.
examples.note: Tomar café = to drink coffee. No creía que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que tomaran la decisión ese día.
examples.en: I didn't think they would make the decision that day.
examples.note: Doubt about a future event, seen from the past.

examples.es: No creía que tomara el autobús para ir al trabajo.
examples.en: I didn't think she took the bus to get to work.
examples.note: Tomar el autobús = to take the bus.

contrast.es: Creía que tomaba el autobús para ir al trabajo.
contrast.en: I thought she took the bus to get to work.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Tomar is regular in this tense (tomara, tomaras, tomáramos, tomaran), so the catches are in the meaning. It covers drink, eat, take transport and decisions: 'que tomaras una decisión', never 'hicieras una decisión'. Nosotros takes an accent: tomáramos. Don't confuse it with the present tomemos.

title: coger

triggers.explanation: Suggesting something is a wish about what someone else does, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Sugería que cogieras el tren.
examples.en: I suggested that you take the train.
examples.note: The g→j change of the present (cojas) does not carry over: cogieras, never 'cojieras'.

examples.es: Sugería que cogiéramos un atajo.
examples.en: I suggested that we take a shortcut.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: cogiéramos. Coger un atajo = to take a shortcut.

examples.es: Sugería que cogieras un taxi en vez de esperar al autobús.
examples.en: I suggested that you take a taxi instead of waiting for the bus.
examples.note: En vez de + infinitive: the waiting has the same subject as the suggestion's target (tú).

contrast.es: Me dijo que cogías un taxi todos los días.
contrast.en: He told me you took a taxi every day.
contrast.note: Reporting a fact takes the indicative. Suggesting takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Después de que about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te pidió que después de que cogieras las llaves, cerraras la puerta.
examples.en: He asked you to close the door after you picked up the keys.
examples.note: The picking up hadn't happened yet. Coger las llaves = to pick up the keys.

examples.es: Dije que después de que cogiera el autobús, te llamaría.
examples.en: I said that after I took the bus, I'd call you.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Decidí que después de que cogiera las vacaciones, empezaría a estudiar.
examples.en: I decided that after I took my holiday, I'd start studying.
examples.note: Coger las vacaciones = to take a holiday. The holiday was still ahead.

contrast.es: Después de que cogí las vacaciones, empecé a estudiar.
contrast.en: After I took my holiday, I started studying.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que cogiera el autobús.
examples.en: It was possible that he would take the bus.
examples.note: Era posible que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que cogiéramos el último tren.
examples.en: It was possible that we would catch the last train.
examples.note: Coger un tren = to catch a train.

examples.es: Era posible que cogieras frío sin abrigo.
examples.en: It was possible that you would catch a chill without a coat.
examples.note: Coger frío = to catch a chill.

contrast.es: Cogiste frío sin abrigo.
contrast.en: You caught a chill without a coat.
contrast.note: A real event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Coger has no g→j change in the imperfect subjunctive: cogiera, cogieras, cogiéramos, cogieran, never 'cojiera' (the present coja does not carry over). The real catch is regional: in Spain coger is everyday and innocent, but in much of Latin America it is vulgar. In that case learners should use tomar, agarrar or other verbs.

title: entrar

triggers.explanation: Forbidding something is a wish about what someone else does, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prohibía que entraras en mi cuarto.
examples.en: I forbade you to go into my room.
examples.note: Entrar en = to go into (Spain). Regular: entraras.

examples.es: Prohibía que entraran sin llamar.
examples.en: I forbade them to come in without knocking.
examples.note: Sin llamar is an infinitive because the knocking has the same subject (ellos).

examples.es: Prohibía que entraras en mi cuarto, aunque yo no estuviera.
examples.en: I forbade you to enter my room, even if I wasn't there.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the prohibition and the hypothetical aunque yo no estuviera.

contrast.es: Te prohibía entrar en mi cuarto.
contrast.en: I forbade you to enter my room.
contrast.note: Prohibir can take an infinitive when the person is an indirect object (te prohibía entrar), or que + subjunctive (prohibía que entraras). Both mean the same.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Abrí la puerta para que entrara el aire.
examples.en: I opened the door so the air could come in.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / el aire), so para que.

examples.es: Dejé la llave para que entraras en casa.
examples.en: I left the key so you could get into the house.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Te esperé para que entráramos juntos.
examples.en: I waited for you so that we would go in together.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: entráramos.

contrast.es: Esperé para entrar contigo.
contrast.en: I waited to go in with you.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Surprise is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me extrañaba que no entraran.
examples.en: It surprised me that they didn't come in.
examples.note: Me extrañaba que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me extrañaba que entraras sin llamar.
examples.en: It surprised me that you walked in without knocking.
examples.note: Entrar sin llamar = to walk in without knocking.

examples.es: Me extrañaba que entraran en la reunión sin invitación.
examples.en: It surprised me that they came into the meeting without an invitation.
examples.note: Sin invitación = without an invitation.

contrast.es: Vi que entraban en la reunión sin invitación.
contrast.en: I saw that they came into the meeting without an invitation.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Entrar is regular: entrara, entraras, entráramos, entraran. The catch is the preposition: entrar en is standard in Spain and entrar a is common in Latin America. Never 'entrar la casa' without one. 'Que entraras' is a different subject, so it needs the subjunctive. Same subject means an infinitive.

title: subir vs bajar

triggers.explanation: Saying something was unnecessary is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hacía falta que subieras la maleta.
examples.en: You didn't need to carry the suitcase up.
examples.note: Subir takes -ier- endings: subieras (from subieron).

examples.es: No hacía falta que bajáramos todavía.
examples.en: We didn't need to go down yet.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: bajáramos.

examples.es: No hacía falta que bajaras la música.
examples.en: You didn't need to turn the music down.
examples.note: Bajar la música = to turn down the music. Bajar + noun = to lower or carry down.

contrast.es: Bajaste la música.
contrast.en: You turned the music down.
contrast.note: A real, completed action takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era probable que subieran los precios.
examples.en: It was likely that prices would go up.
examples.note: Subir = to go up. Plural subject: los precios.

examples.es: Era probable que bajara la temperatura.
examples.en: It was likely that the temperature would drop.
examples.note: Bajar = to go down, to drop.

examples.es: Era probable que subieran el sueldo en enero.
examples.en: It was likely that they would raise the salary in January.
examples.note: Subir el sueldo = to raise the salary. The subject is an unnamed 'they'.

contrast.es: Estaba seguro de que subirían el sueldo en enero.
contrast.en: I was sure they would raise the salary in January.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Likelihood uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet happened, from a past viewpoint, takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me dijo que esperara hasta que subiera el ascensor.
examples.en: He told me to wait until the lift came up.
examples.note: The lift hadn't arrived yet.

examples.es: El médico dijo que no salieras hasta que bajara la fiebre.
examples.en: The doctor said not to go out until your fever went down.
examples.note: Bajar la fiebre = for a fever to go down. Fiebre is the subject.

examples.es: Me dijo que esperara en el coche hasta que subiera mi hermano.
examples.en: He told me to wait in the car until my brother got in.
examples.note: Subir al coche = to get into a car. Subir a for vehicles.

contrast.es: Esperé en el coche hasta que subió mi hermano.
contrast.en: I waited in the car until my brother got in.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Subir and bajar are regular in this tense: subiera (from subieron), bajara. The catches are the prepositions: subir a / bajar de for vehicles ('que subieras al tren', 'que bajaras del tren'), and when carrying things they take a direct object: subir la maleta. Nosotros takes an accent: bajáramos, subiéramos.

title: tirar vs sacar

triggers.explanation: Pleading for someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te rogué que tiraras la basura.
examples.en: I asked you to throw out the rubbish.
examples.note: Tirar la basura = to put out the rubbish. Regular: tiraras.

examples.es: Te rogué que sacaras al perro.
examples.en: I asked you to take the dog out.
examples.note: Sacar al perro = to take the dog out. The c→qu of the present (saques) does not apply: sacaras.

examples.es: Te rogué que no tiraras esos papeles.
examples.en: I asked you not to throw those papers away.
examples.note: Negative requests keep the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Vi que tirabas esos papeles.
contrast.en: I saw that you were throwing those papers away.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. A request uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Saying it was time for someone to act is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era hora de que tiraras esos zapatos.
examples.en: It was time for you to throw those shoes out.
examples.note: Era hora de que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era hora de que sacaras el carné de conducir.
examples.en: It was time for you to get your driving licence.
examples.note: Sacar el carné = to get a licence.

examples.es: Era hora de que sacáramos conclusiones.
examples.en: It was time for us to draw conclusions.
examples.note: Sacar conclusiones = to draw conclusions. Nosotros takes an accent: sacáramos.

contrast.es: Era hora de sacar conclusiones.
contrast.en: It was time to draw conclusions.
contrast.note: No specific subject = infinitive. A specific subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Una vez que about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Te dijo que una vez que tiraras la basura, fueras con él.
examples.en: He told you that once you'd thrown out the rubbish, you should go with him.
examples.note: The rubbish hadn't been thrown yet.

examples.es: Te dijeron que una vez que sacaras el billete, esperaras aquí.
examples.en: They told you that once you'd got your ticket, you should wait here.
examples.note: Sacar el billete = to get a ticket.

examples.es: Prometí que una vez que sacáramos las entradas, te avisaría.
examples.en: I promised that once we'd got the tickets, I'd let you know.
examples.note: Sacar las entradas = to get the tickets.

contrast.es: Una vez que sacamos las entradas, te avisé.
contrast.en: Once we'd got the tickets, I let you know.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Tirar and sacar are regular in this tense: tirara, sacara. The c→qu of the present (saque, saques) does not carry over, so never 'saquara'. Tirar has many meanings: throw, pull, throw away, waste. Remember tirar la basura = put it in the bin, while sacar la basura = take it out to the street.

title: echar

triggers.explanation: Calling something natural is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era natural que echaras de menos a tu familia.
examples.en: It was natural that you missed your family.
examples.note: Echar de menos = to miss (Spain). Regular: echaras.

examples.es: Era natural que se echaran a reír.
examples.en: It was natural that they burst out laughing.
examples.note: Echarse a + infinitive = to burst out doing something.

examples.es: Era natural que te echara de menos.
examples.en: It was natural that he missed you.
examples.note: Echar de menos + a person: te is the object.

contrast.es: Era evidente que te echaba de menos.
contrast.en: It was obvious that he missed you.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era natural gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Lo puse en la nevera para que no se echara a perder.
examples.en: I put it in the fridge so it wouldn't go off.
examples.note: Echarse a perder = to go off, to spoil.

examples.es: Te di el informe para que le echaras un vistazo.
examples.en: I gave you the report so you could have a look at it.
examples.note: Echar un vistazo = to take a look.

examples.es: Te lo dejé para que me echaras una mano.
examples.en: I left it with you so that you'd give me a hand.
examples.note: Echar una mano = to lend a hand. Different subjects (yo / tú).

contrast.es: Me echaste una mano.
contrast.en: You gave me a hand.
contrast.note: A real, completed action takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dije que en cuanto echara la carta, volvería.
examples.en: I said that as soon as I posted the letter, I'd come back.
examples.note: Echar una carta = to post a letter.

examples.es: Me dijeron que en cuanto echara azúcar, lo removiera.
examples.en: They told me to stir it as soon as I added sugar.
examples.note: Echar azúcar = to add sugar.

examples.es: Dije que en cuanto lo echara de menos, lo llamaría.
examples.en: I said that as soon as I missed him, I'd call him.
examples.note: A future feeling from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: En cuanto lo eché de menos, lo llamé.
contrast.en: As soon as I missed him, I called him.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Echar is regular (echara, echaras, echáramos, echaran) but sits inside lots of fixed expressions: echar de menos (Spain; extrañar in Latin America), echar una mano (help), echar un vistazo (take a look), echarse a perder (spoil). The meaning is in the expression, so the translation is not word for word.

title: caer

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Podía ser que cayera una tormenta esa tarde.
examples.en: A storm might hit that afternoon.
examples.note: Caer's preterite is cayeron, with a y: cayera, never 'cayiera' or 'caigiera'.

examples.es: Podía ser que cayéramos en la trampa.
examples.en: We might fall into the trap.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: cayéramos. Caer en la trampa = to fall into the trap.

examples.es: Podía ser que te cayera bien mi hermano.
examples.en: You might like my brother.
examples.note: Caer bien = to make a good impression. It works like gustar: the subject is mi hermano.

contrast.es: Te cayó bien mi hermano.
contrast.en: You liked my brother.
contrast.note: A real event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Sadness is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me daba pena que cayeras enfermo.
examples.en: It saddened me that you fell ill.
examples.note: Caer enfermo = to fall ill.

examples.es: Me daba pena que le cayera mal a tanta gente.
examples.en: It saddened me that so many people didn't like him.
examples.note: Caer mal a = to make a bad impression on. The subject is the one who is disliked.

examples.es: Me daba pena que no te cayera bien mi hermano.
examples.en: It saddened me that you didn't like my brother.
examples.note: Mi hermano is the subject of cayera.

contrast.es: Veía que no te caía bien mi hermano.
contrast.en: I could see you didn't like my brother.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Sujeté la escalera para que no me cayera.
examples.en: I held the ladder so that I wouldn't fall.
examples.note: Caerse is reflexive when someone falls over: me cayera.

examples.es: Até los libros para que no se cayeran.
examples.en: I tied the books together so they wouldn't fall.
examples.note: Plural subject: los libros.

examples.es: Te agarré bien para que no te cayeras.
examples.en: I held you tight so that you wouldn't fall.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

contrast.es: Te agarré bien y no te caíste.
contrast.en: I held you tight and you didn't fall.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Caer has a y in the imperfect subjunctive: cayera, cayeras, cayéramos, cayeran (from cayeron), never 'caiga' (present) or 'cayiera'. 'Me caía bien' is about impressions and works like gustar: 'que te cayera bien'. Caerse (to fall over) needs the reflexive: 'que no te cayeras'.

title: sentar vs sentarse

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to do something is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que te sentaras a mi lado.
examples.en: I wanted you to sit next to me.
examples.note: The e→ie of the present (te sientes) is gone: sentaras, never 'sientaras'.

examples.es: Quería que se sentaran en silencio.
examples.en: I wanted them to sit down in silence.
examples.note: Reflexive plural: se sentaran.

examples.es: Quería que te sentaras aquí, junto a la ventana.
examples.en: I wanted you to sit here, next to the window.
examples.note: Junto a = next to.

contrast.es: Quería sentarme junto a la ventana.
contrast.en: I wanted to sit next to the window.
contrast.note: Same subject = infinitive. A different subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando me sentara, abriera el libro.
examples.en: He told me to open my book when I sat down.
examples.note: The sitting down hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Dijo que cuando se sentaran todos, empezaríamos.
examples.en: He said that when everybody had sat down, we'd start.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so sentaran.

examples.es: Te prometí que cuando te sentaras, verías mejor.
examples.en: I promised you that when you sat down, you'd see better.
examples.note: A promise about the future, from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando te sentaste, viste mejor.
contrast.en: When you sat down, you saw better.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Dejé la silla libre para que te sentaras.
examples.en: I left the chair free so you could sit down.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Moví el bolso para que se sentara la señora.
examples.en: I moved the bag so the lady could sit down.
examples.note: La señora is the subject, so sentara is singular.

examples.es: Puse más sillas para que se sentaran todos.
examples.en: I put out more chairs so that everyone could sit down.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so sentaran.

contrast.es: Puse más sillas y se sentaron todos.
contrast.en: I put out more chairs and everyone sat down.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Sentarse has no stem change in the imperfect subjunctive: me sentara, te sentaras, nos sentáramos, se sentaran, never 'sientara'. The present trap is gone ('te sientes' could be sentarse or sentirse), but the reflexive still matters: sentar = to seat someone, sentarse = to sit down.

title: seguir

triggers.explanation: Saying something was necessary is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hacía falta que siguieras las instrucciones.
examples.en: You needed to follow the instructions.
examples.note: Seguir keeps its e→i stem (from siguieron): siguieras, never 'seguieras'.

examples.es: Hacía falta que siguiéramos adelante.
examples.en: We needed to keep going.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: siguiéramos. Seguir adelante = to carry on.

examples.es: Hacía falta que siguieras estudiando para aprobar.
examples.en: You needed to keep studying to pass.
examples.note: Seguir + gerund = to keep doing something.

contrast.es: Hacía falta seguir estudiando para aprobar.
contrast.en: It was necessary to keep studying to pass.
contrast.note: No specific subject = infinitive. A specific subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Doubt calls for the subjunctive, so after a past verb it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que siguiera lloviendo al día siguiente.
examples.en: I doubted it would still be raining the next day.
examples.note: Seguir + gerund: siguiera lloviendo.

examples.es: Dudaba que siguieran trabajando allí.
examples.en: I doubted they were still working there.
examples.note: Plural subject: siguieran.

examples.es: Dudaba que siguiera vivo.
examples.en: I doubted he was still alive.
examples.note: Seguir + adjective = to still be.

contrast.es: Sabía que seguía vivo.
contrast.en: I knew he was still alive.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Dudaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque siguiera lloviendo, saldríamos.
examples.en: Even if it was still raining, we'd go out.
examples.note: Hypothetical situation, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Te dije que aunque siguieras enfadado, vinieras a la cena.
examples.en: I told you that even if you were still angry, you should come to the dinner.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: aunque and the reported request.

examples.es: Aunque siguiese sin entenderlo, lo intentaría.
examples.en: Even if I still didn't understand it, I'd try.
examples.note: This is the -se form, equivalent to siguiera. Seguir sin + infinitive = to still not do something.

contrast.es: Aunque seguía sin entenderlo, lo intenté.
contrast.en: Although I still didn't understand it, I tried.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Seguir keeps its e→i stem in every imperfect subjunctive form: siguiera, siguieras, siguiéramos, siguieran (from siguieron), never 'seguiera'. The u stays, as in the infinitive. Seguir + gerund = keep doing, seguir + adjective = still be, seguir sin + infinitive = still not be doing.

title: esperar

triggers.explanation: Saying what was better is an evaluation, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era preferible que esperaras en el coche.
examples.en: It was better that you waited in the car.
examples.note: Esperar = to wait. Regular: esperaras.

examples.es: Era preferible que esperáramos a mañana.
examples.en: It was better that we waited until tomorrow.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: esperáramos. Esperar a = to wait until.

examples.es: Era preferible que no esperaras nada de ellos.
examples.en: It was better that you didn't expect anything from them.
examples.note: Esperar = to expect. The same verb covers wait, hope and expect.

contrast.es: Sabía que no esperabas nada de ellos.
contrast.en: I knew you didn't expect anything from them.
contrast.note: Knowing a fact takes the indicative. A judgement of what is better takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pedí que esperaras aquí.
examples.en: I asked you to wait here.
examples.note: Pedir que + imperfect subjunctive, because the request is in the past.

examples.es: Te pedí que esperáramos juntos.
examples.en: I asked you that we wait together.
examples.note: Nosotros: esperáramos, with an accent.

examples.es: Te pedí que no esperaras un milagro.
examples.en: I asked you not to expect a miracle.
examples.note: Negative request, so the subjunctive stays.

contrast.es: Esperabas un milagro.
contrast.en: You were expecting a miracle.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative (esperabas).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed or habitual past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Mi abuela me decía que cuando esperara el autobús, usara el banco.
examples.en: My grandmother used to tell me to use the bench when I waited for the bus.
examples.note: The waiting hadn't happened yet, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Pensábamos que cuando esperáramos los resultados, estaríamos nerviosos.
examples.en: We thought that when we waited for the results, we'd be nervous.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint, with a conditional result.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando esperara un hijo, todo cambiaría.
examples.en: He told me that when I was expecting a baby, everything would change.
examples.note: Esperar un hijo = to be expecting a baby.

contrast.es: Cuando esperaba a mi hijo, todo cambió.
contrast.en: When I was expecting my son, everything changed.
contrast.note: A real past situation takes the indicative. A future event seen from the past takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Esperar is regular in this tense: esperara, esperaras, esperáramos, esperaran. It has two meanings, wait and hope or expect. 'Esperaba que' (I hoped) takes the subjunctive, and 'esperar a que' (wait until) also does: 'esperé a que llegaras'. Without que, esperar + infinitive keeps the same subject.

title: conseguir

triggers.explanation: Wishing for someone else's success is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Deseaba que consiguieras el trabajo.
examples.en: I hoped you would get the job.
examples.note: The e→i of conseguir stays in the imperfect subjunctive (from consiguieron): consiguieras.

examples.es: Deseaba que consiguiéramos un buen precio.
examples.en: I hoped we would get a good price.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: consiguiéramos.

examples.es: Deseaba que consiguieras aprobar el examen.
examples.en: I hoped you would manage to pass the exam.
examples.note: Conseguir + infinitive = to manage to do something.

contrast.es: Sabía que conseguías aprobar los exámenes.
contrast.en: I knew you managed to pass your exams.
contrast.note: Knowing a fact takes the indicative. Wishing takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: When something isn't certain, the subjunctive is used.

examples.es: No era seguro que consiguiera entradas.
examples.en: It wasn't certain that I'd get tickets.
examples.note: No era seguro que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No era seguro que consiguieran el permiso.
examples.en: It wasn't certain that they'd get the permit.
examples.note: Plural subject: consiguieran.

examples.es: No era seguro que consiguiéramos llegar a tiempo.
examples.en: It wasn't certain that we'd manage to arrive on time.
examples.note: Conseguir + infinitive says you succeed, unlike poder.

contrast.es: Estaba seguro de que conseguiríamos llegar a tiempo.
contrast.en: I was sure we'd manage to arrive on time.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Uncertainty uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hacía todo para que consiguieras tus sueños.
examples.en: I did everything so that you would achieve your dreams.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Te ayudé para que consiguieras el puesto.
examples.en: I helped you so that you'd get the position.
examples.note: Conseguir un puesto = to get a post.

examples.es: Trabajaba para que consiguiéramos la casa.
examples.en: I worked so that we could get the house.
examples.note: The subject changes from yo to nosotros.

contrast.es: Trabajaba para conseguir la casa.
contrast.en: I worked to get the house.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + imperfect subjunctive.

tricky: Conseguir keeps its e→i in the imperfect subjunctive: consiguiera, consiguieras, consiguiéramos, consiguieran (from consiguieron). The u stays, as in the infinitive, never 'conseguiera'. Conseguir + infinitive means manage to, so it says you succeeded, unlike poder: 'conseguí hacerlo' vs 'pude hacerlo'.

title: crear vs creer

triggers.explanation: Calling something essential is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era fundamental que crearas buenos hábitos.
examples.en: It was essential that you created good habits.
examples.note: Crear = to create. Regular: crearas.

examples.es: Era fundamental que creyeran en sí mismos.
examples.en: It was essential that they believed in themselves.
examples.note: Creer takes a y (from creyeron): creyeran, never 'creieran'.

examples.es: Era fundamental que creyeras en tu proyecto.
examples.en: It was essential that you believed in your project.
examples.note: Creer en = to believe in.

contrast.es: Era evidente que creías en tu proyecto.
contrast.en: It was obvious that you believed in your project.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era fundamental gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Saying something was unlikely is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era probable que creara problemas.
examples.en: It was unlikely that he would create problems.
examples.note: Crear: creara. Different from creyera (creer).

examples.es: No era probable que creyera esa historia.
examples.en: It was unlikely that he would believe that story.
examples.note: Creer + direct object = to believe something.

examples.es: No era probable que ella creara una empresa ese año.
examples.en: It was unlikely that she would start a company that year.
examples.note: Crear una empresa = to set up a company.

contrast.es: Era seguro que ella crearía una empresa ese año.
contrast.en: It was certain that she would start a company that year.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional here (a future from the past). Unlikelihood uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando creara el archivo, lo guardara.
examples.en: He told me to save the file when I created it.
examples.note: The creating hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Te prometí que cuando creyeras en ti mismo, todo cambiaría.
examples.en: I promised you that when you believed in yourself, everything would change.
examples.note: Creer en uno mismo = to believe in yourself.

examples.es: Dije que cuando creara la cuenta, te mandaría la contraseña.
examples.en: I said that when I created the account, I'd send you the password.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando creé la cuenta, te mandé la contraseña.
contrast.en: When I created the account, I sent you the password.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Crear is creara (regular), but creer has a y: creyera, creyeras, creyéramos, creyeran (from creyeron). The two verbs are now different in the middle: 'quería que crearas' (create) vs 'quería que creyeras' (believe). Never 'creiera'. Notice that the present-tense swap of vowels (cree / crea) does not happen here.

title: quedar vs quedarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá me quedara tiempo.
examples.en: I wish I had some time left.
examples.note: Quedar = to be left over. It works like gustar: the subject is tiempo.

examples.es: Ojalá te quedaras en Madrid un año más.
examples.en: I wish you would stay in Madrid another year.
examples.note: Quedarse = to stay. The speaker thinks it is unlikely.

examples.es: Ojalá nos quedaran entradas.
examples.en: I wish there were tickets left for us.
examples.note: Entradas is plural, so quedaran.

contrast.es: Ojalá nos queden entradas.
contrast.en: I hope there are tickets left for us.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te llamé para que quedáramos.
examples.en: I called you so that we would arrange to meet.
examples.note: Quedar = to arrange to meet. Nosotros takes an accent.

examples.es: Guardé un trozo para que me quedara algo.
examples.en: I saved a piece so that I would have something left.
examples.note: Algo is the subject of quedara.

examples.es: Te compré la talla grande para que te quedara bien.
examples.en: I bought you the large size so that it would fit you well.
examples.note: Quedar bien = to fit well. The subject is the garment.

contrast.es: Te compré la talla grande y te quedó bien.
contrast.en: I bought you the large size and it fit you well.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Dijimos que cuando quedáramos, te contaría todo.
examples.en: We said that when we met up, I'd tell you everything.
examples.note: The meeting hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te quedaras sin gasolina, me avisaras.
examples.en: I told you to let me know when you ran out of petrol.
examples.note: Quedarse sin = to run out of.

examples.es: Sabía que cuando se quedara solo, lloraría.
examples.en: I knew that when he was left alone, he'd cry.
examples.note: Quedarse solo = to be left alone.

contrast.es: Cuando se quedó solo, lloró.
contrast.en: When he was left alone, he cried.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Quedar and quedarse are both regular: quedara, quedaras, quedáramos, quedaran. The -se changes the meaning: 'que quedáramos' (that we arrange to meet) vs 'que nos quedáramos' (that we stay). Quedar alone also means to be left or to fit, and works like gustar: 'me quedaban dos'.

title: volverse vs hacerse (become)

triggers.explanation: Worry is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me preocupaba que te volvieras cínico.
examples.en: I was worried you would become cynical.
examples.note: Volverse + adjective = to turn, to become. No o→ue change: volvieras.

examples.es: Me preocupaba que se hiciera tarde.
examples.en: I was worried it was getting late.
examples.note: Hacerse tarde = to get late. Hacer's stem is hic-: hiciera.

examples.es: Me preocupaba que se volviera loco.
examples.en: I was worried he would go mad.
examples.note: Volverse loco = to go mad. It is a deeper, often unwelcome change.

contrast.es: Veía que se volvía loco.
contrast.en: I could see he was going mad.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te decía que cuando te hicieras mayor, lo entenderías.
examples.en: I used to tell you that when you grew up, you'd understand.
examples.note: Hacerse mayor = to grow up.

examples.es: Pensé que cuando se volviera loco, nadie podría pararlo.
examples.en: I thought that when he went mad, nobody would be able to stop him.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint, with a conditional result.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te hicieras rico, no te olvidaras de mí.
examples.en: I told you that when you got rich, you shouldn't forget me.
examples.note: Hacerse rico = to get rich, by effort.

contrast.es: Cuando te hiciste rico, te olvidaste de mí.
contrast.en: When you got rich, you forgot about me.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque me hiciera rico, seguiría aquí.
examples.en: Even if I got rich, I'd stay here.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque se volviera famoso, no cambiaría.
examples.en: Even if he became famous, he wouldn't change.
examples.note: Volverse famoso = to become famous.

examples.es: Aunque se hiciera vegetariano, seguiría comiendo queso.
examples.en: Even if he became vegetarian, he'd keep eating cheese.
examples.note: Hacerse vegetariano = to become vegetarian by choice.

contrast.es: Aunque se hizo vegetariano, siguió comiendo queso.
contrast.en: Although he became vegetarian, he kept eating cheese.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real event. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Hacerse is a change you drive (se hiciera rico, médico, vegetariano), and volverse is a deeper, often unwelcome change (se volviera loco, cínico). Both need the reflexive: 'que te hicieras', 'que te volvieras'. Hacer is irregular (hiciera, from hicieron) and volver loses its o→ue (volviera, never 'vuelviera').

title: dejar de vs parar

triggers.explanation: Calling something essential is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era imprescindible que dejaras de fumar.
examples.en: It was essential that you quit smoking.
examples.note: Dejar de + infinitive = to quit. Keep the de.

examples.es: Era imprescindible que pararas un momento.
examples.en: It was essential that you stopped for a moment.
examples.note: Parar = to stop (often just for now).

examples.es: Era imprescindible que pararas de correr un momento para recuperar el aliento.
examples.en: It was essential that you stopped running for a moment to catch your breath.
examples.note: Parar de + infinitive = to stop doing. Para recuperar is an infinitive because the subject is the same.

contrast.es: Era imprescindible parar de correr un momento.
contrast.en: It was essential to stop running for a moment.
contrast.note: No specific subject = infinitive. A specific subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Dije que cuando dejaras de llorar, hablaríamos.
examples.en: I said that when you stopped crying, we'd talk.
examples.note: The crying hadn't stopped yet.

examples.es: Decidimos que cuando parara de llover, saldríamos.
examples.en: We decided that when it stopped raining, we'd go out.
examples.note: Parar de llover = to stop raining.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando dejara de fumar, me sentiría mejor.
examples.en: I promised that when I quit smoking, I'd feel better.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando dejé de fumar, me sentí mejor.
contrast.en: When I quit smoking, I felt better.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te lo dije para que dejaras de preocuparte.
examples.en: I told you so that you'd stop worrying.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Le di el biberón para que parara de llorar.
examples.en: I gave him the bottle so that he'd stop crying.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Se lo expliqué para que dejáramos de discutir.
examples.en: I explained it to him so that we would stop arguing.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: dejáramos.

contrast.es: Se lo expliqué y dejamos de discutir.
contrast.en: I explained it to him and we stopped arguing.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Dejar de + infinitive means to quit, while parar de means to stop (often just for now). Both are regular: dejara, parara. Keep the de: 'que dejaras de fumar', because 'que dejaras fumar' would not mean quit. Nosotros takes an accent: dejáramos, paráramos.

title: acabar vs terminar

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Lo hice antes de que acabara el día.
examples.en: I did it before the day ended.
examples.note: Antes de que + imperfect subjunctive after a past main verb.

examples.es: Salimos antes de que terminara la película.
examples.en: We left before the film ended.
examples.note: The film hadn't ended when we left.

examples.es: Quería llegar antes de que terminara la película, pero había tráfico.
examples.en: I wanted to get there before the film ended, but there was traffic.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / la película), so antes de que.

contrast.es: Llegué después de que terminó la película.
contrast.en: I arrived after the film ended.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Hoping something happens is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que terminaras pronto.
examples.en: I hoped you would finish soon.
examples.note: Esperaba que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que acabáramos esto ese día.
examples.en: I hoped we would finish this that day.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: acabáramos.

examples.es: Esperaba que no acabara mal esa historia.
examples.en: I hoped that story wouldn't end badly.
examples.note: Acabar mal = to end badly. The subject is esa historia.

contrast.es: Sabía que esa historia acabaría mal.
contrast.en: I knew that story would end badly.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Hope uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses uncertainty. In a past context, the imperfect subjunctive marks stronger doubt than the indicative.

examples.es: Quizás terminara antes de lo previsto.
examples.en: Maybe he finished earlier than planned.
examples.note: Quizás + imperfect subjunctive = doubt about something in the past.

examples.es: Quizás acabáramos tarde aquella noche, no lo recuerdo.
examples.en: Maybe we finished late that night; I don't remember.
examples.note: The speaker really isn't sure.

examples.es: Quizás acabara en la cárcel, nadie lo supo nunca.
examples.en: Maybe he ended up in jail; nobody ever knew.
examples.note: Acabar en = to end up in.

contrast.es: Quizás acabó en la cárcel.
contrast.en: Maybe he ended up in jail.
contrast.note: Quizás + indicative is also possible and sounds more confident. The subjunctive signals more doubt.

tricky: Acabar and terminar are both regular (acabara, terminara). The catches are the patterns: acabar de + infinitive means 'just did' (acababa de comer), acabar + gerund means to end up (acabé durmiendo), and acabar con means to put an end to. Terminar de + infinitive is simply to finish doing. Nosotros takes an accent: acabáramos, termináramos.

title: soler vs acostumbrarse

triggers.explanation: Doubt calls for the subjunctive, so after a past verb it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que soliera llegar tarde.
examples.en: I doubted he usually arrived late.
examples.note: Soler is defective, and soliera is rare. Soler + infinitive = to usually do. No o→ue: soliera, never 'sueliera'.

examples.es: Dudaba que solieran salir a cenar.
examples.en: I doubted they usually went out for dinner.
examples.note: Plural subject: solieran.

examples.es: Dudaba que soliera ir al gimnasio.
examples.en: I doubted he usually went to the gym.
examples.note: Doubting a habit.

contrast.es: Sabía que solía ir al gimnasio.
contrast.en: I knew he usually went to the gym.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative (solía). Dudaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something good is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era bueno que te acostumbraras al frío.
examples.en: It was good that you got used to the cold.
examples.note: Acostumbrarse a = to get used to. Regular: acostumbraras.

examples.es: Era bueno que nos acostumbrásemos a madrugar.
examples.en: It was good that we got used to getting up early.
examples.note: This is the -se form, equivalent to acostumbráramos. Nosotros takes an accent.

examples.es: Era bueno que se acostumbraran a vivir solos.
examples.en: It was good that they got used to living alone.
examples.note: Acostumbrarse a + infinitive.

contrast.es: Era evidente que se acostumbraban a vivir solos.
contrast.en: It was obvious that they were getting used to living alone.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era bueno gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque me acostumbrara al ruido, preferiría el silencio.
examples.en: Even if I got used to the noise, I'd prefer silence.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque no te acostumbraras, tendrías que seguir.
examples.en: Even if you didn't get used to it, you'd have to carry on.
examples.note: A hypothetical situation.

examples.es: Aunque soliera salir temprano, aquel día se quedaría.
examples.en: Even if he usually left early, that day he'd stay.
examples.note: Soler + infinitive. Soliera is rare in speech.

contrast.es: Aunque solía salir temprano, se quedó.
contrast.en: Although he usually left early, he stayed.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Soler is defective: it has no future or conditional, and the imperfect subjunctive soliera is rare but exists. It loses its o→ue (soliera, never 'sueliera') and always takes an infinitive. Acostumbrarse always needs a (+ noun or infinitive): 'que te acostumbraras a madrugar'. Without it, the sentence is wrong.

title: darse cuenta vs realizar

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá te dieras cuenta a tiempo.
examples.en: I wish you would realise in time.
examples.note: Darse cuenta uses dar: dieras, with no accent.

examples.es: Ojalá nos diéramos cuenta de nuestro error.
examples.en: I wish we would realise our mistake.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: diéramos. Darse cuenta de = to realise.

examples.es: Ojalá se diera cuenta de lo que pasaba.
examples.en: I wish he would realise what was happening.
examples.note: Pasaba stays indicative, because it describes a fact.

contrast.es: Ojalá se dé cuenta de lo que pasa.
contrast.en: I hope he realises what's happening.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te lo repetí para que te dieras cuenta.
examples.en: I repeated it to you so that you would realise.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Me dieron el contrato para que realizara los cambios.
examples.en: They gave me the contract so that I would make the changes.
examples.note: Realizar = to carry out, not to realise. The z→c of the present (realice) does not carry over.

examples.es: Se lo repetí para que se diera cuenta de su error.
examples.en: I repeated it to him so that he would realise his mistake.
examples.note: Darse cuenta de su error.

contrast.es: Se lo repetí y se dio cuenta de su error.
contrast.en: I repeated it to him and he realised his mistake.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te pidió que cuando realizaras el pago, le avisaras.
examples.en: He asked you to let him know when you made the payment.
examples.note: Realizar el pago = to make the payment.

examples.es: Acordamos que cuando realizáramos la compra, guardaríamos el recibo.
examples.en: We agreed that when we made the purchase, we'd keep the receipt.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: realizáramos.

examples.es: Me explicaron que cuando realizara el pedido, recibiría un correo.
examples.en: They explained to me that when I placed the order, I'd receive an email.
examples.note: Realizar un pedido = to place an order.

contrast.es: Cuando realicé el pedido, recibí un correo.
contrast.en: When I placed the order, I received an email.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Darse cuenta de uses dar: me diera, te dieras, se diera, nos diéramos, se dieran, with no written accent except in the nosotros form diéramos (the present dé does not carry over). Realizar (realizara, from realizaron) means to carry out, not to realise, a classic false friend: 'que realizaras el pago' (make it), never 'que realizaras tu error'.

title: asistir vs atender

triggers.explanation: Saying something was mandatory is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era obligatorio que asistieras a la reunión.
examples.en: It was mandatory that you attended the meeting.
examples.note: Asistir a = to attend. Asistir takes -ier- endings: asistieras.

examples.es: Era obligatorio que asistiéramos al curso.
examples.en: It was mandatory that we attended the course.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: asistiéramos.

examples.es: Era obligatorio que atendieran a todos los clientes.
examples.en: It was mandatory that they served every customer.
examples.note: Atender a = to serve or look after. The e→ie of the present is gone: atendieran.

contrast.es: Era evidente que atendían a todos los clientes.
contrast.en: It was obvious that they served every customer.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era obligatorio gives a rule (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Le pedí que asistiera a la boda.
examples.en: I asked him to go to the wedding.
examples.note: Asistir a la boda = to attend the wedding.

examples.es: Le pedí que atendiera el teléfono.
examples.en: I asked her to answer the phone.
examples.note: Atender el teléfono = to answer the phone.

examples.es: Le pedí que atendiera a los niños mientras yo estaba fuera.
examples.en: I asked him to look after the children while I was out.
examples.note: Mientras + indicative here: a real, simultaneous situation.

contrast.es: Atendía a los niños mientras yo estaba fuera.
contrast.en: He looked after the children while I was out.
contrast.note: A real, habitual fact uses the indicative. A request uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dijo que cuando asistieras a la boda, le llevaras un regalo.
examples.en: She told you to take her a present when you went to the wedding.
examples.note: The wedding hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Me aseguraron que cuando atendieran mi pedido, me avisarían.
examples.en: They assured me that when they dealt with my order, they'd let me know.
examples.note: Atender un pedido = to deal with an order.

examples.es: Decidí que cuando asistiera a la conferencia, tomaría notas.
examples.en: I decided that when I attended the conference, I'd take notes.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando asistí a la conferencia, tomé notas.
contrast.en: When I attended the conference, I took notes.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Both are regular in this tense, with -ier- endings: asistiera, asistieras, asistiéramos, asistieran and atendiera, atendieras, atendiéramos, atendieran. Atender loses its e→ie (never 'atiendiera'). Asistir a means attend, atender means serve or look after, and neither is the everyday 'help': for that use ayudar.

title: soportar vs apoyar

triggers.explanation: Not understanding someone's behaviour is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No entendía que apoyaras a ese equipo.
examples.en: I didn't understand how you supported that team.
examples.note: Apoyar = to support. Regular: apoyaras.

examples.es: No entendía que soportaras tanto ruido.
examples.en: I didn't understand how you put up with so much noise.
examples.note: Soportar = to put up with, to bear. It never means to support a person.

examples.es: No entendía que lo soportaras.
examples.en: I didn't understand how you stood him.
examples.note: Lo soportaras = you put up with him.

contrast.es: Veía que lo soportabas sin quejarte.
contrast.en: I could see you put up with him without complaining.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something fair is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era justo que apoyáramos a nuestros amigos.
examples.en: It was fair that we supported our friends.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: apoyáramos.

examples.es: Era justo que apoyaran a las familias que lo necesitaban.
examples.en: It was fair that they supported the families who needed it.
examples.note: Lo necesitaban stays indicative, because it describes a fact.

examples.es: Era justo que apoyaras a tu hermano.
examples.en: It was fair that you backed your brother.
examples.note: Apoyar a = to back someone.

contrast.es: Era evidente que apoyabas a tu hermano.
contrast.en: It was obvious that you backed your brother.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era justo gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablé con ellos para que te apoyaran.
examples.en: I talked to them so that they would support you.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ellos).

examples.es: Reforcé la pared para que soportara el peso.
examples.en: I reinforced the wall so that it would hold the weight.
examples.note: Soportar el peso = to bear the weight. The subject is la pared.

examples.es: Reforcé la estantería para que soportara más peso sin que se inclinara.
examples.en: I reinforced the shelf so that it could bear more weight without tilting.
examples.note: Sin que adds a second imperfect subjunctive (inclinara).

contrast.es: Reforcé la estantería y soportó más peso.
contrast.en: I reinforced the shelf and it bore more weight.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Soportar means to put up with or to bear a load, and never to support someone: that's apoyar ('que apoyaras a tu equipo', 'que soportaras el ruido'). Both are regular in this tense: apoyara, soportara. Nosotros takes an accent: apoyáramos, soportáramos.

title: introducir vs presentar

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to do something is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que me presentaras a tu hermana.
examples.en: I wanted you to introduce me to your sister.
examples.note: Presentar a = to introduce a person. Regular: presentaras.

examples.es: Quería que introdujeras la tarjeta en la ranura.
examples.en: I wanted you to insert the card into the slot.
examples.note: Introducir = to insert. The preterite is introdujeron, so introdujeras. The -zc- of the present does not carry over.

examples.es: Quería que presentaras tu proyecto el lunes.
examples.en: I wanted you to present your project on Monday.
examples.note: Presentar un proyecto = to present a project.

contrast.es: Presentaste tu proyecto el lunes.
contrast.en: You presented your project on Monday.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Dije que cuando me presentaras a tu madre, estaría nervioso.
examples.en: I said that when you introduced me to your mother, I'd be nervous.
examples.note: The introduction hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Te dijeron que cuando introdujeras los datos, pulsaras intro.
examples.en: They told you to press enter when you entered the data.
examples.note: Introducir los datos = to enter the data.

examples.es: Me aseguraron que cuando introdujera los datos, el sistema los validaría.
examples.en: They assured me that when I entered the data, the system would validate it.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando introduje los datos, el sistema los validó.
contrast.en: When I entered the data, the system validated it.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que presentara el informe al día siguiente.
examples.en: It was possible that he would present the report the next day.
examples.note: Era posible que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que introdujeran cambios.
examples.en: It was possible that they would introduce changes.
examples.note: Introducir cambios = to bring in changes. Introdujeran, with no i before -eran.

examples.es: Era posible que presentaran la dimisión.
examples.en: It was possible that they would hand in their resignation.
examples.note: Presentar la dimisión = to resign formally.

contrast.es: Presentaron la dimisión esa semana.
contrast.en: They handed in their resignation that week.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Introducir has a j in the imperfect subjunctive: introdujera, introdujeras, introdujéramos, introdujeran (from introdujeron), never 'introduzciera' or 'introduciera'. The present -zc- does not carry over, and the i is dropped after the j. Presentar is regular (presentara). Introducir is for things (data, a card), and presentar is for people and projects.

title: pretender vs fingir

triggers.explanation: Calling something ridiculous is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era ridículo que fingieras estar enfermo.
examples.en: It was ridiculous that you pretended to be ill.
examples.note: Fingir = to pretend. The g→j of the present (finjas) does not carry over: fingieras.

examples.es: Era ridículo que pretendieran cambiar las reglas.
examples.en: It was ridiculous that they intended to change the rules.
examples.note: Pretender = to intend or aim to, not to pretend.

examples.es: Era ridículo que pretendiera convencerme.
examples.en: It was ridiculous that he was trying to convince me.
examples.note: Pretender + infinitive = to try or aim to do.

contrast.es: Veía que pretendía convencerme.
contrast.en: I could see he was trying to convince me.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque fingiera, se le notaría.
examples.en: Even if he pretended, it would show.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque pretendieras engañarme, no lo conseguirías.
examples.en: Even if you tried to fool me, you wouldn't succeed.
examples.note: Pretender + infinitive = to try or aim to do something.

examples.es: Aunque pretendieran ayudarnos, no confiaría en ellos.
examples.en: Even if they meant to help us, I wouldn't trust them.
examples.note: A hypothetical intention, with a conditional result.

contrast.es: Aunque pretendían ayudarnos, no confiábamos en ellos.
contrast.en: Although they meant to help us, we didn't trust them.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Saying something was unnecessary is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No hacía falta que fingieras.
examples.en: You didn't need to pretend.
examples.note: No hacía falta que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No hacía falta que pretendieras ser perfecto.
examples.en: You didn't need to aim to be perfect.
examples.note: Pretender ser = to aim to be.

examples.es: No hacía falta que fingieras alegría.
examples.en: You didn't need to fake happiness.
examples.note: Fingir + noun = to fake a feeling.

contrast.es: Fingías alegría.
contrast.en: You were faking happiness.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative (fingías).

tricky: Pretender is a false friend: it means to aim or intend, not to pretend, which is fingir. Pretender is regular (pretendiera, from pretendieron). Fingir has no g→j in this tense: fingiera, fingieras, fingiéramos, fingieran, never 'finjiera'. The j of the present does not carry over.

title: avergonzado vs embarazada

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que estuviera embarazada.
examples.en: I didn't think she was pregnant.
examples.note: Embarazada = pregnant, never embarrassed. Estar's preterite is estuvieron: estuviera.

examples.es: No creía que se avergonzara de su familia.
examples.en: I didn't think he was ashamed of his family.
examples.note: Avergonzarse de = to be ashamed of. The o→üe of the present is gone: avergonzara.

examples.es: No creía que estuviera embarazada; solo estaba avergonzada.
examples.en: I didn't think she was pregnant; she was just embarrassed.
examples.note: Avergonzada is the word for embarrassed. Estaba stays indicative because it is a fact.

contrast.es: Creía que estaba embarazada, pero me equivocaba.
contrast.en: I thought she was pregnant, but I was wrong.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Calling something understandable is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era comprensible que te diera vergüenza.
examples.en: It was understandable that you felt embarrassed.
examples.note: Dar vergüenza = to make someone feel embarrassed. Diera, with no accent.

examples.es: Era comprensible que se avergonzara.
examples.en: It was understandable that he felt ashamed.
examples.note: Reflexive: se avergonzara.

examples.es: Era comprensible que estuviera avergonzada después de aquello.
examples.en: It was understandable that she was embarrassed after that.
examples.note: Estar avergonzada = to be embarrassed.

contrast.es: Era evidente que estaba avergonzada después de aquello.
contrast.en: It was obvious that she was embarrassed after that.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era comprensible gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te avergonzaras, me lo contaras.
examples.en: I told you to tell me when you felt ashamed.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Me decía que cuando me diera vergüenza, respirara hondo.
examples.en: He used to tell me to breathe deeply when I felt embarrassed.
examples.note: Dar vergüenza works like gustar.

examples.es: Dijo que cuando estuviera embarazada, tendría derecho a baja.
examples.en: He said that when she was pregnant, she'd be entitled to leave.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando estuvo embarazada, tuvo derecho a baja.
contrast.en: When she was pregnant, she was entitled to leave.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Embarazada means pregnant, never embarrassed; embarrassed is avergonzado/a or 'me daba vergüenza'. Avergonzarse has no o→üe in this tense: avergonzara, avergonzaras, avergonzáramos, avergonzaran (from avergonzaron), never 'avergüenzara'. Estar gives estuviera, and dar gives diera, with no accent.

title: conducir vs manejar

triggers.explanation: Calling something dangerous is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era peligroso que condujeras cansado.
examples.en: It was dangerous for you to drive tired.
examples.note: Conducir's preterite is condujeron, so condujeras. The -zc- of the present does not carry over.

examples.es: Era peligroso que manejaras con lluvia.
examples.en: It was dangerous for you to drive in the rain.
examples.note: Manejar = to drive (Latin America). Regular: manejaras.

examples.es: Era peligroso que condujeras sin gafas.
examples.en: It was dangerous for you to drive without glasses.
examples.note: Sin gafas is a prepositional phrase, with no new verb.

contrast.es: Sabía que conducías sin gafas.
contrast.en: I knew you drove without glasses.
contrast.note: Knowing a fact takes the indicative. A judgement takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A habitual or completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Mi padre me decía que cuando condujera, usara el cinturón.
examples.en: My father used to tell me to wear my seatbelt when I drove.
examples.note: The driving hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando manejara de noche, usaría gafas.
examples.en: I promised that when I drove at night, I'd wear glasses.
examples.note: A promise about the future, from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Dije que cuando condujera por la ciudad, iría despacio.
examples.en: I said that when I drove through the city, I'd go slowly.
