examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando conducía por la ciudad, iba despacio.
contrast.en: When I drove through the city, I went slowly.
contrast.note: A habitual past event takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Doubt calls for the subjunctive, so after a past verb it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que manejara bien.
examples.en: I doubted he drove well.
examples.note: Dudaba que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que condujeran tan rápido.
examples.en: I doubted they drove that fast.
examples.note: Condujeran, with no i before -eran.

examples.es: Dudaba que condujera ese camión.
examples.en: I doubted he drove that lorry.
examples.note: Camión = lorry (British English) or truck (American English). The Spanish word is the same everywhere.

contrast.es: Sabía que conducía ese camión.
contrast.en: I knew he drove that lorry.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Dudaba que takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Conducir has a j in the imperfect subjunctive: condujera, condujeras, condujéramos, condujeran (from condujeron), never 'conduciera' or 'conduzcara'. The -zc- of the present does not carry over, and the i is dropped after the j. Manejar is regular (manejara). The choice is partly regional: conducir is used everywhere and is the usual verb in Spain, while manejar is common in much of Latin America.

title: probar vs intentar

triggers.explanation: Calling something advisable is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era recomendable que intentaras ir temprano.
examples.en: It was advisable that you tried to go early.
examples.note: Intentar + infinitive = to try to do. Regular: intentaras.

examples.es: Era recomendable que probaras el vino antes de comprarlo.
examples.en: It was advisable that you tasted the wine before buying it.
examples.note: Probar = to taste. The o→ue of the present is gone: probaras, never 'pruebaras'.

examples.es: Era recomendable que intentaras hablar con ella.
examples.en: It was advisable that you tried to talk to her.
examples.note: Intentar hablar = to try to speak.

contrast.es: Era recomendable intentar hablar con ella.
contrast.en: It was advisable to try to talk to her.
contrast.note: No specific subject = infinitive. A specific subject = que + imperfect subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Corté un trozo para que probara el queso.
examples.en: I cut a piece so that he could taste the cheese.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Te invité para que probaras el postre.
examples.en: I invited you so that you would try the dessert.
examples.note: Probar el postre = to try the dessert.

examples.es: Hablé contigo para que intentaras otra vez.
examples.en: I talked to you so that you would try again.
examples.note: Intentar otra vez = to try again.

contrast.es: Hablé contigo y volviste a intentarlo.
contrast.en: I talked to you and you tried again.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te pedí que cuando probaras el café, me dijeras qué opinabas.
examples.en: I asked you to tell me what you thought when you tried the coffee.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives. Opinabas stays indicative, because it is a fact.

examples.es: Me advirtieron que cuando intentara abrirla, lo hiciera con cuidado.
examples.en: They warned me to be careful when I tried to open it.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Te aseguré que cuando lo intentaras de nuevo, tendrías más suerte.
examples.en: I assured you that when you tried again, you'd have more luck.
examples.note: Lo is the object of intentar.

contrast.es: Cuando lo intentaste de nuevo, tuviste más suerte.
contrast.en: When you tried again, you had more luck.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Probar loses its o→ue in the imperfect subjunctive: probara, probaras, probáramos, probaran, never 'pruebara'. Intentar is regular (intentara). Probar is to test, taste or try something, and intentar + infinitive is to try to do something. Don't mix them: 'que probaras el queso' (taste) vs 'que intentaras abrirlo' (try).

title: mover vs mudarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá te mudaras pronto.
examples.en: I wish you would move soon.
examples.note: Mudarse = to move house. Regular: mudaras.

examples.es: Ojalá nos mudáramos a una casa grande.
examples.en: I wish we would move to a big house.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: mudáramos.

examples.es: Ojalá se moviera la fila más rápido.
examples.en: I wish the queue would move faster.
examples.note: Moverse = to move. The o→ue of the present is gone: moviera.

contrast.es: Ojalá se mueva la fila más rápido.
contrast.en: I hope the queue moves faster.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Te pedí que me avisaras antes de que te mudaras.
examples.en: I asked you to let me know before you moved.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the request and the time clause.

examples.es: Hablamos antes de que se mudara.
examples.en: We talked before he moved out.
examples.note: The move hadn't happened yet when we talked.

examples.es: Quité el mueble antes de que se moviera el camión.
examples.en: I took the furniture away before the lorry moved off.
examples.note: Moverse = to move off.

contrast.es: Quité el mueble después de que se movió el camión.
contrast.en: I took the furniture away after the lorry moved off.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era probable que me mudara en verano.
examples.en: I would probably move in the summer.
examples.note: Era probable que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era probable que movieran la reunión al jueves.
examples.en: It was likely that they would move the meeting to Thursday.
examples.note: Mover = to move something. Movieran, from movieron.

examples.es: Era probable que se mudara a otra ciudad.
examples.en: It was likely that he would move to another city.
examples.note: Mudarse a = to move to.

contrast.es: Estaba seguro de que se mudaría a otra ciudad.
contrast.en: I was sure he would move to another city.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Likelihood uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Mover loses its o→ue in the imperfect subjunctive: moviera, movieras, moviéramos, movieran (from movieron), never 'mueviera'. Mudarse is regular (mudara). Mover is to shift something, moverse is to move yourself, and mudarse is to change house. Don't confuse them.

title: aprender vs enseñar

triggers.explanation: Calling something essential is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era esencial que aprendieras de tus errores.
examples.en: It was essential that you learned from your mistakes.
examples.note: Aprender takes -ier- endings: aprendieras.

examples.es: Era esencial que enseñáramos con el ejemplo.
examples.en: It was essential that we taught by example.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: enseñáramos. The ñ stays.

examples.es: Era esencial que aprendiera a escuchar.
examples.en: It was essential that he learned to listen.
examples.note: Aprender a + infinitive = to learn to do.

contrast.es: Era evidente que aprendía a escuchar.
contrast.en: It was obvious that he was learning to listen.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era esencial gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dijo que en cuanto aprendiera a nadar, iríamos al mar.
examples.en: He said that as soon as he learned to swim, we'd go to the sea.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Dijiste que en cuanto me enseñaras la casa, decidiríamos.
examples.en: You said that as soon as you showed me the house, we'd decide.
examples.note: Enseñar la casa = to show the house.

examples.es: Te prometí que en cuanto aprendieras la lección, podrías salir.
examples.en: I promised you that as soon as you learned the lesson, you could go out.
examples.note: Podrías is a conditional, a future from the past.

contrast.es: En cuanto aprendiste la lección, saliste.
contrast.en: As soon as you learned the lesson, you went out.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Repetí la lección para que aprendieras.
examples.en: I repeated the lesson so that you would learn.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Fui a la escuela para que me enseñaran a nadar.
examples.en: I went to the school so that they would teach me to swim.
examples.note: Enseñar a + infinitive = to teach to do.

examples.es: Le pagaba para que me enseñara a tocar la guitarra.
examples.en: I paid him so that he would teach me to play the guitar.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

contrast.es: Le pagaba para aprender a tocar la guitarra.
contrast.en: I paid him to learn to play the guitar.
contrast.note: Same subject = para + infinitive. A different subject = para que + imperfect subjunctive.

tricky: Aprender and enseñar are both regular in this tense: aprendiera (from aprendieron), enseñara. The ñ stays. Enseñar covers both teach and show: 'que me enseñaras inglés' (teach) vs 'que me enseñaras la casa' (show). Aprender needs a before an infinitive: aprender a nadar.

title: dar vs regalar

triggers.explanation: Calling something crazy is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era una locura que regalaras tanto dinero.
examples.en: It was crazy that you gave away so much money.
examples.note: Regalar = to give as a gift, or to give away. Regular: regalaras.

examples.es: Era una locura que me dieras este coche.
examples.en: It was crazy that you gave me this car.
examples.note: Dar's preterite is dieron, so dieras, with no accent.

examples.es: Era una locura que le diera todo su dinero.
examples.en: It was crazy that he gave her all his money.
examples.note: Le is the person receiving the money.

contrast.es: Veía que le daba todo su dinero.
contrast.en: I could see he gave her all his money.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me dijeron que cuando regalara algo, pusiera una nota.
examples.en: They told me to add a note when I gave a present.
examples.note: The gift hadn't been given yet.

examples.es: Me dijiste que cuando me dieras la respuesta, lo decidiríamos.
examples.en: You told me that when you gave me the answer, we'd decide.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Me aconsejó que cuando regalara un libro, escribiera una dedicatoria.
examples.en: He advised me to write a dedication when I gave a book as a gift.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported advice.

contrast.es: Cuando regalé un libro, escribí una dedicatoria.
contrast.en: When I gave a book as a gift, I wrote a dedication.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que regalara nada.
examples.en: I didn't think he would give anything.
examples.note: No creía que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que nos dieran descuento.
examples.en: I didn't think they would give us a discount.
examples.note: Dar descuento = to give a discount.

examples.es: No creía que me regalara nada: era muy tacaño.
examples.en: I didn't think he would give me anything: he was very stingy.
examples.note: Tacaño = stingy. The reason (era) is a fact, so it is indicative.

contrast.es: Creía que me regalaba algo cada año.
contrast.en: I thought he gave me something every year.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

tricky: Dar's imperfect subjunctive is diera, dieras, diéramos, dieran (from dieron), with no accent, unlike the present dé. Regalar is regular (regalara). Regalar is to give as a gift, with nothing expected back, and dar is the general verb: 'que me dieras' (give me) vs 'que me regalaras' (give me as a present).

title: prestar vs pedir prestado

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me daba miedo que prestaras tu coche a cualquiera.
examples.en: I was afraid you would lend your car to anyone.
examples.note: Prestar = to lend. Regular: prestaras.

examples.es: Me daba miedo que pidieras prestado tanto dinero.
examples.en: I was afraid you would borrow so much money.
examples.note: Pedir prestado = to borrow. Pedir keeps e→i (from pidieron): pidieras.

examples.es: Me daba miedo que pidiera prestado más dinero.
examples.en: I was afraid he would borrow more money.
examples.note: Prestado doesn't change.

contrast.es: Veía que pedía prestado más dinero.
contrast.en: I could see he borrowed more money.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablé con él para que te prestara la moto.
examples.en: I talked to him so that he would lend you the motorbike.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Hablé con ella para que nos prestara la casa.
examples.en: I talked to her so that she would lend us the house.
examples.note: Nos is the person receiving the loan.

examples.es: Lo llamé para que te prestara el coche ese fin de semana.
examples.en: I called him so that he would lend you the car that weekend.
examples.note: Prestar + indirect object (te) + thing.

contrast.es: Lo llamé y te prestó el coche ese fin de semana.
contrast.en: I called him and he lent you the car that weekend.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando pidieras prestado algo, lo devolvieras.
examples.en: I told you to give something back when you borrowed it.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Te advertí que cuando te prestara el coche, tuvieras cuidado.
examples.en: I warned you to be careful when I lent you the car.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Acordamos que cuando pidiéramos prestado dinero, firmaríamos un papel.
examples.en: We agreed that when we borrowed money, we'd sign a paper.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: pidiéramos.

contrast.es: Cuando pedimos prestado dinero, firmamos un papel.
contrast.en: When we borrowed money, we signed a paper.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Prestar is regular (prestara), but pedir prestado carries pedir's e→i, which stays in the imperfect subjunctive: pidiera prestado, pidieras prestado, pidiéramos prestado, pidieran prestado (from pidieron). 'Que me prestaras' = that you lend me, 'que pidieras prestado' = that you borrow. Never mix up who gives and who takes.

title: llamar vs llamarse

triggers.explanation: Asking someone to act is a wish, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Te pedí que llamaras a tu madre.
examples.en: I asked you to call your mother.
examples.note: Llamar = to call. Regular: llamaras.

examples.es: Te pedí que me llamaras cuando llegaras.
examples.en: I asked you to call me when you arrived.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the request and the time clause.

examples.es: Te pedí que me llamaras Ana, no señora.
examples.en: I asked you to call me Ana, not ma'am.
examples.note: Llamar + person + name = to call someone a name.

contrast.es: Me llamabas señora.
contrast.en: You used to call me ma'am.
contrast.note: A plain habitual fact uses the indicative (llamabas).

triggers.explanation: When the person you describe doesn't exist, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: No había nadie que llamara a esa hora.
examples.en: There was nobody who called at that hour.
examples.note: Nadie = no such person, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No había nadie que se llamara así en mi clase.
examples.en: There was nobody called that in my class.
examples.note: Llamarse = to be called. The pronoun changes the meaning: se llamara.

examples.es: No había nadie que se llamara Pancracio en el pueblo.
examples.en: There was nobody called Pancracio in the village.
examples.note: A non-existent person calls for the subjunctive.

contrast.es: Había alguien que se llamaba Pancracio en el pueblo.
contrast.en: There was someone called Pancracio in the village.
contrast.note: Había alguien que + indicative: such a person existed.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dijo que cuando llamaras, preguntaras por Marta.
examples.en: He told you that when you called, you should ask for Marta.
examples.note: The call hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Te avisé de que cuando me llamaras, ya estaría en casa.
examples.en: I told you that when you called me, I'd already be at home.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Me pidió que cuando te llamara el médico, le avisara.
examples.en: He asked me to let him know when the doctor called you.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

contrast.es: Cuando te llamó el médico, me avisaste.
contrast.en: When the doctor called you, you told me.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Llamar is regular (llamara, llamaras), and llamarse adds the pronoun: me llamara, te llamaras, se llamara, nos llamáramos. The pronoun changes the meaning: 'que llamara' (that he called) vs 'que se llamara' (that he was named). Never mix up who is calling and who is called.

title: levantar vs levantarse

triggers.explanation: Preferring that someone else act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Prefería que te levantaras temprano.
examples.en: I preferred that you got up early.
examples.note: Levantarse = to get up. Regular: te levantaras.

examples.es: Prefería que se levantaran todos a la vez.
examples.en: I preferred that everyone got up at the same time.
examples.note: Todos is plural, so levantaran.

examples.es: Prefería que levantaras al niño con cuidado.
examples.en: I preferred that you lifted the child carefully.
examples.note: Levantar + object = to lift someone or something. Without the pronoun, it is not 'to get up'.

contrast.es: Levantabas al niño con cuidado.
contrast.en: You lifted the child carefully.
contrast.note: A plain fact uses the indicative. A preference uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet happened, from a past viewpoint, takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Me dijo que esperara hasta que se levantara la niebla.
examples.en: He told me to wait until the fog lifted.
examples.note: Levantarse = to lift (of fog).

examples.es: Te pedí que te quedaras sentado hasta que se levantaran los demás.
examples.en: I asked you to stay seated until the others got up.
examples.note: Los demás is plural, so levantaran.

examples.es: El médico dijo que descansaras hasta que te levantaras sin dolor.
examples.en: The doctor said to rest until you could get up without pain.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the reported advice and the time clause.

contrast.es: Descansé hasta que me levanté sin dolor.
contrast.en: I rested until I got up without pain.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te puse la alarma para que te levantaras a tiempo.
examples.en: I set the alarm for you so that you'd get up on time.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Hablaba bajo para que no se levantara el niño.
examples.en: I spoke quietly so that the child wouldn't get up.
examples.note: Levantarse = to get up out of bed (to wake up is despertarse).

examples.es: Te ayudé para que levantáramos la mesa.
examples.en: I helped you so that we could lift the table.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: levantáramos. Levantar + object, without the pronoun.

contrast.es: Te ayudé y levantamos la mesa.
contrast.en: I helped you and we lifted the table.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Levantar and levantarse are both regular (levantara), but the reflexive decides the meaning: 'que levantaras la caja' (lift) vs 'que te levantaras' (get up). Nosotros takes an accent: levantáramos.

title: ir vs irse

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quería que te fueras.
examples.en: I didn't want you to leave.
examples.note: Ir's imperfect subjunctive comes from fueron: fueras. It is the same as ser.

examples.es: No quería que se fuera sin despedirse.
examples.en: I didn't want him to leave without saying goodbye.
examples.note: Irse = to go away, to leave. Sin despedirse is an infinitive because the subject is the same.

examples.es: No quería que fueras a casa de Pedro.
examples.en: I didn't want you to go to Pedro's house.
examples.note: Ir a = to go to. Without the pronoun, it is just 'to go there'.

contrast.es: Sabía que ibas a casa de Pedro.
contrast.en: I knew you were going to Pedro's house.
contrast.note: Knowing a fact takes the indicative (ibas). A wish takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te fueras, cerraras la puerta.
examples.en: I told you to close the door when you left.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Mi madre me pedía que cuando fuéramos al mercado, comprara pan.
examples.en: My mother used to ask me to buy bread when we went to the market.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: fuéramos.

examples.es: Te dijeron que cuando fueras al médico, preguntaras por el análisis.
examples.en: They told you that when you went to the doctor, you should ask about the test.
examples.note: Ir al médico = to go to the doctor.

contrast.es: Cuando fuiste al médico, preguntaste por el análisis.
contrast.en: When you went to the doctor, you asked about the test.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite fuiste).

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que se fuera al día siguiente.
examples.en: It was possible that he would leave the next day.
examples.note: Era posible que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que fuéramos al cine.
examples.en: It was possible that we would go to the cinema.
examples.note: Fuéramos can be ser or ir. The context shows it's ir here.

examples.es: Era posible que nos fuéramos de viaje.
examples.en: It was possible that we would go away on a trip.
examples.note: Irse de viaje = to go away on a trip.

contrast.es: Estaba seguro de que nos iríamos de viaje.
contrast.en: I was sure we would go away on a trip.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Possibility uses the subjunctive.

tricky: Ir's imperfect subjunctive is fuera, fueras, fuéramos, fueran (from fueron), the same as ser. Context tells you which verb it is. Never 'vaya' (present) or 'iera'. Irse adds the pronoun: me fuera, te fueras, se fuera, nos fuéramos.

title: dormir vs dormirse

triggers.explanation: Hoping something happens is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que durmieras bien.
examples.en: I hoped you slept well.
examples.note: Dormir changes o→u in the imperfect subjunctive (from durmieron): durmieras.

examples.es: Esperaba que no te durmieras en la reunión.
examples.en: I hoped you wouldn't fall asleep in the meeting.
examples.note: Dormirse = to fall asleep.

examples.es: Esperaba que se durmiera pronto el bebé.
examples.en: I hoped the baby would fall asleep soon.
examples.note: El bebé is the subject, placed after the verb.

contrast.es: Sabía que el bebé se dormía pronto.
contrast.en: I knew the baby fell asleep quickly.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Esperaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Te pedí que me lo dijeras antes de que me durmiera.
examples.en: I asked you to tell me before I fell asleep.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the request and the time clause.

examples.es: Hablamos antes de que los niños durmieran la siesta.
examples.en: We talked before the children had their nap.
examples.note: Plural subject: los niños.

examples.es: Te llamé antes de que se durmiera el niño.
examples.en: I called you before the boy fell asleep.
examples.note: The falling asleep hadn't happened yet.

contrast.es: Te llamé después de que se durmió el niño.
contrast.en: I called you after the boy fell asleep.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando durmieras, apagaras el móvil.
examples.en: I told you to turn off your phone when you slept.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dijo que cuando se durmiera, saldríamos.
examples.en: He said that when he fell asleep, we'd go out.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Le pedí que cuando me durmiera, no me despertara.
examples.en: I asked him not to wake me when I fell asleep.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives.

contrast.es: Cuando me dormí, nadie me despertó.
contrast.en: When I fell asleep, nobody woke me.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Dormir has a stem change to u in every imperfect subjunctive form: durmiera, durmieras, durmiéramos, durmieran (from durmieron), never 'dormiera' or 'duermiera'. Dormirse is to fall asleep: 'que durmieras' (that you slept) vs 'que te durmieras' (that you fell asleep).

title: estar de acuerdo vs acordar

triggers.explanation: Calling something important is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era importante que estuviéramos de acuerdo.
examples.en: It was important that we agreed.
examples.note: Estar's preterite is estuvieron: estuviéramos. Keep the full phrase: estar de acuerdo.

examples.es: Era importante que acordáramos un horario.
examples.en: It was important that we agreed on a schedule.
examples.note: Acordar = to agree on. The o→ue of the present is gone: acordáramos.

examples.es: Era importante que acordaran los términos antes de firmar.
examples.en: It was important that they agreed the terms before signing.
examples.note: Antes de firmar is an infinitive because the subject is the same (ellos).

contrast.es: Acordaron los términos antes de firmar.
contrast.en: They agreed the terms before signing.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que estuviera de acuerdo.
examples.en: I didn't think he agreed.
examples.note: Estar de acuerdo = to agree.

examples.es: No creía que estuvieran de acuerdo con el plan.
examples.en: I didn't think they agreed with the plan.
examples.note: Estar de acuerdo con = to agree with.

examples.es: No creía que acordaran nada ese día.
examples.en: I didn't think they would agree on anything that day.
examples.note: Acordar nada = to agree on anything.

contrast.es: Creía que acordarían algo ese día.
contrast.en: I thought they would agree on something that day.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative (here a conditional). No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablé con ella para que estuviera de acuerdo.
examples.en: I talked to her so that she would agree.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ella).

examples.es: Hablé con el vendedor para que acordara un precio justo.
examples.en: I talked to the seller so that he would agree a fair price.
examples.note: Acordar un precio = to agree a price.

examples.es: Les escribí para que acordaran una fecha.
examples.en: I wrote to them so that they would agree a date.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ellos).

contrast.es: Les escribí y acordaron una fecha.
contrast.en: I wrote to them and they agreed a date.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Estar de acuerdo needs the full phrase: estuviera de acuerdo, estuvieran de acuerdo (from estuvieron). Acordar loses its o→ue in this tense: acordara, acordaras, acordáramos, acordaran, never 'acuerdara'. Estar de acuerdo is to hold the same opinion, and acordar is to agree on something.

title: hacer falta vs necesitar

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive. Podía ser que is the past version of puede que.

examples.es: Podía ser que hiciera falta más tiempo.
examples.en: More time might be needed.
examples.note: Hacer falta = to be needed. Hacer's stem is hic-: hiciera.

examples.es: Podía ser que necesitáramos ayuda.
examples.en: We might need help.
examples.note: Necesitar is regular. Nosotros takes an accent: necesitáramos.

examples.es: Podía ser que me hiciera falta un abrigo.
examples.en: I might need a coat.
examples.note: Hacer falta works like gustar: un abrigo is the subject.

contrast.es: Me hizo falta un abrigo.
contrast.en: I needed a coat.
contrast.note: A real, completed fact takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que necesitara ayuda.
examples.en: I didn't think he needed help.
examples.note: No creía que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que te hicieran falta más libros.
examples.en: I didn't think you needed more books.
examples.note: Libros is plural, so hicieran. Hacer falta agrees with the thing needed.

examples.es: No creía que necesitaras tanto dinero.
examples.en: I didn't think you needed so much money.
examples.note: Necesitar + noun, with no preposition.

contrast.es: Creía que necesitabas tanto dinero.
contrast.en: I thought you needed so much money.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando necesitaras algo, me llamaras.
examples.en: I told you to call me when you needed something.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Mi madre decía que cuando me hiciera falta dinero, se lo pidiera.
examples.en: My mother used to say I should ask her when I needed money.
examples.note: Hacer falta + dinero, with a pronoun for the person.

examples.es: Dijo que cuando necesitara ayuda, la pediría.
examples.en: He said that when he needed help, he'd ask for it.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando necesitó ayuda, la pidió.
contrast.en: When he needed help, he asked for it.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Hacer falta works like gustar: the thing needed is the subject and agrees ('que te hiciera falta tiempo', 'que te hicieran falta libros'). Hacer's imperfect subjunctive is hiciera (from hicieron), never 'hagiera'. Necesitar is regular (necesitara) and takes a personal subject.

title: importar vs interesar

triggers.explanation: Doubt calls for the subjunctive, so after a past verb it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que le importara.
examples.en: I doubted he cared.
examples.note: Importar works like gustar. Le is the person.

examples.es: Dudaba que les interesaran las noticias.
examples.en: I doubted they were interested in the news.
examples.note: Las noticias is plural, so interesaran.

examples.es: Dudaba que me importara su opinión.
examples.en: I doubted that I cared about his opinion.
examples.note: Su opinión is the subject, so importara is singular.

contrast.es: Sabía que me importaba su opinión.
contrast.en: I knew I cared about his opinion.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Dudaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Surprise is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era extraño que no te interesara.
examples.en: It was strange that you weren't interested.
examples.note: Interesar works like gustar.

examples.es: Era extraño que no te importaran los precios.
examples.en: It was strange that you didn't care about the prices.
examples.note: Los precios is plural, so importaran.

examples.es: Era extraño que no le interesara el fútbol.
examples.en: It was strange that he wasn't interested in football.
examples.note: El fútbol is the subject.

contrast.es: Era verdad que no le interesaba el fútbol.
contrast.en: It was true that he wasn't interested in football.
contrast.note: Era verdad states a fact (indicative). Era extraño reacts to it (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que aunque no te interesara, escucharas.
examples.en: I told you to listen even if you weren't interested.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: aunque and the reported request.

examples.es: Aunque no te importara, te lo diría.
examples.en: Even if you didn't care, I'd tell you.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque le importara poco, se lo diría.
examples.en: Even if he cared little, I'd tell him.
examples.note: Importar poco = to matter little.

contrast.es: Aunque le importaba poco, se lo dije.
contrast.en: Although he cared little, I told him.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

tricky: Importar and interesar both work like gustar, so the thing that matters is the subject and agrees: 'que te importara el precio', 'que te importaran los precios'. Both are regular in this tense: importara, interesara. Importar is to matter or care, and interesar is to interest.

title: funcionar vs trabajar

triggers.explanation: Calling something odd is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era raro que el coche no funcionara.
examples.en: It was odd that the car didn't work.
examples.note: Funcionar = to work (of machines). Regular: funcionara.

examples.es: Era raro que trabajaras los domingos.
examples.en: It was odd that you worked on Sundays.
examples.note: Trabajar = to work (of people).

examples.es: Era raro que trabajara de noche.
examples.en: It was odd that he worked at night.
examples.note: Trabajar de noche = to work nights.

contrast.es: Sabía que trabajaba de noche.
contrast.en: I knew he worked at night.
contrast.note: Knowing a fact takes the indicative. A reaction takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá funcionara el plan.
examples.en: I wish the plan would work.
examples.note: The speaker thinks it is unlikely.

examples.es: Ojalá funcionaran los frenos.
examples.en: I wish the brakes worked.
examples.note: Los frenos is plural, so funcionaran.

examples.es: Ojalá funcionara el wifi en el hotel.
examples.en: I wish the wifi worked in the hotel.
examples.note: The speaker implies it doesn't.

contrast.es: Ojalá funcione el wifi en el hotel.
contrast.en: I hope the wifi works in the hotel.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Revisé el motor para que funcionara.
examples.en: I checked the engine so that it would work.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / el motor).

examples.es: Trabajé duro para que funcionara el negocio.
examples.en: I worked hard so that the business would work.
examples.note: Funcionar for a business or plan.

examples.es: Llamé al técnico para que funcionara la lavadora antes del fin de semana.
examples.en: I called the technician so that the washing machine would work before the weekend.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / la lavadora).

contrast.es: Llamé al técnico y la lavadora funcionó antes del fin de semana.
contrast.en: I called the technician and the washing machine worked before the weekend.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Funcionar is for machines, systems and plans, and trabajar is mainly for people. Both are regular in this tense (funcionara, trabajara), so the catch is choosing the right verb: 'que el coche funcionara', but 'que tú trabajaras'. Don't say 'el coche trabajaba' for 'the car worked'.

title: cumplir

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me prometieron que cuando cumpliera dieciocho, podría conducir.
examples.en: They promised me that when I turned eighteen, I'd be able to drive.
examples.note: Cumplir + age = to turn that age. Cumpliera, from cumplieron.

examples.es: Dije que cuando cumpliera treinta años, haría una fiesta.
examples.en: I said that when I turned thirty, I'd have a party.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando cumpliera con mis obligaciones, descansaría.
examples.en: I promised that when I'd fulfilled my duties, I'd rest.
examples.note: Cumplir con = to fulfil a duty.

contrast.es: Cuando cumplí con mis obligaciones, descansé.
contrast.en: When I fulfilled my duties, I rested.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Demanding that someone act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te exigí que cumplieras las normas.
examples.en: I demanded that you follow the rules.
examples.note: Cumplir las normas = to follow the rules.

examples.es: Te exigí que cumplieras con el plazo.
examples.en: I demanded that you meet the deadline.
examples.note: Cumplir con el plazo = to meet the deadline.

examples.es: Te exigí que cumplieras lo prometido.
examples.en: I demanded that you keep your promise.
examples.note: Lo prometido = what was promised.

contrast.es: Cumpliste lo prometido.
contrast.en: You kept your promise.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Calling something unfair is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era justo que no cumplieran su palabra.
examples.en: It wasn't fair that they didn't keep their word.
examples.note: Cumplir su palabra = to keep your word.

examples.es: No era justo que cumpliera la condena sin pruebas.
examples.en: It wasn't fair that he served his sentence without evidence.
examples.note: Cumplir una condena = to serve a sentence.

examples.es: No era justo que cumpliera todo el castigo.
examples.en: It wasn't fair that he served the whole punishment.
examples.note: Cumplir un castigo = to serve a punishment.

contrast.es: Era evidente que cumplía todo el castigo.
contrast.en: It was obvious that he was serving the whole punishment.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). No era justo gives a judgement (subjunctive).

tricky: Cumplir is regular in this tense: cumpliera, cumplieras, cumpliéramos, cumplieran (from cumplieron). Its meaning depends on the object: 'que cumplieras veinte años' (turn twenty), 'que cumplieras las normas' (follow the rules), 'que cumplieras con tu deber' (fulfil your duty). Cumplir con needs the preposition for duties.

title: llegar vs alcanzar

triggers.explanation: Calling something impossible is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era imposible que llegáramos a tiempo.
examples.en: It was impossible that we arrived on time.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: llegáramos. The g→gu of the present is not needed here.

examples.es: Era imposible que alcanzara el estante.
examples.en: It was impossible that he reached the shelf.
examples.note: Alcanzar = to reach. The z→c of the present does not carry over: alcanzara.

examples.es: Era imposible que alcanzáramos el objetivo.
examples.en: It was impossible that we reached the target.
examples.note: Alcanzar un objetivo = to achieve a target.

contrast.es: Alcanzamos el objetivo.
contrast.en: We reached the target.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando llegaras, me llamaras.
examples.en: I told you to call me when you arrived.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Te dijo que cuando alcanzaras la cima, miraras abajo.
examples.en: He told you to look down when you reached the top.
examples.note: Alcanzar la cima = to reach the summit.

examples.es: Me aseguraron que cuando llegara el momento, lo sabría.
examples.en: They assured me that when the moment came, I'd know.
examples.note: Llegar el momento = for the moment to come.

contrast.es: Cuando llegó el momento, lo supe.
contrast.en: When the moment came, I knew.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te subí a la silla para que alcanzaras el estante.
examples.en: I lifted you onto the chair so that you could reach the shelf.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Te desperté temprano para que llegaras a tiempo.
examples.en: I woke you early so that you would arrive on time.
examples.note: Llegar a tiempo = to arrive on time.

examples.es: Ahorré para que me alcanzara el dinero.
examples.en: I saved so that I would have enough money.
examples.note: Alcanzar + a person = to be enough. El dinero is the subject.

contrast.es: Ahorré y me alcanzó el dinero.
contrast.en: I saved and I had enough money.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Llegar and alcanzar are regular in this tense: llegara, alcanzara. The spelling changes of the present (llegue, alcance) do not carry over, so never 'lleguara' or 'alcancara'. Alcanzar also means to be enough ('me alcanzara el dinero'), which works like gustar. Llegar is to arrive, alcanzar is to reach.

title: quitar vs quitarse

triggers.explanation: Saying what was better is an evaluation, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era mejor que te quitaras los zapatos.
examples.en: It was better that you took your shoes off.
examples.note: Quitarse = to take off (your own clothes). Regular: quitaras.

examples.es: Era mejor que quitáramos esto de aquí.
examples.en: It was better that we took this away from here.
examples.note: Quitar = to remove. Nosotros takes an accent: quitáramos.

examples.es: Era mejor que le quitaras los zapatos al niño.
examples.en: It was better that you took the child's shoes off.
examples.note: Quitar + object + le = to remove something from someone else.

contrast.es: Le quitabas los zapatos al niño.
contrast.en: You used to take the child's shoes off.
contrast.note: A plain habitual fact uses the indicative. A judgement uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te quitaras el abrigo, lo colgaras.
examples.en: I told you to hang up your coat when you took it off.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Me pidió que cuando quitara los platos, pasara la fregona.
examples.en: She asked me to mop the floor when I cleared the plates.
examples.note: Quitar los platos = to clear the plates.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando se quitara las gafas, vería sus ojos.
examples.en: He told me that when she took off her glasses, I'd see her eyes.
examples.note: Quitarse las gafas = to take your glasses off.

contrast.es: Cuando se quitó las gafas, vi sus ojos.
contrast.en: When she took off her glasses, I saw her eyes.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Le puse hielo para que se le quitara el dolor.
examples.en: I put ice on it so that the pain would go away.
examples.note: Quitársele el dolor = for the pain to go away.

examples.es: Usé vinagre para que se quitara la mancha.
examples.en: I used vinegar so that the stain would come out.
examples.note: Quitarse = to come off, to come out.

examples.es: Los llamé para que me quitaran la multa.
examples.en: I called them so that they would cancel my fine.
examples.note: Quitar la multa = to cancel the fine.

contrast.es: Los llamé y me quitaron la multa.
contrast.en: I called them and they cancelled my fine.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Quitar is regular in this tense (quitara, quitaras, quitáramos, quitaran), with no spelling change. The reflexive changes who is affected: 'que quitaras la mesa' (remove it) vs 'que te quitaras el abrigo' (take your own coat off). Quitársele algo = for something to go away from you.

title: llevar vs vestirse (wear)

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to do something is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que llevaras tu abrigo.
examples.en: I wanted you to wear your coat.
examples.note: Llevar = to wear or carry. Regular: llevaras.

examples.es: Quería que te vistieras rápido.
examples.en: I wanted you to get dressed quickly.
examples.note: Vestirse keeps e→i in every form (from vistieron): vistieras.

examples.es: Quería que llevaras el vestido azul.
examples.en: I wanted you to wear the blue dress.
examples.note: Llevar + clothes = to be wearing them.

contrast.es: Llevabas el vestido azul.
contrast.en: You were wearing the blue dress.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative (llevabas).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te vistieras, me avisaras.
examples.en: I told you to let me know when you got dressed.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dijimos que cuando nos vistiéramos, saldríamos.
examples.en: We said that when we got dressed, we'd go out.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: vistiéramos.

examples.es: Me dijeron que cuando llevaras traje, nadie te reconocería.
examples.en: They told me that when you wore a suit, nobody would recognise you.
examples.note: Llevar traje = to wear a suit.

contrast.es: Cuando llevaste traje, nadie te reconoció.
contrast.en: When you wore a suit, nobody recognised you.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Preparé la ropa para que se vistiera rápido.
examples.en: I got the clothes ready so that he would get dressed quickly.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Le di un abrigo para que llevara algo caliente.
examples.en: I gave him a coat so that he would wear something warm.
examples.note: Llevar algo caliente = to wear something warm.

examples.es: Le di un pañuelo para que llevara la cabeza cubierta.
examples.en: I gave her a scarf so that she would keep her head covered.
examples.note: Llevar + part of the body + adjective = to have it covered.

contrast.es: Le di un pañuelo y llevó la cabeza cubierta.
contrast.en: I gave her a scarf and she kept her head covered.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Vestirse keeps e→i in every imperfect subjunctive form: me vistiera, te vistieras, se vistieran, nos vistiéramos, never 'vestiera'. Llevar is regular (llevara). Llevar is to wear or carry something, and vestirse is the act of getting dressed.

title: ganar vs ganarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá ganara mi equipo.
examples.en: I wish my team would win.
examples.note: The speaker thinks it is unlikely.

examples.es: Ojalá ganáramos el partido.
examples.en: I wish we would win the match.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: ganáramos.

examples.es: Ojalá ganaran más dinero ese año.
examples.en: I wish they would earn more money that year.
examples.note: Ganar dinero = to earn money.

contrast.es: Ojalá ganen más dinero este año.
contrast.en: I hope they earn more money this year.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Dije que cuando ganara dinero, viajaría.
examples.en: I said that when I earned money, I'd travel.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Mi padre decía que cuando te ganaras la vida, lo entenderías.
examples.en: My father used to say that when you earned your own living, you'd understand.
examples.note: Ganarse la vida = to earn a living. Always with the pronoun.

examples.es: Me aseguró que cuando se ganara tu confianza, hablaría.
examples.en: He assured me that when he had earned your trust, he'd talk.
examples.note: Ganarse la confianza = to earn someone's trust.

contrast.es: Cuando se ganó tu confianza, habló.
contrast.en: When he earned your trust, he talked.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Lo entrené para que ganara la carrera.
examples.en: I trained him so that he would win the race.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Le di una oportunidad para que se ganara el respeto.
examples.en: I gave him a chance so that he could earn respect.
examples.note: Ganarse el respeto = to earn respect.

examples.es: Le ayudé para que se ganara la vida con dignidad.
examples.en: I helped him so that he could earn a living with dignity.
examples.note: Ganarse la vida with the pronoun.

contrast.es: Le ayudé y se ganó la vida con dignidad.
contrast.en: I helped him and he earned a living with dignity.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Ganar and ganarse are both regular (ganara, ganaras, ganáramos, ganaran). Always say 'ganarse la vida' with the reflexive, never 'ganar la vida'. Ganar is the plain verb (win, earn), and ganarse is to earn something personally, such as respect, trust or a living.

title: soñar

triggers.explanation: Wishing something for someone else is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te deseaba que soñaras cosas bonitas.
examples.en: I wished that you would dream of nice things.
examples.note: The o→ue of the present is gone: soñaras, never 'sueñaras'.

examples.es: Te deseaba que soñaras con una vida mejor.
examples.en: I wished that you would dream of a better life.
examples.note: Soñar con = to dream of. It always takes con.

examples.es: Te deseaba que soñaras en grande.
examples.en: I wished that you would dream big.
examples.note: Soñar en grande = to dream big.

contrast.es: Soñabas en grande.
contrast.en: You used to dream big.
contrast.note: A plain habitual fact uses the indicative (soñabas).

triggers.explanation: Judging something as not odd is an emotional evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No era raro que soñaras con ella.
examples.en: It wasn't odd that you dreamed about her.
examples.note: Soñar con + person = to dream about someone.

examples.es: No era raro que soñaran con viajar.
examples.en: It wasn't odd that they dreamed of travelling.
examples.note: Soñar con + infinitive = to dream of doing.

examples.es: No era raro que soñara con su infancia.
examples.en: It wasn't odd that she dreamed of her childhood.
examples.note: Su infancia = her childhood.

contrast.es: Era evidente que soñaba con su infancia.
contrast.en: It was obvious that she dreamed of her childhood.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). No era raro gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A habitual or completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando soñaras con él, me lo contaras.
examples.en: I told you to tell me when you dreamed about him.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Pensábamos que cuando soñáramos juntos, todo sería posible.
examples.en: We thought that when we dreamed together, everything would be possible.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: soñáramos.

examples.es: Decía que cuando soñara con volar, se despertaría feliz.
examples.en: He used to say that when he dreamed of flying, he'd wake up happy.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

contrast.es: Cuando soñaba con volar, me despertaba feliz.
contrast.en: When I dreamed of flying, I woke up happy.
contrast.note: A habitual past event takes the indicative.

tricky: Soñar takes con for what you dream about ('que soñaras con ella'), not 'de' or 'sobre'. It loses its o→ue in the imperfect subjunctive: soñara, soñaras, soñáramos, soñaran, never 'sueñara'. The ñ stays. 'Soñar en grande' is to dream big.

title: olvidar vs olvidarse

triggers.explanation: Not wanting something to happen is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No quería que olvidaras mi cumpleaños.
examples.en: I didn't want you to forget my birthday.
examples.note: Olvidar + object = to forget something. Regular: olvidaras.

examples.es: No quería que te olvidaras de las llaves.
examples.en: I didn't want you to forget the keys.
examples.note: Olvidarse de = to forget about something.

examples.es: No quería que olvidaras las llaves en el coche.
examples.en: I didn't want you to leave the keys in the car.
examples.note: Olvidar + place = to leave something behind by mistake.

contrast.es: Olvidaste las llaves en el coche.
contrast.en: You left the keys in the car.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Saying something was likely or easy to happen is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era fácil que olvidaras el paraguas.
examples.en: You were likely to forget the umbrella.
examples.note: Era fácil que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era fácil que nos olvidáramos de todo.
examples.en: We were likely to forget everything.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: olvidáramos.

examples.es: Era fácil que se olvidara de avisarte.
examples.en: He was likely to forget to let you know.
examples.note: Olvidarse de + infinitive = to forget to do.

contrast.es: Se olvidó de avisarte.
contrast.en: He forgot to let you know.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Lo apunté antes de que se me olvidara.
examples.en: I wrote it down before I forgot it.
examples.note: Se me olvida = I forget it (the thing is the subject).

examples.es: Te lo dije antes de que me olvidara.
examples.en: I told you before I forgot.
examples.note: Me olvidara = I forgot (reflexive).

examples.es: La llamé antes de que se olvidara de nosotros.
examples.en: I called her before she forgot about us.
examples.note: Olvidarse de + person = to forget about them.

contrast.es: La llamé después de que se olvidó de nosotros.
contrast.en: I called her after she forgot about us.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Olvidar and olvidarse are both regular (olvidara, olvidaras, olvidáramos, olvidaran). Olvidar + object is the plain verb, olvidarse de is 'to forget about', and se me olvidó is the accidental 'it slipped my mind': 'antes de que se me olvidara'. Don't mix the patterns.

title: notar vs fijarse

triggers.explanation: Calling something important is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era importante que notaras la diferencia.
examples.en: It was important that you noticed the difference.
examples.note: Notar = to notice. Regular: notaras.

examples.es: Era importante que te fijaras en los detalles.
examples.en: It was important that you paid attention to the details.
examples.note: Fijarse en = to pay attention to. It needs en.

examples.es: Era importante que te fijaras bien en la señal.
examples.en: It was important that you looked carefully at the sign.
examples.note: Fijarse bien = to look carefully.

contrast.es: Te fijaste bien en la señal.
contrast.en: You looked carefully at the sign.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que notara el cambio.
examples.en: I didn't think he noticed the change.
examples.note: No creía que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que se fijara en nada.
examples.en: I didn't think he paid attention to anything.
examples.note: Fijarse en nada = to notice nothing.

examples.es: No creía que se fijara en lo que decía.
examples.en: I didn't think he paid attention to what I said.
examples.note: En lo que decía: decía is indicative because it is a fact.

contrast.es: Creía que se fijaba en lo que decía.
contrast.en: I thought he paid attention to what I said.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablé más alto para que lo notaran.
examples.en: I spoke louder so that they would notice it.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ellos).

examples.es: Puse un cartel para que se fijaran en la oferta.
examples.en: I put up a sign so that they would notice the offer.
examples.note: Fijarse en la oferta = to pay attention to the offer.

examples.es: Cambié el color para que se notara menos.
examples.en: I changed the colour so that it would show less.
examples.note: Notarse = to show, to be noticeable.

contrast.es: Cambié el color y se notó menos.
contrast.en: I changed the colour and it showed less.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Notar is regular (notara), and fijarse is regular too (me fijara, te fijaras, nos fijáramos) but always needs en: 'que te fijaras en eso'. Notar is to notice, fijarse en is to pay attention to, and notarse is for things that show: 'que no se notara'.

title: preocupar vs preocuparse

triggers.explanation: Saying something made no sense is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No tenía sentido que te preocuparas.
examples.en: There was no point in you worrying.
examples.note: Preocuparse = to worry. Regular: te preocuparas.

examples.es: No tenía sentido que me preocupara tanto.
examples.en: There was no point in my worrying so much.
examples.note: Me preocupara: yo is the subject, so the pronoun is me.

examples.es: No tenía sentido que te preocuparas por algo que ya no podías cambiar.
examples.en: There was no point in you worrying about something you could no longer change.
examples.note: Preocuparse por = to worry about. Podías stays indicative.

contrast.es: Te preocupabas por algo que no podías cambiar.
contrast.en: You were worrying about something you couldn't change.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que le preocupara.
examples.en: I didn't think it worried him.
examples.note: Preocupar works like gustar. The thing that worries is the subject.

examples.es: No creía que les preocuparan los gastos.
examples.en: I didn't think the expenses worried them.
examples.note: Los gastos is plural, so preocuparan.

examples.es: No creía que se preocupara por nada.
examples.en: I didn't think he worried about anything.
examples.note: Preocuparse por nada = to worry about nothing.

contrast.es: Creía que se preocupaba por todo.
contrast.en: I thought he worried about everything.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Mi madre llamó para que no me preocupara.
examples.en: My mother called so that I wouldn't worry.
examples.note: Different subjects (mi madre / yo). Me preocupara: yo is the one worrying.

examples.es: Te avisé para que no se preocuparan tus padres.
examples.en: I let you know so that your parents wouldn't worry.
examples.note: Tus padres is plural, so preocuparan.

examples.es: Le escribí para que no se preocupara.
examples.en: I wrote to him so that he wouldn't worry.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

contrast.es: Le escribí y no se preocupó.
contrast.en: I wrote to him and he didn't worry.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Preocupar works like gustar and agrees with the thing that worries: 'que te preocupara el dinero', 'que te preocuparan los gastos'. Preocuparse is the personal verb, and it takes por: 'que te preocuparas por eso'. Both are regular in this tense: preocupara.

title: resultar

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era probable que resultara caro.
examples.en: It was likely that it would turn out expensive.
examples.note: Resultar + adjective = to turn out to be. Regular: resultara.

examples.es: Era probable que resultaran útiles.
examples.en: It was likely that they would turn out to be useful.
examples.note: Plural subject, so resultaran.

examples.es: Era probable que resultara que tenías razón.
examples.en: It was likely that it would turn out that you were right.
examples.note: Resultar que + indicative = it turns out that. Tenías stays indicative.

contrast.es: Resultó que tenías razón.
contrast.en: It turned out that you were right.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque resultara difícil, lo haría.
examples.en: Even if it turned out to be difficult, I'd do it.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque resultara raro, lo intentaríamos.
examples.en: Even if it seemed odd, we'd try it.
examples.note: Resultar raro = to seem odd.

examples.es: Aunque me resultara difícil entenderlo, lo intentaría.
examples.en: Even if I found it hard to understand, I'd try.
examples.note: Resultarle difícil a alguien = to be hard for someone. It works like gustar.

contrast.es: Aunque me resultaba difícil entenderlo, lo intenté.
contrast.en: Although I found it hard to understand, I tried.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Dijimos que cuando resultara necesario, avisaríamos.
examples.en: We said that when it turned out to be necessary, we'd let you know.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Decidieron que cuando resultara más barato, comprarían.
examples.en: They decided that when it turned out cheaper, they'd buy.
examples.note: Resultar más barato = to turn out cheaper.

examples.es: Dijo que cuando resultara evidente, todos lo verían.
examples.en: He said that when it became obvious, everybody would see it.
examples.note: Resultar evidente = to become obvious.

contrast.es: Cuando resultó evidente, todos lo vieron.
contrast.en: When it became obvious, everybody saw it.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Resultar is regular in this tense (resultara, resultaran) but flexible: turn out to be ('que resultara útil'), gustar-style ('me resultara difícil'), and 'resultar que' + indicative ('resultó que tenías razón'). Don't use it for 'to result in': that is dar como resultado or llevar a.

title: sobrar vs bastar

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá sobrara comida.
examples.en: I wish there were food left over.
examples.note: Sobrar = to be left over. The subject is la comida.

examples.es: Ojalá nos bastaran los ahorros.
examples.en: I wish our savings were enough.
examples.note: Los ahorros is plural, so bastaran. Bastar = to be enough.

examples.es: Ojalá bastara con una llamada.
examples.en: I wish a phone call were enough.
examples.note: Bastar con = to be enough.

contrast.es: Ojalá baste con una llamada.
contrast.en: I hope a phone call is enough.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que sobrara comida.
examples.en: It was possible that there would be food left over.
examples.note: Era posible que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que nos sobraran entradas.
examples.en: It was possible that we would have spare tickets.
examples.note: Entradas is plural, so sobraran.

examples.es: Era posible que con eso bastara.
examples.en: It was possible that that would be enough.
examples.note: Bastar con eso = for that to be enough.

contrast.es: Con eso bastó.
contrast.en: That was enough.
contrast.note: A real, completed fact takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Mi madre decía que cuando sobrara tiempo, descansara.
examples.en: My mother used to say that when there was time to spare, I should rest.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported advice.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando bastara con una firma, me avisaras.
examples.en: I told you to let me know when a signature was enough.
examples.note: Bastar con una firma = for a signature to be enough.

examples.es: Me aconsejaron que cuando me sobrara dinero, ahorrara.
examples.en: They advised me to save when I had money to spare.
examples.note: Sobrarle dinero a alguien = to have money left over.

contrast.es: Cuando me sobró dinero, ahorré.
contrast.en: When I had money to spare, I saved.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Sobrar and bastar both work like gustar and agree with the thing: 'que te sobrara tiempo', 'que te sobraran euros', 'que bastara con eso'. Both are regular in this tense: sobrara, bastara. Sobrar is to be left over or too much, and bastar is to be enough.

title: costar vs valer

triggers.explanation: Doubt calls for the subjunctive, so after a past verb it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que costara tanto.
examples.en: I doubted it cost that much.
examples.note: The o→ue of the present is gone: costara, never 'cuestara'.

examples.es: Dudaba que valiera la pena.
examples.en: I doubted it was worth it.
examples.note: Valer la pena = to be worth it. Valiera, from valieron.

examples.es: Dudaba que valieran tanto esos cuadros.
examples.en: I doubted those paintings were worth that much.
examples.note: Esos cuadros is plural, so valieran.

contrast.es: Sabía que valían tanto esos cuadros.
contrast.en: I knew those paintings were worth that much.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Dudaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive means 'even if', for something hypothetical. A real fact takes the indicative.

examples.es: Aunque costara caro, lo compraría.
examples.en: Even if it cost a lot, I'd buy it.
examples.note: Hypothetical, so the subjunctive. The result is in the conditional.

examples.es: Aunque valiera poco, me gustaría.
examples.en: Even if it was worth little, I'd like it.
examples.note: Valer poco = to be worth little.

examples.es: Aunque costara más, valdría la pena.
examples.en: Even if it cost more, it would be worth it.
examples.note: Valdría is the conditional of valer. Don't confuse it with the subjunctive valiera.

contrast.es: Aunque costaba más, valía la pena.
contrast.en: Although it cost more, it was worth it.
contrast.note: Aunque + indicative = a real, known fact. Aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Dijo que cuando costara menos, lo compraríamos.
examples.en: He said that when it cost less, we'd buy it.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Pensaba que cuando valiera la pena, lo haría.
examples.en: I thought that when it was worth it, I'd do it.
examples.note: A future condition from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Me advirtieron que cuando costara más de cien euros, les pidiera permiso.
examples.en: They warned me to ask them for permission when it cost more than a hundred euros.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

contrast.es: Cuando costó más de cien euros, les pedí permiso.
contrast.en: When it cost more than a hundred euros, I asked them for permission.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Costar loses its o→ue in the imperfect subjunctive: costara, costaras, costáramos, costaran, never 'cuestara'. Valer is irregular in the present (valga), but its imperfect subjunctive comes from valieron: valiera, valieras, valiéramos, valieran, never 'valgiera'. Don't confuse valiera (subjunctive) with valdría (conditional).

title: durar vs tardar

triggers.explanation: Likelihood isn't certainty, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era probable que durara poco.
examples.en: It was likely that it would last a short time.
examples.note: Durar = to last. Regular: durara.

examples.es: Era probable que tardaras una hora.
examples.en: It was likely that you would take an hour.
examples.note: Tardar = to take (time). A person is the subject.

examples.es: Era probable que la reunión durara dos horas.
examples.en: It was likely that the meeting would last two hours.
examples.note: Durar + time = to last that long. The subject is the event.

contrast.es: Estaba seguro de que la reunión duraría dos horas.
contrast.en: I was sure the meeting would last two hours.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Likelihood uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Lo cuidé para que durara.
examples.en: I looked after it so that it would last.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / lo).

examples.es: Te llevé en coche para que no tardaras.
examples.en: I drove you so that you wouldn't take long.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Salimos pronto para que no tardáramos en llegar.
examples.en: We left early so that we wouldn't take long to arrive.
examples.note: Tardar en + infinitive = to take a long time to do. Nosotros takes an accent.

contrast.es: Salimos pronto y no tardamos en llegar.
contrast.en: We left early and we didn't take long to arrive.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando tardaras en llegar, me llamaras.
examples.en: I told you to call me when you were late arriving.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dijimos que cuando durara demasiado, nos iríamos.
examples.en: We said that when it lasted too long, we'd leave.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando tardara más de una hora, avisaría.
examples.en: I promised that when I took more than an hour, I'd let you know.
examples.note: Tardar más de = to take more than.

contrast.es: Cuando tardé más de una hora, avisé.
contrast.en: When I took more than an hour, I let you know.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Durar is how long something lasts (durara) and tardar is how long it takes (tardara). 'Que tardaras una hora' (it takes you an hour) vs 'que durara una hora' (it lasts an hour). Both are regular in this tense. Tardar en + infinitive means to take a long time to do something. Nosotros takes an accent: tardáramos.

title: pagar vs cobrar

triggers.explanation: Calling something reasonable is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era razonable que pagaras tu parte.
examples.en: It was reasonable that you paid your share.
examples.note: Pagar = to pay. The g→gu of the present (pagues) does not apply: pagaras.

examples.es: Era razonable que cobraran por el servicio.
examples.en: It was reasonable that they charged for the service.
examples.note: Cobrar = to charge or to collect payment.

examples.es: Era razonable que cobrara más por las horas extra.
examples.en: It was reasonable that he got paid more for the overtime.
examples.note: Cobrar más = to earn more.

contrast.es: Era evidente que cobraba más por las horas extra.
contrast.en: It was obvious that he got paid more for the overtime.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era razonable gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Hasta que about something not yet happened, from a past viewpoint, takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Te dije que no salieras hasta que pagaras.
examples.en: I told you not to leave until you paid.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the reported order and the time clause.

examples.es: Dije que no me iría hasta que me cobraran.
examples.en: I said I wouldn't leave until they charged me.
examples.note: Cobrar a alguien = to charge someone.

examples.es: Dije que no me iría hasta que cobrara lo que me debían.
examples.en: I said I wouldn't leave until I got paid what they owed me.
examples.note: Cobrar = to receive payment. Debían stays indicative, because it is a fact.

contrast.es: Esperé hasta que cobré lo que me debían.
contrast.en: I waited until I got paid what they owed me.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te di efectivo para que pagaras.
examples.en: I gave you cash so that you could pay.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / tú).

examples.es: Te contraté para que cobraras a final de mes.
examples.en: I hired you so that you would get paid at the end of the month.
examples.note: Cobrar a final de mes = to get paid at month end.

examples.es: Envié la factura para que nos pagaran.
examples.en: I sent the invoice so that they would pay us.
examples.note: Nos is the person receiving the payment.

contrast.es: Envié la factura y nos pagaron.
contrast.en: I sent the invoice and they paid us.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Pagar has no g→gu in the imperfect subjunctive: pagara, pagaras, pagáramos, pagaran, never 'paguara'. Cobrar is regular (cobrara). Pagar is handing money over, and cobrar is receiving it or charging for it. Don't confuse who pays and who gets paid.

title: mandar vs enviar

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que me mandaras una foto.
examples.en: I wanted you to send me a photo.
examples.note: Mandar = to send. Regular: mandaras.

examples.es: Quería que enviaras el paquete ese día.
examples.en: I wanted you to send the parcel that day.
examples.note: Enviar has no accent in this tense: enviaras, unlike the present envíes.

examples.es: Quería que mandaras a tu hermano a la tienda.
examples.en: I wanted you to send your brother to the shop.
examples.note: Mandar a + person = to send someone. Mandar can also mean to order.

contrast.es: Mandabas a tu hermano a la tienda.
contrast.en: You used to send your brother to the shop.
contrast.note: A plain habitual fact uses the indicative (mandabas).

triggers.explanation: En cuanto about an event still to come from a past viewpoint takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dije que en cuanto mandara el correo, te avisaría.
examples.en: I said that as soon as I sent the email, I'd let you know.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Dijiste que en cuanto enviaras el archivo, lo revisarías.
examples.en: You said that as soon as you sent the file, you'd check it.
examples.note: Enviar un archivo = to send a file.

examples.es: Me aseguraron que en cuanto mandaran el paquete, me llamarían.
examples.en: They assured me that as soon as they sent the parcel, they'd call me.
examples.note: Plural subject: mandaran.

contrast.es: En cuanto mandaron el paquete, me llamaron.
contrast.en: As soon as they sent the parcel, they called me.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).
