triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Le di tu dirección a la tienda para que te enviara el libro.
examples.en: I gave your address to the shop so that it would send you the book.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / la tienda).

examples.es: Le di tu número a Marta para que te mandara un mensaje.
examples.en: I gave your number to Marta so that she would send you a message.
examples.note: Mandar un mensaje = to send a message.

examples.es: Les escribí para que nos mandaran el presupuesto.
examples.en: I wrote to them so that they would send us the quote.
examples.note: Nos is the person receiving the quote.

contrast.es: Les escribí y nos mandaron el presupuesto.
contrast.en: I wrote to them and they sent us the quote.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Enviar loses its accent in the imperfect subjunctive: enviara, enviaras, enviáramos, enviaran, unlike the present envíe, envíes. Mandar is regular (mandara). Enviar is only to send, and mandar also means to order. Nosotros takes an accent: enviáramos, mandáramos.

title: casarse

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá te casaras pronto.
examples.en: I wish you would get married soon.
examples.note: Casarse = to get married. Regular: casaras.

examples.es: Ojalá se casaran en primavera.
examples.en: I wish they would get married in spring.
examples.note: Plural subject, so casaran.

examples.es: Ojalá se casara con alguien que la quisiera.
examples.en: I wish she would marry someone who loved her.
examples.note: Casarse con = to marry. Alguien que la quisiera is unidentified, so the second verb is also subjunctive.

contrast.es: Ojalá se case con alguien que la quiera.
contrast.en: I hope she marries someone who loves her.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Hablamos antes de que te casaras.
examples.en: We talked before you got married.
examples.note: The wedding hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Mis padres ahorraron antes de que se casaran.
examples.en: My parents saved before they got married.
examples.note: Plural subject: casaran.

examples.es: Hablé con ella antes de que se casara con él.
examples.en: I talked to her before she married him.
examples.note: Casarse con él = to marry him. Different subjects (yo / ella).

contrast.es: Hablé con ella después de que se casó con él.
contrast.en: I talked to her after she married him.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te pedí que cuando te casaras, me invitaras.
examples.en: I asked you to invite me when you got married.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the request.

examples.es: Dijeron que cuando se casaran, vivirían allí.
examples.en: They said that when they got married, they'd live there.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando me casara con ella, cambiaría.
examples.en: I promised that when I married her, I'd change.
examples.note: Casarse con ella.

contrast.es: Cuando me casé con ella, cambié.
contrast.en: When I married her, I changed.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Casarse is regular (me casara, te casaras, nos casáramos) but always takes con: 'que te casaras con ella', never 'casarse a ella'. Without the pronoun, casar means to marry off (a priest marries a couple). Nosotros takes an accent: casáramos.

title: despedir vs despedirse

triggers.explanation: Calling something unfair is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era injusto que te despidieran.
examples.en: It was unfair that they fired you.
examples.note: Despedir = to fire. Despidieran keeps e→i (from despidieron).

examples.es: Era injusto que despidieran a tantos trabajadores.
examples.en: It was unfair that they fired so many workers.
examples.note: Despedir a = to fire someone.

examples.es: Era injusto que lo despidieran sin avisar.
examples.en: It was unfair that they fired him without warning.
examples.note: Sin avisar is an infinitive because the subject is the same (ellos).

contrast.es: Lo despidieron sin avisar.
contrast.en: They fired him without warning.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Le avisé antes de que lo despidieran.
examples.en: I warned him before they fired him.
examples.note: The firing hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Llegué antes de que se despidiera el presidente.
examples.en: I arrived before the president said goodbye.
examples.note: Despedirse = to say goodbye.

examples.es: Hablamos antes de que me despidieran.
examples.en: We talked before they fired me.
examples.note: Different subjects (nosotros / ellos).

contrast.es: Hablamos después de que me despidieron.
contrast.en: We talked after they fired me.
contrast.note: Después de que + a completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando te despidieras, abrazaras a todos.
examples.en: I told you to hug everyone when you said goodbye.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dijeron que cuando despidieran al jefe, habría cambios.
examples.en: They said that when they fired the boss, there would be changes.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Le pedí que cuando se despidiera, no llorara.
examples.en: I asked her not to cry when she said goodbye.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives.

contrast.es: Cuando se despidió, no lloró.
contrast.en: When she said goodbye, she didn't cry.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Despedir and despedirse keep e→i in every imperfect subjunctive form: despidiera, despidieras, despidiéramos, despidieran (from despidieron), never 'despediera'. Despedir is to fire (or to see someone off), and despedirse is to say goodbye.

title: morir vs matar

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Tenía miedo de que se muriera la planta.
examples.en: I was afraid the plant would die.
examples.note: Morirse = to die (of living things). The o→u: muriera, from murieron.

examples.es: Tenía miedo de que mataran al protagonista en la serie.
examples.en: I was afraid they would kill the main character in the series.
examples.note: Matar = to kill. Regular: mataran.

examples.es: Tenía miedo de que muriera sin verme.
examples.en: I was afraid he would die without seeing me.
examples.note: Morir = to die. Sin verme is an infinitive, because the subject is the same.

contrast.es: Sabía que moriría sin verme.
contrast.en: I knew he would die without seeing me.
contrast.note: Certainty uses the conditional (a future from the past). Fear uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, because the event hadn't happened yet.

examples.es: Regué la planta antes de que se muriera.
examples.en: I watered the plant before it died.
examples.note: The plant hadn't died yet.

examples.es: Cargué el móvil antes de que se muriera la batería.
examples.en: I charged my phone before the battery died.
examples.note: Morirse is also used for batteries and phones.

examples.es: Comimos algo antes de que nos muriéramos de hambre.
examples.en: We ate something before we starved.
examples.note: Morirse de hambre = to starve. Nosotros takes an accent: muriéramos.

contrast.es: Comimos algo y no nos morimos de hambre.
contrast.en: We ate something and we didn't starve.
contrast.note: A real result takes the indicative.

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses uncertainty. In a past or hypothetical context, the imperfect subjunctive marks stronger doubt than the indicative.

examples.es: Quizás me muriera de risa si lo viera.
examples.en: Maybe I'd die laughing if I saw it.
examples.note: Morirse de risa = to die laughing. Si lo viera also takes the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Quizás matara el tiempo leyendo mientras esperaba.
examples.en: Maybe he passed the time reading while he waited.
examples.note: Matar el tiempo = to kill time.

examples.es: Quizás matara dos pájaros de un tiro con ese viaje.
examples.en: Maybe he killed two birds with one stone with that trip.
examples.note: Matar dos pájaros de un tiro = to kill two birds with one stone.

contrast.es: Quizás mató dos pájaros de un tiro con ese viaje.
contrast.en: Maybe he killed two birds with one stone with that trip.
contrast.note: Quizás + indicative is also possible and sounds more confident. The subjunctive signals more doubt.

tricky: Morir has o→u in every imperfect subjunctive form: muriera, murieras, muriéramos, murieran (from murieron), never 'moriera' or 'mueriera'. Matar is regular (matara). In everyday talk morirse is more common than morir for living things dying. Morirse de + noun is an exaggeration: morirse de risa, de hambre.

title: oler vs saber a

triggers.explanation: Calling something odd is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era raro que oliera tan bien.
examples.en: It was odd that it smelled so good.
examples.note: Oler's preterite is olieron, so oliera. No h and no o→ue: never 'huelera'.

examples.es: Era raro que supiera a fresa.
examples.en: It was odd that it tasted of strawberry.
examples.note: Saber a = to taste of. Saber's preterite is supieron, so supiera.

examples.es: Era raro que oliera a gas allí.
examples.en: It was odd that it smelled of gas there.
examples.note: Oler a = to smell of.

contrast.es: Notaba que olía a gas allí.
contrast.en: I noticed that it smelled of gas there.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Puse canela para que oliera bien.
examples.en: I put in cinnamon so that it would smell good.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / eso).

examples.es: Añadí limón para que supiera a fresco.
examples.en: I added lemon so that it would taste fresh.
examples.note: Saber a fresco = to taste fresh.

examples.es: Añadí vainilla para que supiera a postre.
examples.en: I added vanilla so that it would taste like a dessert.
examples.note: Saber a postre = to taste like a dessert.

contrast.es: Añadí vainilla y supo a postre.
contrast.en: I added vanilla and it tasted like a dessert.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Me dijo que cuando oliera a quemado, apagara el horno.
examples.en: He told me to turn off the oven when it smelled of burning.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Me explicó que cuando supiera a menta, ya estaría listo.
examples.en: He explained that when it tasted of mint, it would be ready.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Me avisaron de que cuando oliera a lluvia, cerrara las ventanas.
examples.en: They told me to close the windows when it smelled of rain.
examples.note: Oler a lluvia = to smell of rain.

contrast.es: Cuando olió a lluvia, cerré las ventanas.
contrast.en: When it smelled of rain, I closed the windows.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Oler takes neither h nor o→ue in the imperfect subjunctive: oliera, olieras, oliéramos, olieran (from olieron), never 'huelera'. Saber a uses supiera, from supieron. Oler is smell and saber a is taste: 'que oliera a mar' (smell of the sea) vs 'que supiera a mar' (taste of the sea).

title: cerrar vs apagar

triggers.explanation: Saying something was necessary is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era necesario que cerraras la puerta.
examples.en: It was necessary that you closed the door.
examples.note: Cerrar = to close. The e→ie of the present is gone: cerraras, never 'cierraras'.

examples.es: Era necesario que apagaras el móvil.
examples.en: It was necessary that you turned off your phone.
examples.note: Apagar = to turn off. The g→gu of the present (apagues) does not apply: apagaras.

examples.es: Era necesario que cerraras el gas.
examples.en: It was necessary that you turned off the gas.
examples.note: Cerrar el gas = to turn off the gas supply at the tap.

contrast.es: Cerraste el gas.
contrast.en: You turned off the gas.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando cerraras, apagaras las luces.
examples.en: I told you to turn off the lights when you closed up.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Me pidió que cuando apagara el ordenador, lo desenchufara.
examples.en: He asked me to unplug the computer when I turned it off.
examples.note: Apagar el ordenador = to shut down the computer.

examples.es: Dije que cuando cerraran la tienda, me iría.
examples.en: I said that when they closed the shop, I'd leave.
examples.note: Plural subject: cerraran.

contrast.es: Cuando cerraron la tienda, me fui.
contrast.en: When they closed the shop, I left.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Quizás expresses uncertainty. In a past context, the imperfect subjunctive marks stronger doubt than the indicative.

examples.es: Quizás cerraran temprano aquel día.
examples.en: Maybe they closed early that day.
examples.note: Quizás + imperfect subjunctive = doubt about something in the past.

examples.es: Quizás apagáramos la calefacción, no lo recuerdo.
examples.en: Maybe we turned the heating off; I don't remember.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: apagáramos.

examples.es: Quizás se apagara el wifi por la noche.
examples.en: Maybe the wifi switched off during the night.
examples.note: Apagarse = to go off by itself.

contrast.es: Quizás se apagó el wifi por la noche.
contrast.en: Maybe the wifi switched off during the night.
contrast.note: Quizás + indicative is also possible and sounds more confident. The subjunctive signals more doubt.

tricky: Cerrar loses its e→ie in the imperfect subjunctive: cerrara, cerraras, cerráramos, cerraran, never 'cierrara'. Apagar has no g→gu either: apagara, never 'apaguara'. Cerrar is to close and apagar is to switch off, although both can be used for a tap (cerrar el grifo) or a light (apagar la luz).

title: arreglar vs arreglarse

triggers.explanation: Needing someone else to act is a request, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Necesitaba que arreglaras el grifo.
examples.en: I needed you to fix the tap.
examples.note: Arreglar = to fix. Regular: arreglaras.

examples.es: Necesitaba que te arreglaras rápido.
examples.en: I needed you to get ready quickly.
examples.note: Arreglarse = to get ready (to smarten up).

examples.es: Necesitaba que me arreglaras el pelo.
examples.en: I needed you to do my hair.
examples.note: Arreglar + a part of the body = to fix or style it.

contrast.es: Me arreglaste el pelo.
contrast.en: You did my hair.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llamé al técnico para que arreglara la lavadora.
examples.en: I called the technician so that he would fix the washing machine.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / el técnico).

examples.es: Le di tiempo para que se arreglara.
examples.en: I gave him time so that he could get ready.
examples.note: Se arreglara: él is the one getting ready.

examples.es: Vine temprano para que nos arregláramos juntos.
examples.en: I came early so that we could get ready together.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: arregláramos.

contrast.es: Vine temprano y nos arreglamos juntos.
contrast.en: I came early and we got ready together.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando arreglaras el coche, me avisaras.
examples.en: I told you to let me know when you fixed the car.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dije que cuando te arreglaras, saldríamos.
examples.en: I said that when you got ready, we'd go out.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Pensaba que cuando se arreglara el problema, volveríamos.
examples.en: I thought that when the problem was sorted out, we'd go back.
examples.note: Arreglarse = to sort itself out.

contrast.es: Cuando se arregló el problema, volvimos.
contrast.en: When the problem was sorted out, we went back.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Arreglar and arreglarse are both regular (arreglara, me arreglara). The pronoun changes the meaning: 'que arreglaras el coche' (fix it) vs 'que te arreglaras' (get ready). Arreglarse also means to sort itself out, or to manage ('arreglárselas').

title: pegar

triggers.explanation: Calling something horrible is an emotional judgement, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era horrible que pegaras a tu hermano.
examples.en: It was horrible that you hit your brother.
examples.note: Pegar a = to hit someone. The g→gu of the present (pegues) does not apply: pegaras.

examples.es: Era horrible que le pegaran a un niño.
examples.en: It was horrible that they hit a child.
examples.note: Le is the person hit. The subject is an unnamed 'they'.

examples.es: Era horrible que le pegaran a un animal indefenso.
examples.en: It was horrible that they hit a defenceless animal.
examples.note: Indefenso = defenceless.

contrast.es: Vi que le pegaban a un animal indefenso.
contrast.en: I saw that they were hitting a defenceless animal.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Usé cola para que pegara bien.
examples.en: I used glue so that it would stick well.
examples.note: Pegar = to stick. The subject is the thing being stuck.

examples.es: Presioné un minuto para que se pegara.
examples.en: I pressed for a minute so that it would stick.
examples.note: Pegarse = to stick on its own.

examples.es: Elegí otro color para que pegara con la camisa.
examples.en: I chose another colour so that it would go with the shirt.
examples.note: Pegar con = to match, to go with.

contrast.es: Elegí otro color y pegó con la camisa.
contrast.en: I chose another colour and it went with the shirt.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te pedí que cuando pegaras el cartel, me avisaras.
examples.en: I asked you to let me know when you put up the poster.
examples.note: Pegar el cartel = to stick up the poster.

examples.es: Mi madre decía que cuando le pegara un grito, vendría.
examples.en: My mother used to say that when I shouted at her, she'd come.
examples.note: Pegar un grito = to shout.

examples.es: Pensaba que cuando pegara un portazo, sabría que estaba enfadado.
examples.en: I thought that when he slammed the door, I'd know he was angry.
examples.note: Pegar un portazo = to slam the door.

contrast.es: Cuando pegó un portazo, supe que estaba enfadado.
contrast.en: When he slammed the door, I knew he was angry.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Pegar has no g→gu in the imperfect subjunctive: pegara, pegaras, pegáramos, pegaran, never 'peguara'. It has three unrelated meanings (hit, stick, match), and many fixed expressions: pegar un grito, pegar un portazo, pegar con. Context decides which one you mean.

title: meter vs poner

triggers.explanation: Preferring that someone else act is a wish, so the subjunctive. After a past verb, it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Prefería que metieras la ropa en la maleta.
examples.en: I preferred that you put the clothes in the suitcase.
examples.note: Meter = to put inside. Meter takes -ier- endings (from metieron): metieras.

examples.es: Prefería que pusieras el libro en la mesa.
examples.en: I preferred that you put the book on the table.
examples.note: Poner = to put or place. The preterite is pusieron, so pusieras. The -g- of the present (pongas) is gone.

examples.es: Prefería que metieras el coche en el garaje.
examples.en: I preferred that you put the car in the garage.
examples.note: Meter en = to put into an enclosed space.

contrast.es: Metías el coche en el garaje.
contrast.en: You used to put the car in the garage.
contrast.note: A plain habitual fact uses the indicative (metías).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando metieras la llave, la giraras.
examples.en: I told you to turn the key when you put it in.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Mi abuela decía que cuando pusieras la mesa, usaras los platos buenos.
examples.en: My grandmother used to say that when you set the table, you should use the good plates.
examples.note: Poner la mesa = to set the table.

examples.es: Le pedí que cuando me metiera en la cama, apagara la luz.
examples.en: I asked him to turn off the light when I got into bed.
examples.note: Meterse en la cama = to get into bed.

contrast.es: Cuando me metí en la cama, apagó la luz.
contrast.en: When I got into bed, he turned off the light.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Abrí la maleta para que metiera la ropa.
examples.en: I opened the suitcase so that he could put his clothes in.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Me hizo sitio para que pusiera la bolsa.
examples.en: He made room for me so that I could put my bag down.
examples.note: Different subjects (él / yo). Hacer sitio = to make room.

examples.es: Hablé con él para que se metiera en el equipo.
examples.en: I talked to him so that he would join the team.
examples.note: Meterse en = to get involved in, to join.

contrast.es: Hablé con él y se metió en el equipo.
contrast.en: I talked to him and he joined the team.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Meter is regular with -ier- endings: metiera, metieras, metiéramos, metieran (from metieron). Poner's imperfect subjunctive is pusiera (from pusieron), never 'pongiera'. Check the destination: meter en is inside something, poner en is on or at a place. Nosotros takes an accent: metiéramos, pusiéramos.

title: andar vs caminar

triggers.explanation: Calling something healthy is an evaluation, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era saludable que caminaras cada día.
examples.en: It was healthy that you walked every day.
examples.note: Caminar = to walk. Regular: caminaras.

examples.es: Era saludable que anduvieras un poco después de comer.
examples.en: It was healthy that you walked a little after eating.
examples.note: Andar's preterite is anduvieron, so anduvieras. It is irregular, unlike the present andes.

examples.es: Era saludable que camináramos más rápido.
examples.en: It was healthy that we walked faster.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: camináramos.

contrast.es: Era evidente que caminábamos más rápido.
contrast.en: It was obvious that we walked faster.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era saludable gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that is unlikely or contrary to fact.

examples.es: Ojalá anduviera bien el reloj.
examples.en: I wish the watch worked properly.
examples.note: Andar bien = to work well (of a watch or machine).

examples.es: Ojalá no anduviera metido en problemas.
examples.en: I wish he weren't mixed up in trouble.
examples.note: Andar + participle = to be (in a state).

examples.es: Ojalá anduviera mejor este coche.
examples.en: I wish this car ran better.
examples.note: Andar mejor = to run better. The speaker implies it doesn't.

contrast.es: Ojalá ande mejor este coche.
contrast.en: I hope this car runs better.
contrast.note: Ojalá + present subjunctive = a real, open hope. Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive = unlikely.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Saqué al perro para que caminara un rato.
examples.en: I took the dog out so that it would walk for a while.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / el perro).

examples.es: Le di la mano para que anduviera seguro.
examples.en: I held her hand so that she would walk safely.
examples.note: Andar seguro = to walk confidently.

examples.es: Lo sujeté para que caminara sin miedo.
examples.en: I supported him so that he would walk without fear.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

contrast.es: Lo sujeté y caminó sin miedo.
contrast.en: I supported him and he walked without fear.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Andar is irregular in the imperfect subjunctive: anduviera, anduvieras, anduviéramos, anduvieran (from anduvieron), never 'andara'. Caminar is regular (caminara). In the present, both are regular, but here the irregular preterite stem carries over for andar. Andar is also used for machines and states ('anda mal').

title: comprender vs entender

triggers.explanation: Hoping for someone else's understanding is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que lo entendieras.
examples.en: I hoped you would understand it.
examples.note: The e→ie of the present is gone: entendieras, from entendieron.

examples.es: Esperaba que comprendieras mi situación.
examples.en: I hoped you would understand my situation.
examples.note: Comprender = to understand (often a person or situation).

examples.es: Esperaba que comprendieras lo que sentía.
examples.en: I hoped you would understand what I felt.
examples.note: Sentía stays indicative, because it describes a fact.

contrast.es: Sabía que comprendías lo que sentía.
contrast.en: I knew you understood what I felt.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Esperaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Judging how hard something is, is an evaluation, not a statement of fact.

examples.es: Era difícil que entendiera esto.
examples.en: It was hard for him to understand this.
examples.note: Era difícil que + imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Era difícil que entendiéramos todo.
examples.en: It was hard for us to understand everything.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: entendiéramos.

examples.es: Era difícil que entendieran sus motivos.
examples.en: It was hard for them to understand his reasons.
examples.note: Entender los motivos = to understand the reasons.

contrast.es: Era evidente que entendían sus motivos.
contrast.en: It was obvious that they understood his reasons.
contrast.note: Era evidente states a fact (indicative). Era difícil gives a judgement (subjunctive).

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Hablé despacio para que me entendiera.
examples.en: I spoke slowly so that he would understand me.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Lo expliqué con ejemplos para que lo comprendieran.
examples.en: I explained it with examples so that they would understand it.
examples.note: Plural subject: comprendieran.

examples.es: Escribí claro para que se comprendiera.
examples.en: I wrote clearly so that it would be understood.
examples.note: Se comprendiera = a reflexive passive: it would be understood.

contrast.es: Escribí claro y se comprendió.
contrast.en: I wrote clearly and it was understood.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Entender loses its e→ie in the imperfect subjunctive: entendiera, entendieras, entendiéramos, entendieran (from entendieron), never 'entiendiera'. Comprender is regular (comprendiera). They are close in meaning: entender is the everyday verb, and comprender is a little more formal or about people and situations.

title: discutir vs comentar

triggers.explanation: Disliking something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No me gustaba que discutieras con tu madre.
examples.en: I didn't like you arguing with your mother.
examples.note: Discutir = to argue. Regular: discutieras.

examples.es: No me gustaba que comentaras mi vida.
examples.en: I didn't like you commenting on my life.
examples.note: Comentar = to comment on. Regular: comentaras.

examples.es: No me gustaba que discutieran delante de los niños.
examples.en: I didn't like them arguing in front of the children.
examples.note: Delante de = in front of.

contrast.es: Veía que discutían delante de los niños.
contrast.en: I could see they argued in front of the children.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Llamé a todos para que comentaran el plan.
examples.en: I called everyone so that they would comment on the plan.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / todos).

examples.es: Me calmé para que no discutiéramos.
examples.en: I calmed down so that we wouldn't argue.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: discutiéramos.

examples.es: Te llamé para que comentáramos el contrato.
examples.en: I called you so that we could discuss the contract.
examples.note: Comentar el contrato = to talk the contract over.

contrast.es: Te llamé y comentamos el contrato.
contrast.en: I called you and we discussed the contract.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando discutieras, no gritaras.
examples.en: I told you not to shout when you argued.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dije que cuando comentara la noticia, me escucharan.
examples.en: I said that when I commented on the news, they should listen to me.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Prometimos que cuando discutiéramos, no nos iríamos.
examples.en: We promised that when we argued, we wouldn't walk out.
examples.note: Discutir here means to argue, not to discuss calmly.

contrast.es: Cuando discutimos, no te fuiste.
contrast.en: When we argued, you didn't walk out.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Discutir is mostly a false friend: it usually means to argue (discutiera), not to discuss. It can mean to debate a topic, but to talk something over calmly use comentar or hablar de. Both are regular in this tense (discutiera, comentara). Nosotros takes an accent: discutiéramos, comentáramos.

title: tratar vs tratarse

triggers.explanation: Doubt calls for the subjunctive, so after a past verb it is the imperfect subjunctive.

examples.es: Dudaba que tratara bien a sus empleados.
examples.en: I doubted he treated his employees well.
examples.note: Tratar bien a = to treat well.

examples.es: Dudaba que se tratara de algo grave.
examples.en: I doubted it was about something serious.
examples.note: Tratarse de = to be about. It is impersonal and takes de.

examples.es: Dudaba que tratara de ayudarnos.
examples.en: I doubted he was trying to help us.
examples.note: Tratar de + infinitive = to try to do.

contrast.es: Sabía que trataba de ayudarnos.
contrast.en: I knew he was trying to help us.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Dudaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive. Podía ser que is the past version of puede que.

examples.es: Podía ser que tratara de venir.
examples.en: He might be trying to come.
examples.note: Tratar de + infinitive = to try to.

examples.es: Podía ser que se tratara de un error.
examples.en: It might be a mistake.
examples.note: Tratarse de un error = to be a mistake.

examples.es: Podía ser que se tratara de ti.
examples.en: It might be about you.
examples.note: Tratarse de + person = to be about someone.

contrast.es: Se trataba de ti.
contrast.en: It was about you.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative (trataba).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando trataras con él, fueras amable.
examples.en: I told you to be kind when you dealt with him.
examples.note: Tratar con = to deal with.

examples.es: Me aconsejó que cuando se tratara de dinero, le pidiera consejo.
examples.en: He advised me to ask him for advice when it came to money.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported advice.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando se tratara de ti, sería justo.
examples.en: I promised that when it came to you, I'd be fair.
examples.note: Cuando se trate de = when it comes to.

contrast.es: Cuando se trató de ti, fui justo.
contrast.en: When it came to you, I was fair.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Tratar de + infinitive means to try, tratar a means to treat, tratar con means to deal with, and tratarse de means to be about. All are regular in this tense: tratara, trataras, tratáramos, trataran. Tratarse de is impersonal, so it stays singular: 'que se tratara de unos papeles'.

title: dedicar vs dedicarse

triggers.explanation: Wanting someone else to act is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Quería que dedicaras tiempo a tu familia.
examples.en: I wanted you to devote time to your family.
examples.note: Dedicar = to devote. The c→qu of the present (dediques) does not apply: dedicaras.

examples.es: Quería que te dedicaras a la música.
examples.en: I wanted you to dedicate yourself to music.
examples.note: Dedicarse a = to do for a living, to devote yourself to.

examples.es: Quería que dedicaras este libro a tu madre.
examples.en: I wanted you to dedicate this book to your mother.
examples.note: Dedicar algo a alguien = to dedicate something to someone.

contrast.es: Dedicaste este libro a tu madre.
contrast.en: You dedicated this book to your mother.
contrast.note: A real, completed event takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Era posible que se dedicara a la política.
examples.en: It was possible that he would go into politics.
examples.note: Dedicarse a la política = to work in politics.

examples.es: Era posible que dedicáramos el verano a viajar.
examples.en: It was possible that we would spend the summer travelling.
examples.note: Dedicar + time + a + infinitive = to spend time doing. Nosotros takes an accent.

examples.es: Era posible que se dedicara a vender coches.
examples.en: It was possible that he sold cars for a living.
examples.note: Dedicarse a + infinitive = to do something for a living.

contrast.es: Sabía que se dedicaba a vender coches.
contrast.en: I knew he sold cars for a living.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Era posible que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando dedicaras tiempo a estudiar, aprobarías.
examples.en: I told you that when you devoted time to studying, you'd pass.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Pensaba que cuando se dedicara a pintar, sería feliz.
examples.en: I thought that when he devoted himself to painting, he'd be happy.
examples.note: Dedicarse a pintar = to devote yourself to painting.

examples.es: Dije que cuando me dedicara a lo que amaba, sería feliz.
examples.en: I said that when I devoted myself to what I loved, I'd be happy.
examples.note: Lo que amaba stays indicative, because it is a fact.

contrast.es: Cuando me dediqué a lo que amaba, fui feliz.
contrast.en: When I devoted myself to what I loved, I was happy.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Dedicar has no c→qu in the imperfect subjunctive: dedicara, dedicaras, dedicáramos, dedicaran, never 'dediquara'. Dedicarse a always takes a, as in 'que te dedicaras a la música'. Dedicar needs both an object and a: dedicar tiempo a la familia.

title: hay que vs tener que

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que hubiera que pagar.
examples.en: I didn't think it was necessary to pay.
examples.note: Hay que is impersonal. In this tense, it is hubiera que, singular and with no subject.

examples.es: No creía que tuviéramos que esperar.
examples.en: I didn't think we had to wait.
examples.note: Tener que has a subject: tuviéramos. Nosotros takes an accent.

examples.es: No creía que hubiera que tener tanto cuidado.
examples.en: I didn't think it was necessary to be so careful.
examples.note: Hubiera que + infinitive = it was necessary to.

contrast.es: Creía que había que tener tanto cuidado.
contrast.en: I thought it was necessary to be so careful.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative. No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Possibility is not certainty, so the subjunctive. Podía ser que is the past version of puede que.

examples.es: Podía ser que tuviera que irme.
examples.en: I might have to leave.
examples.note: Tener's preterite is tuvieron, so tuviera.

examples.es: Podía ser que hubiera que repetirlo.
examples.en: It might be necessary to repeat it.
examples.note: Haber que = to be necessary. It is impersonal.

examples.es: Podía ser que tuvieras que pedirlo tú.
examples.en: You might have to ask for it yourself.
examples.note: Tener que + infinitive = to have to. Tú is the subject.

contrast.es: Tuviste que pedirlo tú.
contrast.en: You had to ask for it yourself.
contrast.note: A real, completed fact takes the indicative (preterite).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Te dije que cuando tuvieras que irte, me avisaras.
examples.en: I told you to let me know when you had to leave.
examples.note: Two imperfect subjunctives: the time clause and the reported request.

examples.es: Dijimos que cuando hubiera que decidir, decidiríamos.
examples.en: We said that when it was necessary to decide, we'd decide.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Prometí que cuando tuviera que votar, votaría.
examples.en: I promised that when I had to vote, I'd vote.
examples.note: Tener que votar = to have to vote.

contrast.es: Cuando tuve que votar, voté.
contrast.en: When I had to vote, I voted.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Hay que is impersonal, so its imperfect subjunctive is just hubiera que, never 'hubieran que' or 'habiera que': 'era posible que hubiera que repetirlo'. Tener que has a subject and agrees (tuviera, tuvieras, tuviéramos, tuvieran, from tuvieron). Hay que is general and tener que is personal: 'hubiera que esperar' vs 'tuviéramos que esperar'.

title: aprobar vs suspender

triggers.explanation: Hoping for something is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Esperaba que aprobaras el examen.
examples.en: I hoped you would pass the exam.
examples.note: Aprobar = to pass. The o→ue of the present is gone: aprobaras, never 'apruebaras'.

examples.es: Esperaba que no suspendiéramos otra vez.
examples.en: I hoped we wouldn't fail again.
examples.note: Suspender = to fail (Spain). Nosotros takes an accent: suspendiéramos.

examples.es: Esperaba que no suspendieran a tantos alumnos.
examples.en: I hoped they wouldn't fail so many students.
examples.note: Suspender a = to fail someone.

contrast.es: Sabía que suspendían a tantos alumnos.
contrast.en: I knew they failed so many students.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative. Esperaba que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Not believing something is a doubt, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: No creía que aprobara sin estudiar.
examples.en: I didn't think he would pass without studying.
examples.note: Sin estudiar is an infinitive because the subject is the same.

examples.es: No creía que suspendieran a nadie.
examples.en: I didn't think they would fail anyone.
examples.note: Plural subject: suspendieran.

examples.es: No creía que suspendiera el examen.
examples.en: I didn't think he would fail the exam.
examples.note: Suspender el examen = to fail the exam.

contrast.es: Creía que suspendería el examen.
contrast.en: I thought he would fail the exam.
contrast.note: Creía que takes the indicative (here a conditional). No creía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Le ayudé a estudiar para que aprobara.
examples.en: I helped him study so that he would pass.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / él).

examples.es: Repasé con ellos para que no suspendieran.
examples.en: I revised with them so that they wouldn't fail.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / ellos).

examples.es: Le di clases para que aprobara el examen.
examples.en: I gave him lessons so that he would pass the exam.
examples.note: Dar clases = to give lessons.

contrast.es: Le di clases y aprobó el examen.
contrast.en: I gave him lessons and he passed the exam.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Aprobar loses its o→ue in the imperfect subjunctive: aprobara, aprobaras, aprobáramos, aprobaran, never 'aprueba-'. Suspender is regular with -ier- endings (suspendiera, from suspendieron). In Latin America, reprobar is often used for fail, and in Spain suspender.

title: caber

triggers.explanation: Fear is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Temía que no cupiéramos todos.
examples.en: I was afraid we wouldn't all fit.
examples.note: Caber's preterite is cupieron, so cupiéramos. Nosotros takes an accent.

examples.es: Temía que no cupiera en el maletero.
examples.en: I was afraid it wouldn't fit in the boot.
examples.note: Caber en = to fit in.

examples.es: Temía que no cupieran todos los libros en la estantería.
examples.en: I was afraid all the books wouldn't fit on the shelf.
examples.note: Todos los libros is plural, so cupieran.

contrast.es: Sabía que no cabían todos los libros en la estantería.
contrast.en: I knew all the books didn't fit on the shelf.
contrast.note: Sabía que takes the indicative (cabían). Temía que takes the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Moví la mesa para que cupiera el sofá.
examples.en: I moved the table so that the sofa would fit.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / el sofá).

examples.es: Compré una caja grande para que cupieran los juguetes.
examples.en: I bought a big box so that the toys would fit.
examples.note: Los juguetes is plural, so cupieran.

examples.es: Apreté un poco para que cupiera todo.
examples.en: I squeezed a little so that everything would fit.
examples.note: Todo is the subject of cupiera.

contrast.es: Apreté un poco y cupo todo.
contrast.en: I squeezed a little and everything fitted.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite cupo).

triggers.explanation: Cuando about a future moment seen from the past takes the imperfect subjunctive. A completed past event takes the indicative.

examples.es: Mi madre decía que cuando cupieras en ese vestido, lo comprarían.
examples.en: My mother used to say that when you fitted into that dress, they'd buy it.
examples.note: Caber en = to fit into.

examples.es: Dijeron que cuando cupieran todos, saldríamos.
examples.en: They said that when everybody fitted in, we'd leave.
examples.note: A future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.es: Avisaron de que cuando no cupiera más gente, cerrarían la puerta.
examples.en: They announced that when no more people could fit, they'd close the door.
examples.note: Caber más gente = for more people to fit.

contrast.es: Cuando no cupo más gente, cerraron la puerta.
contrast.en: When no more people could fit, they closed the door.
contrast.note: A completed past event takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Caber is irregular: cupiera, cupieras, cupiéramos, cupieran (from cupieron), never 'cabiera' or 'quepiera'. The present quepa (built on quepo) does not carry over. It goes with en: caber en el maletero. Nosotros takes an accent: cupiéramos.

title: disfrutar vs gozar

triggers.explanation: Wishing something for someone else is a wish, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Te deseaba que disfrutaras mucho.
examples.en: I wished that you would enjoy yourself a lot.
examples.note: Disfrutar = to enjoy. Regular: disfrutaras.

examples.es: Te deseaba que gozaras de buena salud.
examples.en: I wished that you would enjoy good health.
examples.note: Gozar de = to enjoy (a benefit, such as health). The z→c of the present (goces) does not apply.

examples.es: Te deseaba que disfrutaras de cada momento.
examples.en: I wished that you would enjoy every moment.
examples.note: Disfrutar de + noun; the de is optional (disfrutar cada momento).

contrast.es: Disfrutabas de cada momento.
contrast.en: You enjoyed every moment.
contrast.note: A plain statement of fact uses the indicative (disfrutabas).

triggers.explanation: Pleasure at something is an emotional reaction, so the subjunctive.

examples.es: Me alegraba que disfrutaras del viaje.
examples.en: I was glad you enjoyed the trip.
examples.note: Disfrutar de + noun.

examples.es: Me alegraba que gozaran de buena salud.
examples.en: I was glad they enjoyed good health.
examples.note: Plural subject: gozaran.

examples.es: Me alegraba que disfrutaras de tu trabajo.
examples.en: I was glad you enjoyed your work.
examples.note: Disfrutar de tu trabajo = to enjoy your job.

contrast.es: Veía que disfrutabas de tu trabajo.
contrast.en: I could see you enjoyed your work.
contrast.note: Observing a fact uses the indicative. Reacting to it uses the subjunctive.

triggers.explanation: Para que expresses a purpose with a different subject, so it always takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Puse música para que disfrutaran los invitados.
examples.en: I put on music so that the guests would enjoy themselves.
examples.note: Different subjects (yo / los invitados).

examples.es: Ahorré para que mis padres gozaran de su jubilación.
examples.en: I saved so that my parents would enjoy their retirement.
examples.note: Gozar de la jubilación = to enjoy retirement.

examples.es: Organicé una fiesta para que disfrutáramos todos.
examples.en: I organised a party so that we could all enjoy ourselves.
examples.note: Nosotros takes an accent: disfrutáramos.

contrast.es: Organicé una fiesta y disfrutamos todos.
contrast.en: I organised a party and we all enjoyed ourselves.
contrast.note: A real, completed result takes the indicative (preterite).

tricky: Disfrutar is regular (disfrutara) and works with or without de ('disfrutaste la cena' or 'disfrutaste de la cena'). Gozar is regular too, with no z→c in this tense: gozara, never 'gocera', and it prefers de for a benefit: gozar de buena salud. Nosotros takes an accent: disfrutáramos, gozáramos.
